-# tellsh evaluation (v0.2)
-
-Generated by `npm run eval`, `npm run bench` and `node scripts/teacher.js` (teacher section).
-
-**Post-review update (2026-10-10).** Two code reviews of v0.2 found command-injection bugs (optional template
-segments were substituted twice; PowerShell typographic quotes were not escaped), danger-checker gaps, history
-references that could pick the wrong or a stale target, and an over-lenient eval comparison. All were fixed with
-regression tests (`test/regressions.test.js`). The model was **not** retrained; the classifier numbers are unchanged.
-What moved: composer "any answer acceptable" 33.3% → 31.4% (stricter command comparison), e2e EN given gold intent
-91.2% → 91.4%; history references stay at 97.9% with two gold commands updated for `kill_by_port -sTCP:LISTEN`.
+# tellsh evaluation (v0.4 model)
+
+Generated by `npm run eval`, `npm run bench` and `node scripts/teacher.js report` (teacher section).
+
+**v0.3 close4 (2026-10-11): four general rules for the final3 majors** (model unchanged, regression tests in
+`test/regressions28.test.js`, one per example of `review/final3-*.md`). (1) *Paths* (`src/pipeline.js` `pathTail`): an
+unquoted path or name is never cut at its first space. The words after it up to the end of its span (the end of the
+request, a connector, a modifier, a noun) are part of its name (`delete the folder ~/Old Projects` -> `rm -r ~/'Old
+Projects'`, `move /tmp/old notes to /tmp/archive` -> `mv -i '/tmp/old notes' /tmp/archive`); when the end is unclear
+(`delete file /tmp/a.txt b.txt`, name words running into request words) a changing command gets a placeholder and a
+warning. A read-only command only takes an explicit path that ends the request; the composer gets the whole name too, and
+a composed command that changes something never takes a path whose name may go on. (2) *Prompt* (`src/cli.js`
+`confirmRule`): a medium-risk command never runs on a plain Enter, it needs `y`; high and composed need `yes`; an unknown
+rating counts as high. (3) *Project code* (`src/danger.js`): pytest, make, cargo, npx, wrangler, yarn, tox, gradle, mvn,
+rake and just, npm / pnpm / bun with a subcommand, go with a subcommand other than version / help / env, and node /
+python with a script or `-m` are at least medium, also for `--help` / `--version` (`show the help for pytest` -> medium,
+not run by `--yes`). (4) *Scope options* (`src/fill.js` `scopeSlots`): `--workspace` / `-w` / "in workspace X" is kept as
+`npm … --workspace X`; "in project a/b" is a gh repository (`merge pr 42 in project acme/backend` -> `gh pr merge 42
+--repo acme/backend`); a scope the command cannot express (`npm run deploy --env prod`, `--prefix`, `--config`) is a
+`<SCOPE>` placeholder, never dropped. Found on the way: a contested `npm run` script rendered the internal marker
+(`run npm build or test` -> `npm run '?'`, now `npm run <SCRIPT>`). Measured:
+
+| measurement | before | after |
+|---|---|---|
+| public `npm run eval` sections (intent, slots, e2e relex, history, composer, OOD) | — | byte-identical |
+| 4438 distinct requests of all eval sets (bash): command changed / risk changed | — | 0 / 2 (`cargo`, `wrangler --version`: safe -> medium) |
+| dev-tools eval `data/eval_v04/devtools.jsonl`, exact command (rows with `expect_command`) | 293 / 324 | 293 / 324 |
+| gh / wrangler / npm / pip phrasings (`g08_devtools` + dev-tools eval, 2049) ending in a placeholder | 162 | 162 |
+| … whose command or risk changed | — | 14 (all `--version` / `--help` of cargo, make, yarn, wrangler: safe -> medium) |
+| `{cmd} --version` / `--help` for the 85 known tools (bash): safe / medium / high | 160 / 0 / 10 | 144 / 16 / 10 |
+| catalog renders without values, 173 intents x 6 shells: safe / medium / high | 561 / 345 / 96 | 561 / 345 / 96 |
+| final3 examples (6 paths, pytest help, npm workspace, gh project) fixed | 0 / 9 | 9 / 9 |
+| warm latency p50 (bash, composer off; same machine and session, varies run to run) | 0.431 ms | 0.445–0.468 ms |
+
+### Known limits (close4)
+
+* Path ends are read with word lists: a request word that is not on them becomes part of a name (`delete folder
+  /tmp/build output` -> `'/tmp/build output'`, most likely a name that does not exist), a noun right after a path ends it
+  (`extract a.tar.gz to /tmp/my dir` -> `-C /tmp/my`), and a name with an extension is whole (`/tmp/notes.txt` for
+  `… /tmp/notes.txt old`). Quoting the path always works.
+* Scope options are read for npm, pip, gh and wrangler only, from the listed options and "in workspace / repo / project /
+  environment / config X" phrases. A literal option the catalog command lacks is still dropped elsewhere (`chmod -R 777
+  /srv/data` -> `chmod 777 /srv/data`, as before).
+* The project-code list is a list (also `poetry` / `pipenv` / `pdm` / `hatch` / `uv` / `rye` / `bundle` with a
+  subcommand, and interpreters with a script); a tool not on it is judged by its intent's risk only.
+
+**v0.3 close3 (2026-10-11): a structural trust rule instead of more parser patches** (model unchanged, regression tests
+in `test/regressions27.test.js`, one per example of `review/final2-*.md`). (1) *Trust rule* (`src/danger.js`): a command
+is safe ONLY when it is byte-identical to tellsh's own render of a `risk=safe` catalog template with plain-literal slot
+values (no quotes, `$`, backticks, `$'…'`, `;` `|` `&` `<` `>`, control characters, find actions, leading `-`; a program
+slot is a plain program name, never `source` / `.` / `eval` / a path). Everything else — an edited command (any change),
+composer output, a history replay, any unknown program or construct (`diskutil …`, `find -exec ./evil`, `source x`,
+`sed '1e …'`) — is at least high and needs an explicit `yes`; `--yes` never runs it. The parser (deny rules, allowlist)
+only raises risk: it now reads bash `$'…'` quoting (`echo $'\''; rm -rf ~ #'` is critical, not safe) and flags sed
+scripts with `e` / `w` / `W` / `-f`. (2) *Contested selectors* (`src/fill.js`): an alternative or a negation next to a
+selector (`or`, `albo`, `lub`, `not`, `but not`, `nie`, `oprócz`, `except`, …) or two candidate values for one slot
+give a placeholder for that slot: `merge pr 4 or 44` -> `gh pr merge <PR>`, `merge pr 42 but not in repo acme/app` ->
+`gh pr merge 42 --repo <REPO>`, `deploy worker --env prod --env prodprod` -> `--env <WENV>` (the value is also no longer
+removed from the request by substring, so `prod` does not explain `prodprod`). Two fixes found on the way: `merge pr 42
+and don't delete the branch` gave `--delete-branch` (now no flag), and a withheld run number was dropped (`view run
+8080808 2` gave a bare `gh run view`, now `gh run view <NUM>`). Measured:
+
+| measurement | before | after |
+|---|---|---|
+| public `npm run eval` sections (intent, slots, e2e relex, history, composer, OOD) | — | byte-identical |
+| dev-tools eval `data/eval_v04/devtools.jsonl`, exact command (rows with `expect_command`) | 294 / 324 | 293 / 324 |
+| catalog renders without values, 173 intents x 6 shells: safe / medium / high | 561 / 345 / 96 | 561 / 345 / 96 |
+| history dev set (`data/history/eval.jsonl`, bash): safe / medium / high | 23 / 12 / 18 | 0 / 0 / 53 |
+| composer commands on `data/compose/eval.jsonl`: medium / high | 43 / 0 | 0 / 43 |
+| gh / wrangler / npm / pip phrasings (`g08_devtools` + dev-tools eval, 1507) ending in a placeholder | 15 | 15 |
+| warm latency p50 (bash, composer off) | 0.421 ms | 0.404 ms |
+
+The dev-tools loss is `open the details of the last workflow run`: the selector rule withholds "the last" run, which
+used to be dropped silently (`gh run view`, the gold) and is now `gh run view <NUM>`.
+
+### Known limits (close3)
+
+* The trust rule is blunt by design: every edit (also `ls -la` -> `ls -l`), every history replay (`same for /var`) and
+  every composed command needs `yes`; a safe request with an unusual value (a file name with `'`, `$` or `&`, a grep
+  pattern starting with `-`) is high.
+* Contested selectors are read with a word window (five words after the marker, three before an alternative, within a
+  clause): `merge pr 42 or close it` withholds the pull request; a negation far from its selector is not seen. It covers
+  the gh / wrangler selectors and the `npm install` / `pip install` package and `npm run` script only.
+
+**v0.3 close (round 24, 2026-10-11): two design rules instead of more special cases** (model unchanged, regression tests
+in `test/regressions25.test.js`, `test/allowlist.test.js`). (1) *Selector rule* for gh / wrangler: a request is read
+against a closed vocabulary; a word nothing explains withholds the selector as a placeholder (`<PR>`, `<WENV>`, `<NUM>`,
+`<ARGS>`), never a guess and never a bare command. This fixes the four round-23 majors (`deploy worker in preview2`,
+`set worker secret API_KEY --env staging`, `install the project dependencies with npm`, `create a pull request in repo
+acme/app`) and an excluded environment (`deploy worker but not to production`). (2) *Allowlist danger checker*: only
+the commands / subcommands / flags the catalog renders (all shells, generated) are trusted; a wrapper (incl. `sudo`), an
+environment assignment, an unknown program, subcommand or flag is high risk. Measured effect:
+
+| measurement | before | after |
+|---|---|---|
+| public `npm run eval` sections (intent, slots, e2e relex, history, composer, OOD) | — | byte-identical |
+| dev-tools eval `data/eval_v04/devtools.jsonl`, exact command (rows with `expect_command`) | 288 / 324 | 294 / 324 |
+| gh / wrangler phrasings (train + dev-tools eval, 1097) ending in a placeholder | 57 | 103 |
+| catalog renders, 173 intents x 6 shells: safe / medium / high | 643 / 290 / 69 | 643 / 263 / 96 |
+| composer commands on `data/compose/eval.jsonl` that are high risk | 0 / 43 | 0 / 43 |
+| warm latency p50 (bash, composer off) | 0.409 ms | 0.421 ms |
+
+The 27 renders that became high are all `sudo` templates (service start/stop/restart/enable, `apt install` / update,
+`chown`, `dmesg`, macOS `powermetrics`): `sudo` is a wrapper. The v0.4 section below (real-usage data, hybrid encoder)
+was not regenerated: it needs the private dataset and the encoder; the selector rule changes only gh / wrangler /
+`npm install` slots, which that report does not score separately.
+
+**v0.3 close, final-review majors (2026-10-11)** (model unchanged, regression tests in `test/regressions26.test.js`).
+(1) A command substitution `$(…)` / `` `…` `` anywhere outside '…' (also inside "…", e.g. `ls "$(rm -rf ~)"`, which was
+safe) and a process substitution `<(…)` / `>(…)` are high risk; `$((…))` arithmetic is not a substitution. (2) Only
+allowlisted programs are safe: the "expression fragment" exemption is gone (`7z …`, `.hidden …` were safe) and a program
+is matched as written, so a path (`./ls`, `/tmp/x/ls`, `C:\t\ls.exe`) is not the allowlisted `ls`. The pieces of the
+catalog's PowerShell expressions (`$_.Name`, `.Count`, `[math]::Round`) are recorded in the generated allowlist like
+programs; a number, an argument-list item (`'a',`) and `$env:NAME` are matched by shape. (3) An explicit wrangler `--env`
+no longer drops the other unexplained words: `deploy worker --env staging --config other.toml` is
+`npx wrangler deploy --env staging <ARGS>` (was `… --env staging`, nothing missing). (4) Competing repositories are
+withheld even beside an explicit pull request: two `--repo`, `a/b or c/d`, `a/b#42 --repo c/d`, or a pull request URL of
+another repository than `--repo` give `--repo <REPO>`. Two templates changed so the catalog stays on the allowlist:
+Linux `battery` reads `upower -i /org/freedesktop/UPower/devices/DisplayDevice` instead of `"$(upower -e | grep …)"`
+(bash and fish), and the PowerShell `journal_service` filter is `-Match ([regex]::Escape(…))` instead of
+`-Like ('*' + … + '*')` (a bare `*` in the allowlist would have trusted a glob as a program). Measured: public
+`npm run eval` sections byte-identical; dev-tools eval exact 294 / 324 before and after; of all catalog renders only
+these two templates changed (the PowerShell `journal_service` with a `<SERVICE>` placeholder went medium -> safe: the old
+`<SERVICE>` inside `( … )` was read as a redirect); `docker stop $(docker ps -q)` was already high.
+
+### Known limits
+
+* The selector vocabulary is closed and hand-written (EN/PL): harmless paraphrases with an unlisted word get a
+  placeholder (46 more of the 1097 phrasings above), and options the commands do not render (`--draft`, `--base`,
+  `--label`, `--state`, `--squash`, `--port`, `--hostname`) always become `<ARGS>`. A selector hidden in a listed word
+  is not caught (`merge the pr into main` stays `gh pr merge`).
+* The rule covers gh / wrangler (and `npm install` dependency words) only; other intents keep their per-slot parsers.
+* The allowlist knows only what the catalog renders: a safe edit with an unseen flag (`git log --stat`) is high and needs
+  `yes`. Any `$(…)`, backtick or `<(…)` is high, also a
+  harmless one typed in an edit (`echo "$(date)"`); a backtick in a PowerShell edit (its escape character) is high too.
+  Every `sudo` catalog command is high.
+* Dev-tools exact-match losses against the gold: `show live logs from the worker in production` is now
+  `npx wrangler tail --env production` (gold: no `--env`), Polish `z produkcji` / `na produkcji` give `--env <WENV>`.
+
+**v0.4 model (2026-10-10): 24 developer-tool intents + private real-usage training data.** Catalog 149 → 173
+intents (npm/pip/venv, `--version`/`--help`, line ranges, SSH port forwarding, wrangler, gh). A is retrained on the
+public data plus a capped, half-weighted train split of a private real-command dataset (held out by command group;
+see [HYBRID.md](HYBRID.md#v04-real-usage)); thresholds are calibrated on curated rows only (accept 0.34 → 0.375).
+The sections below are the regenerated public metrics. Against v0.3 on public sets the retrained A is slightly
+worse: intent top-1 on `data/eval` 95.6% → 95.4%, end-to-end relex 85.3% → 83.4%, hand-written slot cases 99 → 98/99,
+composer any-acceptable 52.9% → 49.0% (dev) and 22.4% → 17.2% (blind), OOD rejection 94.6% → 92.4%, blind OOD
+100% → 98.4%, model 2.71 → 2.95 MB. In exchange, real-usage intent accuracy goes from 31.6% to 82.0% (A) and 88.8%
+(A+B, retrained encoder of round 8, recalibrated on the leak-free A_dev of round 9), and the new intents reach 95.8% on an independently written eval set — see the v0.4 section at the end.
+Two composer fixes: no composed command for a value with a line break or for a place reference ("list files there").
+
+**v0.3.0 (2026-10-10), after three review rounds.** The model is **retrained** on the v0.3 data (31534 classifier
+rows, 34434 tagged sequences; teacher-labelled paraphrases and hard negatives; every held-out text, its near-duplicates
+up to filler words and word order, and its contrastive rewrites excluded at emission time), and
+`model/compose_explained.json` is rebuilt from the same rows. Runtime fixes from the reviews (all with regression
+tests in `test/regressions*.test.js`): refused or ambiguous history references and paths with trailing punctuation
+stay placeholders and never fall back to a catalog default (`find . … -delete`); "same for X" never replays an older
+changing command or a cut path; a searched, filtered or (for "them") listed directory is never a deletion target;
+typed references follow recency; quoted `'~/x'` from history stays literal; more danger-checker wrappers. Against the
+v0.2 numbers: end-to-end 82.8% → **85.3%**, composer "any answer acceptable" 31.4% → **52.9%**, out-of-domain
+rejection 92.4% → **94.6%**; history references unchanged at 97.9% (dev set). cmd renders 114/149 intents natively
+(117 in v0.2: a value starting with `/` is now refused where cmd.exe would read it as a switch, so the eval rows
+for `dir_size`, `chown` and `create_symlink`, which use POSIX paths like `/var/www`, report a gap).
+
+**Round 4b (stricter history rules, model unchanged).** `gen_data.js` output is byte-identical to the build the shipped
+model was trained on (31534 / 34434), so the model was not retrained; `teacher.js` (Jev) now uses the same exclusion
+index as `gen_data.js` (`exclusionIndex`: held-out texts, near-duplicates, contrastive rewrites **and** eval-only slot
+values). A changing command (rm, mv, cp source/destination, kill, chmod, git branch -d/checkout, docker exec/stop,
+service restart, …) now takes a history value only when it is unambiguous and the newest value of its type: never a
+listed or searched directory (also for "it"), never an older value, never a value a newer listing of the same type may
+have replaced, never a `cd` directory after which other commands ran. This lowers the history numbers on purpose:
+dev 97.9% → **91.7%** (3 rows expected an older branch after `git checkout main`: "delete that branch", "usuń tę gałąź",
+"switch back to that release branch"), blind 82.3% → **79.7%** (an older branch after `git checkout main`; a container
+before a newer `docker ps`); every one of these now renders a placeholder instead. The danger checker now unwraps any
+`-c`/`--command` payload, checks the command at every later word after a wrapper, and rates unreadable payloads
+(`sh -c "$X"`, `$CMD …`, `… | sh`) high. Function words never turn a path into `.` ("list files in the" → `<PATH>`).
+Benchmark re-run on a busier machine (bare `node` startup 75 → 86 ms).
+
+**Round 7 (one line of history, model unchanged).** History references now read **only the single most recent
+command** ("delete it", "same for /var", "there" never reach an older line; the running `tellsh` call that zsh/fish/
+PSReadLine write first is dropped). When that line does not name a value of the needed type, or cannot be read, the
+reference is refused and the slot stays a placeholder. Gold rows whose meaning changed: dev `["sudo systemctl stop
+nginx", "sudo nginx -t"]` + "start it again" → `sudo systemctl start <SERVICE>`; blind (rewritten for the new rule, not
+tuned on) `[… "git commit -m 'wip'"]` + "push it" → `git push` and `["git checkout hotfix/tz-offset", "git log -n 3"]`
++ "delete that branch" → `git branch -d <BRANCH>`. 5 dev rows added (a value two lines back is never used; their
+queries were already held out, so `gen_data.js` output is unchanged). Dev 91.7% (48) → **92.5%** (53); blind 79.7% →
+**82.3%** (both gained rows are rule fixes, not gold edits: "ssh to that host again" after `history | tail` and
+"wejdź do tamtego kontenera" after `docker ps -a` now give the expected placeholders; the 2 edited rows were correct
+under the old gold and are correct under the new one). Round-6 fixes:
+quoted paths with spaces keep their boundaries (CLI argv and earlier `tellsh` lines), invalid history values and refused
+references never become `.`, more place wordings ("the previous folder", "the directory I listed", "w poprzednim
+katalogu"), "its contents"/"usuń jego zawartość", `git -C`/`docker --context` before a listing, "move it there", several
+paths for one slot, `$(…)` locations, here-strings and `sh -c … _ /` in the danger checker, critical writes to system
+files, NUL bytes. Every other eval number is unchanged. Bench: the history case is 1.6 → 0.7 ms p50 (one line parsed).
+
+**Round 8 (review r7; A unchanged, B retrained).** Quoted request text passed as several arguments is no longer read as
+a path (`tellsh "delete folder" /tmp/x` → `rm -r /tmp/x`; a quoted argument that is neither a path nor the first word,
+`tellsh delete folder "my data"`, leaves a changing command's path as a placeholder). The running `tellsh` call is
+dropped from history only on an exact match. Several operands (`touch a.txt b.txt`) are never "it"/"them"; `cat a.txt;
+cd /srv` + "delete it" is refused; "move it there" is refused with a note. Deleting, editing in place or overwriting a
+system file (`rm /etc/passwd`, `sed -i d /etc/passwd`, `… | tee /etc/passwd`) is critical. The composer never fills a
+slot the catalog withheld (`` `pwd` ``, a line break). npm scoped packages (`@types/node`) are kept, an invalid package
+operand is a placeholder. `fetch_model.js` installs only the bundle's own file names. `export_data.js` now filters
+augmented rows against the held-out index (143 leaked copies): B was retrained and recalibrated (see HYBRID.md); the
+hybrid re-ranks the policy's 5 candidates whatever `--top` shows. Every eval number of A is unchanged; the v0.4 devtools
+exact command (A) is 90.7 → 91.0% (scoped packages). `ls /a /b` + "show it" now gives a placeholder (test updated).
+
+**Round 9 (review r8; A unchanged, hybrid recalibrated).** After the first argument, a quoted argument with a space is a
+value only when it starts like a path (`"/tmp/my data"`) or is a file name whose first word is not a request word and
+whose spaces all come after the last `/` (`"My Notes.txt"`, `"data/my notes.txt"`); `delete "folder /tmp/x"`,
+`delete "the file notes.txt"`, `usuń "plik raport.pdf"`, `delete "all files in /tmp/x"` and `delete "my data/a.txt"`
+are unclear (placeholder + warning), also when read back from history. History values of a command scoped elsewhere
+(`git -C /repo blame notes.txt`, `docker --context prod logs web`, `docker -H …`, `DOCKER_HOST=…`) are refused for
+"delete it" / "stop it" / "same for api". After `python3 script.py data.csv`, "delete it" is a placeholder (several
+operands). With bash history an identical last `tellsh` line is no longer dropped (bash writes it after the call).
+`dd of=`, `cp`/`install`/`mv`/`ln -f` onto, `perl -i` on and `chmod 000` of a system file are critical. An unclear
+argument also blanks name/service/container/package slots. The hybrid's A_dev now excludes the dev split from every
+training source (the 23 out-of-domain dev sentences had leaked in); A+B was recalibrated (tau 0.8 → 0.9, alpha 0.75 →
+0.5) and C-ft rescored and recalibrated (see HYBRID.md). Every eval number of A is unchanged (history dev 92.5%); A+B
+real usage 88.3 → 88.8%. Bench re-run on a busier box (bare `node` startup 83 → 112 ms; tellsh's own cold overhead
+unchanged at ~93 ms). The older tests for `docker --context prod logs web` + "stop it" (was `docker stop web`) and the
+script-operand case were updated.
+
+**Round 10 (review r9; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** `wrangler dev` runs the project's configured build command,
+so it is `medium` risk like `npm run` and never auto-run with `--yes`. Attached short-option values scope a history
+command like the separate form (`git -C/repo blame notes.txt`, `docker -Htcp://prod:2375 logs web`, `docker -cprod …`
++ "delete it" / "stop it" are refused). A wrapper that changes the working directory (`env -C /repo`, `--chdir=`,
+`sudo -D /repo`, `unshare --wd`, `systemd-run --working-directory`) makes relative history values ambiguous (absolute
+ones still resolve); one that changes the root (`chroot`, `unshare -R`, `nsenter -r`) makes every value ambiguous.
+`export_data.js` drops the 98 train rows whose text equals a dev text and writes the complete dev-text index, which
+`train_a_dev.sh` now excludes (before, only texts whose own hash was dev); A_dev was rebuilt and the hybrid recalibrated:
+A+B and A+B-safe unchanged (so every A+B number is unchanged), A+C tau 0.8 → 0.9 and A+C-safe tau 0.8 → 0.9, k 3 → 5
+(C-ft rescored on the new A_dev candidates; A+C-ft real usage 87.4 → 87.5%). B was **not** retrained on the cleaned
+export (it saw those 98 rows; it ships as a separate bundle). Every eval number of A is unchanged.
+
+**Round 11 (review r10; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** A login shell runs in the target user's home, so
+`sudo -i` / `--login` (also in a cluster: `sudo -iu bob`), `runuser -l` and `su -` make relative history values
+ambiguous like `sudo -D`; `sudo --chroot` / `-R` makes every value ambiguous like `chroot`. A `cd` / `pushd` inside a
+`( … )` subshell does not outlast it: relative values after it in the same subshell are ambiguous (`(cd /repo && cat
+notes.txt)` + "delete it" is refused; absolute paths and segments after the subshell still resolve; `{ … }` groups are
+unchanged). `npx wrangler tail` / `login` / `whoami` are `medium` risk like `wrangler dev` (npx may run a project-local
+binary), so `--yes` never runs them. Every eval number is unchanged.
+
+**Round 12 (review r11; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** `pkexec` always runs the command in the target user's
+home, and `run0 --chdir=…` / `-D` / `--user=…` / `-u` in another directory, so relative history values after them are
+ambiguous like `sudo -i` (`run0` without them, as root, keeps the directory; its value options are now unwrapped, so
+`run0 --nice=5 cat notes.txt` still resolves). A redirection inside a `( … )` subshell after a `cd` opened its file
+there: `(cd /repo && echo hi > notes.txt)` + "delete it" is refused (a redirection on the subshell itself,
+`( … ) > out.txt`, is opened by the user's shell and still resolves). An explicit encoder rejection in the hybrid
+(pNone ≥ the policy's `none`) now also sets the re-ranked top tool to `__none__`, so the low-confidence composer no
+longer answers in its place (before, `list directories recursively with sizes` with pNone 0.99 gave `ls -l -R`). The
+hybrid eval runs with the composer off, so every A and A+B number is unchanged. Bench re-run.
+
+**Round 13 (review r12; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** `gh pr view/checks/merge` take a `pr` slot (number,
+`https://github.com/…/pull/N` URL or head branch): `merge pull request feature/login` gives `gh pr merge feature/login`
+and a URL is passed as it is (before, both gave a bare `gh pr merge`, which merges the current branch's pull request);
+a selector that is none of these (`merge pull request ../x`, a GitLab URL) shows `gh pr merge <PR>`. `nsenter` and
+`unshare` make every history value ambiguous like `chroot` (the command saw another pid / network / mount namespace:
+`nsenter -t 1234 -p ps -p 42` + "kill it" is refused instead of `kill 42`). A package's version constraint is kept
+(`install requests==2.32.0 with pip`, `install django>=4,<5 with pip`, `install typescript@^5.4 with npm`; before, the
+bare name, and for the npm case `npm install npm`). `train_lm_gpu.py` trains on the last partial batch (with fewer rows
+than `--bs` it looped forever) and stops on an empty train split. Every eval number is unchanged. Bench re-run.
+
+**Round 14 (review r13; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** A quoted pull request target is kept in every shell
+(`merge pull request "feature/login"` gives `gh pr merge feature/login`; a quoted value that is not a number, URL or
+branch, `"foo bar"`, shows `gh pr merge <PR>`; before, all of these gave a bare `gh pr merge`). A describing word after
+"pr" is no longer a target (`check pr status` gives `gh pr checks`, not `gh pr checks status`; also `on github`, `by bob`,
+`quickly`, `for me`), and an unmarked bare word that may or may not be a branch (`merge pr main`) is withheld as `<PR>`;
+it is kept after "branch", "for" or "from" (`merge pull request from bob`). Wrappers that run the command on another
+machine or host (`systemd-run --machine=…`/`-M`/`--host=…`/`-H`, `run0 --machine=…`, `sudo --host=…`, `machinectl shell`)
+make every history value ambiguous like `nsenter` (`systemd-run --machine=web ps -p 42` + "kill it" no longer gives a
+local `kill 42`). pip extras without a version are accepted (`install requests[socks] with pip`; before, `<PKG>`).
+Every eval number is unchanged. Bench re-run.
+
+**Round 15 (review r14; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** A pull request selector with a marker (`/`, `-`, `_`, `.`,
+digit, `#`) is kept before the describing-word check: `merge pr feature/apply`, `merge pr hotfix/weekly`,
+`merge pull request from feature-only` and `merge pr #12-only` keep their target (round 14 dropped them for a bare
+`gh pr merge`, because of a blanket "-ly" stop rule). That rule is now a list of adverbs (`quickly`, `only`, …); another
+unmarked word (`merge pr nightly`) is withheld as `<PR>`, and so is a describing word after "branch" (`merge pull request
+for branch status`). A quoted target ends at its matching quote (`"bob's-fix"` is withheld as `<PR>`, not cut to `bob`);
+`yesterday`, `review`, `fork` and similar words after "pr" are not targets. `systemd-run`/`run0` unit properties
+(`-p WorkingDirectory=…`, `-p RootDirectory=…`, `--property=…`, also `BindPaths=`, `PrivateTmp=`, `PrivatePIDs=` and
+similar) scope history values like `--working-directory` / `chroot` (`systemd-run -p RootDirectory=/srv cat /etc/x` +
+"delete it" no longer gives a host-side `rm /etc/x`). Every eval number is unchanged. Bench re-run.
+
+**Round 16 (review r15; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** A number names the pull request only right after "pr" /
+"pull request" (`pr 45`, `pr #45`, `pr number 45`) or as `#45`; any other number is no longer used
+(`merge pr with 2 approvals`, `merge my pr from 2 days ago`, `merge the 2 open prs` gave `gh pr merge 2`; now
+`gh pr merge <PR>`). A request that names a pull request the parser cannot read (`merge pr bob's`, `merge pr feature/x's`,
+`merge pr in repo v2`), an abbreviation (`e.g.`, `w/o`), a host (`on github.com`) or `issue 45` is withheld as `<PR>`, never
+a bare `gh pr merge`. History replay keeps the placeholder of an optional operand it withholds ("same but merge" after
+`tellsh merge pr nightly` is `gh pr merge <PR>`, "same for foo/bar" after `npm install lodash` is `npm install <PKG>`; both
+were bare). Clustered `systemd-run -tp WorkingDirectory=…` and `PrivateIPC=`, `PrivateDevices=`, `ProtectHome=tmpfs` scope
+history values. Every eval number is unchanged. Bench re-run.
+
+**Round 17 (review r16; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** An issue, ticket or bug number is never the pull request
+(`merge pr for issue #45`, `merge the pull request for ticket #3`), and `#45` alone counts only right after the verb
+(`merge #45`, `squash merge #45`); one in another clause (`merge the pr that closes #12`, `merge the pr, see #99`,
+`merge the pr for #12`) is withheld as `<PR>` (all gave `gh pr merge N`). "merge that pr" reads the pull request of a
+previous `gh pr view/checkout/… N|branch|url` (`gh pr merge 45`); after any other command, `gh pr view` with no or several
+operands, `--repo`, or with no history, it is `gh pr merge <PR>` (all gave a bare `gh pr merge`). The pull request is
+not a model feature, so the classifier input is unchanged. `from the branch main` / `for the branch develop` are read
+(`gh pr merge main`; were bare), an unreadable branch phrase (`from the feature branch`) is withheld. An amount after
+"pr" (`merge pr 2 days old`, `pr 3 times`), `pr 0` and `pr 007` are withheld. Every eval number is unchanged. Bench re-run.
+
+**Round 18 (review r17; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** A pull request (and a branch) read from the previous command
+is ambiguous after a trailing `cd`/`pushd`/`popd` (`gh pr view 7 && cd ../other`, `gh pr view 7; popd`: "merge that pr"
+is `gh pr merge <PR>`; was `gh pr merge 7`, a PR of another repository) and under `GH_REPO`/`GH_HOST` (prefix, `env`, or
+`export` earlier in the line). A pull request picked out among several (`merge the other pr`, `the latest pr`, `the most
+recent pr`, `my last pr`, also with history) is withheld as `<PR>` (all gave a bare `gh pr merge`). A repository the request
+names is kept: `merge pr 45 in repository other/repo` / `--repo other/repo` / `-R other/repo` give `gh pr merge 45 --repo
+other/repo` (were `gh pr merge 45`); an unreadable one (`in another repo`, `in repo v2`) shows `--repo <REPO>`, and "merge that
+pr in repo a/b" does not reuse the PR of this repository. `close that pr` / `close pr 45` are refused (gave `gh pr create
+--fill` / `gh pr view 45`). `-c`/`-a`/`-e` of `gh pr view/review/comment` are switches when reading history. Every eval
+number is unchanged. Bench re-run.
+
+**Round 19 (review r18; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** "Close" is refused for every `gh pr` intent, also when the
+classifier picks `gh_pr_merge` (`close pr 45 and delete branch`, `close pr 45 without merge`, `decline and close pr 45`
+gave `gh pr merge 45`), unless the request also asks for the merge without negating it (`merge and close pr 45`); a negated
+or undone merge (`do not merge pr 45`, `unmerge pr 45`) and `revert pr 45` / `cancel pr 45` are refused too. A repository
+written as `OWNER/REPO` after a preposition (`merge pr 7 in other/repo`, `of org/repo`, `on github.com/org/repo`) or as
+`org/repo#7` is kept as `--repo` (was a bare `gh pr merge 7`); right after "pr for/from" it is still the branch. `--repo`
+values starting with `-` are withheld. History (one line): an `export GH_REPO=…`/`GH_HOST=…` after `gh pr view 45`, or a
+later `gh pr view` / `gh pr list` / `gh pr status`, makes 45 ambiguous; a refused or guarded pull request reference keeps
+`<PR>` (`gh pr view 45; env` gave a bare `gh pr merge`). A pull request picked out by who or when (`by alice`, `from
+yesterday`, `that fixes login`, `opened last week`) is withheld as `<PR>`. Every eval number is unchanged. Bench re-run.
+
+**Round 20 (review r19; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** With history, a pull request the request names but that
+cannot be read (`merge the pr that fixes login`, `merge that pr "bob's"`, `merge that pr main`) stays `<PR>` as without
+history (after `gh pr view 45` it gave `gh pr merge 45`). History (one line): removing a repository scope after
+`gh pr view 45` (`unset GH_REPO`, `export -n GH_REPO`, `Remove-Item Env:GH_REPO`, `rm env:GH_HOST`,
+`[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("GH_REPO", $null)`) makes 45 ambiguous, like an export (it may have been a pull
+request of an inherited `GH_REPO`); a removal before `gh pr view 45` does not. Real-usage split: the command-group
+skeleton keeps some operands (`npm install express` ≠ `npm install react`); under an operand-masked structural skeleton
+552 of 2957 labelled eval rows share a group with train, and A scores 84.6% on them vs 83.5% on the rest (~0.2 pt
+inflation; [HYBRID.md](HYBRID.md#v04-real-usage)). The shipped split is unchanged; `prepare_real.js --group structural`
+is there for the next retrain. Every eval number is unchanged. Bench re-run.
+
+**Round 23 (reviews r21, r22; A unchanged, A+B policy unchanged).** wrangler deploy: after "for", a strong environment name
+is kept (`for production`, `for prod`, `for qa` -> `--env …`; fix21 dropped them to the default target) and a weak one is
+withheld (`for testing`, `for dev`, `for the qa team` -> `--env <WENV>`); a quoted name is decoded (`to "preview2"` ->
+`--env preview2`, was a bare deploy), `env=staging` is read, a marked word after a preposition without a known name in it
+(`to v2`, `to the worker-2 script`) is withheld, and a dry run asked for after a negated one is kept. gh pr: a selector
+after "pr" (`merge pr for the login fix`, `merge pr: fix login`, `merge pr with dependabot`, `merge pr of my colleague`) and
+a related pull request's URL (`merge the pr that depends on <url>`) are withheld as `<PR>`, also with history (gave a bare
+`gh pr merge` / `gh pr merge <url>`); `merge current branch pr` is the current branch's again; `approve pr` and `open pr in
+web` are refused instead of `gh pr create --fill`. Every eval number is unchanged. Bench re-run.

-alternatives), "the rendered command does what is asked" (noul), risk (choice) and up to 3 silver slot spans (noul).
-
-| check | agreement |
-|---|---|
-| intent label = teacher choice | 100.0% |
-| command judged correct (noul ≥ 0.5) | 93.3% |
-| risk level identical | 86.7% (teacher rated higher with conf ≥ 0.5: 28) |

-
-40 rows flagged → `data/teacher/review.jsonl`. After manual inspection (`data/teacher/decisions.jsonl`):

-* risk: **10 intents relabelled safe → medium** (extract_zip, extract_targz, compress_targz, compress_zip, git_stash, git_stash_pop, git_pull, git_new_branch, git_switch_branch, git_clone) — they overwrite files or change the git working tree;
-  4 kept safe where the teacher was stricter than our definition (touch_file, mkdir, git_init, git_add_all);

+## Teacher (TypeSafe Jev, build time only)
+
+All calls to `jev-latest` ($0.042/Mtok input, output free), counted by `scripts/lib/jev.js` in `data/teacher/ledger.json` (every request sent, including failed and retried ones; cache hits are free and not counted). Several rows are packed per call; every row gets its own question(s), and the intent question shows only the request and shell — never our label or a command rendered from it.
+
+| task | calls | failed | input tokens | spend |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| verify | 3292 | 0 | 3641360 | $0.1529 |
+| label | 611 | 0 | 519493 | $0.0218 |
+| mine | 279 | 0 | 259891 | $0.0109 |
+| **total** | **4182** | 0 | 4420744 | **$0.1857** |
+
+**(a) Verification of every training row** (9875 rows; 9875 answered): teacher intent = our label for **97.6%** (not an independent accuracy: the options always contain our label plus the cascade's own top guesses, so this is agreement among 4-6 plausible choices); 112 rows flagged (teacher prefers another option with confidence ≥ 0.6 and gives our label p < 0.3) → `data/teacher/review.jsonl`. This run predates the held-out filter: 715 of the rows sent were held-out texts or near-duplicates of one (none of them is in the training data of the shipped model; `teacher.js` no longer sends them). Risk (asked about the request alone): identical to the catalog risk for 94.4% of rows; 4 intents where the teacher rates most rows differently (mkdir safe→medium, touch_file safe→medium, git_add_all safe→medium, git_init safe→medium).
+
+After manual inspection (`data/teacher/decisions.jsonl`, 132 decisions): **20 rows dropped**, **2 rows relabelled**, 96 flagged rows kept (teacher wrong or request genuinely ambiguous); risk: 10 intents relabelled (extract_zip safe→medium, extract_targz safe→medium, compress_targz safe→medium, compress_zip safe→medium, git_stash safe→medium, git_stash_pop safe→medium, git_pull safe→medium, git_new_branch safe→medium, git_switch_branch safe→medium, git_clone safe→medium), 4 kept.
+
+**(b) New paraphrases**: 1995 candidates (PL+EN, bash/zsh/sh/PowerShell/fish/cmd, written for v0.3; deduplicated against training and every held-out set) labelled by the teacher; **1911 accepted** (teacher picks the proposed intent with p ≥ 0.6; EN 999, PL 912; shells bash 787, zsh 299, powershell 505, sh 114, fish 112, cmd 94), 39 rejected → `data/teacher/label_rejected.jsonl`. 74 of the accepted rows were misclassified by the v0.2 model. Out-of-domain candidates: 445, **380 kept** (teacher p(shell request) < 0.3) → `data/ood_teacher.jsonl`. 45 accepted paraphrases and 1 out-of-domain rows were later removed as near-duplicates of held-out texts.
+
+**(c) Hard negatives**: 601 contrastive rewrites of training rows across confusable intents (e.g. "symlinks" → "broken symlinks", "push" → "pull", "process" → "service"); **463 confirmed** by the teacher and added (broken_symlinks 72, find_symlinks 51, git_pull 9, git_push 10, service_status 20, find_process 18, empty_dirs 68, empty_files 51, block_devices 10, disk_free 18, last_logins 8, show_path 1, hidden_files 25, docker_ps_all 41, service_stop 29, service_restart 32); 3 low-margin training rows of confusable intents (confirmed in (a)) are given double weight. 32 confirmed rewrites and 10 boosted rows were later removed because they were held-out texts, near-duplicates of one, or one-word rewrites of one (`scripts/lib/heldout.js`).

@@ -0,0 +1,617 @@
+# tellsh hybrid: linear cascade + small neural models (v0.3 study, v0.4 real-usage update)
+
+Branch `hybrid`. Question: does a real small language model help tellsh at runtime, and which one is worth shipping?
+Everything below was measured on one shared 8-vCPU box (Xeon Sapphire Rapids, heavily loaded by other jobs during the
+work); **all latency numbers are pinned to one core (`taskset -c 0`)**.
+
+## v0.4 real usage
+
+**Question:** how do A, A+B and A+C-ft do on what people (and coding agents) actually type, and what changes when the
+models are trained on real usage? v0.3 (= master after merging `hybrid`) vs v0.4 (this update), same scripts, same
+machine, back-to-back.
+
+### TL;DR (v0.4)
+
+* **Real usage was the blind spot.** On held-out real requests (2957 EN/PL rows; command groups never seen in training),
+  v0.3 A got **31.6%** of intents right (54.5% on intents the catalog already had); A+B 38.5%. 42% of the labelled
+  real requests target things the catalog did not have (`sed -n 'N,Mp'`, `npm run`, `pip install`, `gh pr …`,
+  `wrangler …`, `--version`/`--help`).
+* **v0.4 adds 24 intents** for those (catalog 149 → 173, per-shell variants, risk, slots, tests) and trains A and B on
+  the real train split as well. Real usage: **A 82.0%, A+B 88.8%, A+C-ft 87.4%** (existing intents A 73.9%,
+  A+B 82.7%; new intents A 93.2%, A+B 97.2%). EN and PL improve alike (A+B 88.5% / 89.0%); zsh 28.1% → 90.9%,
+  bash 49.0% → 86.3%, PowerShell (n=60) 30.0% → 96.7% for A+B.
+* **The new intents work on an independent set too** (`data/eval_v04`, 424 rows written by another author from the
+  catalog only, ~37% non-bash shells): A 9.0% → **95.8%**, A+B **97.6%**, A+C-ft 98.6%; exact command 10.5% → 91.0% (A).
+* **Cost on the public sets is small but real**: A alone loses 0.5 pt on `data/eval` (94.9 → 94.4%), 1.2 pt on
+  shell-phrased requests (96.4 → 95.2%), 0.5 pt on the hybrid blind set; A+B is unchanged or better everywhere
+  (`data/eval` 96.7 → 96.7%, shell 98.8 → 98.2%, both blind sets 99.2 / 99.3%). End-to-end exact command on relexicalised
+  `data/eval`: A 84.1 → 82.2%, A+B 86.9 → 86.3%. Model 2.71 → 2.95 MB.
+* **Out-of-domain**: chit-chat rejection is ~unchanged (A 94.6 → 92.4% on `data/ood_eval`, blind OOD 100%/98.4%).
+  But real shell tasks that are *outside the catalog* are now rejected less often by A (50.8% → 29.1%): the model
+  answers more commands with the nearest catalog intent. A+B never rejected them (4.1% → 2.1%), so this is the main
+  risk of the hybrid and of v0.4: a confident-looking catalog command for a task it does not cover.
+* **B alone got much better** with real data (`data/eval` 85.9% → 90.9%; real usage 88.4%, close to A+B's
+  88.8%), but it still trails A by 3.5 pt on the curated held-out set and answers almost every out-of-catalog
+  request, so the cascade-first hybrid remains the better trade.
+* **C-ft (Qwen2.5-0.5B LoRA, not retrained for v0.4)** is again no better than B inside the hybrid on real usage
+  (87.4% vs 88.8%) and the best on the new-intent set (98.6% vs 97.6%), at ~60× B's latency and 20× its size.
+* **Ship recommendation (v0.4):** ship the retrained **A as the default** (zero dependencies; +50 pt on real usage,
+  −0.5 pt on the public held-out set) and **A+B as the opt-in `--hybrid`** (enc-v2 bundle; best on real usage,
+  no public-set regression). Keep `--yes` refusing re-ranked answers. Do not ship C. Before making `--hybrid` the
+  default, give stage 1 an explicit "shell task, but not in the catalog" signal (train on the 1476 out-of-catalog
+  real commands as a reject class or as composer triggers), because that is where both A and A+B now fail most.
+
+* **Round 8 (review r7): B retrained on leak-free data.** `export_data.js` filtered only the original rows against the
+  held-out index; 143 typo/relexicalised copies were exactly held-out texts ("kill all node processes", "koniec pliku
+  /var/log/syslog") and reached B's training data. Every emitted row is now filtered; B was retrained (same recipe, 53909
+  rows) and the A+B policies recalibrated on the dev split (A+B: tau 0.9 → 0.8, alpha 0.5 → 0.75, none 0.3 → 0.5;
+  A+B-safe: none 0.3 → 0.5). All B / A+B numbers in this section are from the retrained encoder; they move by at most
+  ~1 pt (real usage A+B 88.8 → 88.3%, blind OOD rejection 98.4 → 96.9%, relex e2e 86.8 → 85.4%). **C-ft was trained on
+  the same leaky export and was not retrained (no GPU here; C is not shipped): its numbers may be slightly optimistic.**
+  The runtime now also re-ranks the policy's k = 5 candidates whatever `--top` displays (before, `--top 3` cut it to 3).
+
+* **Round 9 (review r8): A_dev recalibrated without the out-of-domain leak.** `train_a_dev.sh` removed the dev split only
+  from the intent rows; the out-of-domain (and tldr / anaphora) loaders of `gen_data.js` bypassed it, so **all 23 OOD
+  dev sentences** were in A_dev's training data (exact feature matches) and A_dev rejected 100% of the dev OOD rows it
+  was calibrated on. The dev exclusion now goes through `leaks()`, which every training source and every emitted row
+  checks (0 of 23 left; A_dev dev OOD rejection 100% → 93.5%, accept threshold 0.41 → 0.38). Recalibrated on the
+  rebuilt A_dev: **A+B tau 0.8 → 0.9, alpha 0.75 → 0.5** (none 0.5; A+B-safe unchanged). C-ft's letter scores were
+  recomputed for the new A_dev candidates (2644 dev rows, bf16 on CPU, same LoRA; the model itself was not retrained) and
+  A+C recalibrated: tau 0.9 → 0.8 (alpha 0.75); every dev row now has a score (n 4759 → 5175). Effect (all tables
+  above are regenerated): A+B real usage 88.3 → **88.8%**, relex e2e 85.4 → 86.3%, `data/eval` 96.8 → 96.7%, shell
+  98.5 → 98.2%, hybrid blind 99.4 → 99.2%, v0.4 devtools 97.9 → 97.6%; OOD rejection unchanged. A+B defers more often
+  (`data/eval` 15.8 → 24.4%, real usage 31 → 42%), so the real-usage warm p50 goes 1.3 → 7.2 ms and cold 240 → 401 ms.
+  A+C-ft moves by ≤ 0.5 pt.
+
+* **Round 10 (review r9): complete dev-text exclusion.** Augmented train rows (typo / relexicalised copies, other
+  sources) could be byte-identical to dev texts (98 train rows, e.g. "policz pliki w /var/log"), and A_dev excluded only
+  texts whose own hash is dev, not the dev split's relexicalised copies. `export_data.js` now drops train rows equal to
+  any dev text and writes `build/hybrid/dev_texts.json`; `train_a_dev.sh` excludes that whole index (11 more base and 94
+  more derived rows dropped). A_dev rebuilt (accept threshold 0.38 → 0.40); **A+B / A+B-safe policies unchanged**, so
+  every A+B number above is unchanged. C-ft rescored from scratch on the new A_dev candidates (2681 dev rows; the
+  scorer resumes from an existing output file, so it must be deleted first); A+C tau 0.8 → 0.9, A+C-safe tau 0.8 → 0.9,
+  k 3 → 5; A+C-ft moves by ≤ 0.5 pt but defers more (real usage 31 → 42%). **B was not retrained** on the cleaned
+  export: its training data still contains those 98 rows (dev calibration of A+B may be very slightly optimistic).
+
+### Data and method (v0.4)
+
+* **Private dataset** (`/workspace/tellsh-data/dataset.jsonl`, outside git, aggregates only here): unique redacted
+  shell commands from shell histories and coding-agent sessions with 3 EN + 3 PL LLM-written requests each.
+  Only `generic` + `verified` rows are used; the dataset's `tool` field is ignored. Labels: the 24 new intents are
+  assigned by a **command pattern** checked on the command itself (`scripts/real/prepare_real.js`), other rows keep
+  the dataset's catalog intent; compound commands (`sleep 30; cp …`, `cd x && …`) are dropped; the rest is
+  "out of catalog". Redaction placeholders (`<USER>`, …) are replaced by plausible values.
+* **Split by command group**: the value-masked command skeleton (head + subcommands + sorted flags + operand count),
+  so `gh pr view 12 --repo a/b` and `gh pr view 40 --repo c/d` never straddle train and eval; whole groups go to eval per
+  label until ≥25% (never more than half of a label). Any eval text is held out from every training path through the
+  shared `exclusionIndex()` (A, B, the teacher), like the other eval sets.
+  **Caveat (review r19):** the skeleton of the shipped split (`--group v04`) keeps up to two lower-case words after the
+  head, so some operands count as subcommands (`npm install express` / `npm install react`, `cat alpha` / `cat beta` are
+  different groups). Under a structural skeleton (per-tool subcommand depth, operands masked; `--group structural`,
+  `scripts/real/group.js`) 552 of the 2957 labelled eval rows share a group with a train row. A's intent accuracy (cascade
+  top-1, `node scripts/real/group_leak.js`) is 84.6% on those rows and 83.5% on the other 2405, so the leak inflates the
+  real-usage number by ~0.2 pt. The shipped split is kept for reproducibility; the next retrain should use
+  `--group structural`.
+* **Training**: A and B use at most 120 real rows per intent and language (the line-range commands alone are ~2500
+  rows), A at half weight and without tagger rows (the regex silver spans are unreliable on these texts). A's accept
+  threshold is calibrated on curated rows only (noisy real labels pushed it from 0.34 to 0.41 and cost ~1 pt on
+  `data/eval`; now 0.375). New public data: `data/intents/g08_devtools.jsonl` (1625 rows) and the independent eval set
+  `data/eval_v04/devtools.jsonl` (424), both written without access to the private data (57 short texts such as
+  "gh pr list" occur in both and are dropped from training).
+* **Hybrid calibration**: as in v0.3 on the training dev split with a shadow A_dev. *Disclosure:* after the merge,
+  `train_a_dev.sh` silently stopped excluding the dev split (its `sed` pattern no longer matched master's
+  `gen_data.js`), so A_dev was identical to A; fixed and checked strictly before calibrating v0.4. The v0.3 rows use
+  the v0.3 policies from the hybrid branch. C-ft is the v0.3 LoRA (option descriptions now include the new intents);
+  it was scored on every row with A confidence < 0.9 plus a 10% sample.
+* **Caveats**: real-usage labels are LLM-assigned for the existing intents (not human-verified) and the requests are
+  LLM-written from commands; 1242 of the 2957 eval rows are new intents, 654 of them line ranges. "Literal" rows
+  (the request is the command itself) are 251. The relexicalised set differs by 3 rows between versions (new value
+  pools). C rows without an LM score are skipped (blind e2e n=193/194). Latency was measured on a shared, loaded box.
+

+
+## v0.3 study
+
+### TL;DR (v0.3)
+
+* **A+B is the one to ship (opt-in).** The cascade answers alone when its score is >= 0.9 (70–85% of requests, ~0.3 ms);
+  otherwise a 6-layer, PL+EN-vocabulary-pruned multilingual-e5-small (26.7 MB int8 ONNX, ~3.5 ms on one core) re-ranks
+  A's top-5. Intent accuracy on `data/eval` goes from **94.0% to 95.9%**; shell-phrased requests from 94.6% to **97.9%**; end-to-end exact command
+  on relexicalised `data/eval` from 82.8% to **87.7%**; on the noisy private real-history set from 48.5% to 67.1%. On the new blind set it stays the same (98.8% → 98.9%; A is already near the ceiling there).
+  The price: out-of-domain rejection falls from 92.4% to 85.9% (`data/ood_eval`). A "safe" mode keeps A's rejections, so OOD is unchanged, but it gains much less (94.0% → 94.4%).
+* **B alone is worse than A** (85.9% vs 94.0%): the small encoder complements the n-gram cascade but doesn't replace it.
+  Its BIO tagger is no better than A's tagger + regex (slot F1 95.2% vs 95.7%), so the hybrid keeps A's slots.
+* **C (Qwen2.5-0.5B, option-letter scoring in one forward pass)**: SmolLM2 is at chance. Qwen zero-shot picks the right option 65% of the time, 2-shot 79%.
+  A **LoRA fine-tune on CPU** (800 × 8 examples, ~55 min) makes it the most accurate re-ranker (A+C-ft **97.1%** on `data/eval`, 99.1% on blind).
+  But it costs 0.24 s warm / 1.7 s cold per deferred request on one core and 531 MB (q8_0 GGUF), needs a native llama.cpp runtime, and
+  rejects OOD worst (83.7%). Don't ship it in v0.3; use it as a teacher.
+* Latency (1 core): warm A 0.34 ms p50; warm A+B 0.38 ms p50 / 8.3 ms p95 (30% of `data/eval` deferred); cold CLI A 153 ms,
+  A+B 157 ms p50 overall and 340 ms when the encoder has to be loaded (lazy, only for deferred requests).
+
+## Systems
+
+| | what | runtime | size |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| **A** | v0.2 linear cascade (tool -> intent -> BIO tagger, hashed n-grams, int8) — unchanged | pure JS, zero deps | 2.7 MB |
+| **B** | `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small`, vocabulary pruned to PL+EN pieces (250k -> 36k), bottom 6 of 12 layers, fine-tuned as joint tool (55) + intent (149) classifier + BIO slot tagger (37 labels); int8 ONNX | `onnxruntime-node` (or `-web`), own SentencePiece-Unigram tokenizer in JS (`src/rerank/tokenizer.js`, 12 364/12 364 sequences identical to HF) | 26.7 MB (21.7 MB .tgz) |
+| **C** | System-1 decision model: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct scores A's top-k candidates in **one forward pass** (prompt lists options A..E with catalog descriptions; next-token logits of the letters). Few-shot (2 examples, no training) and **C-ft** (LoRA r=16 fine-tuned on CPU, 800 steps × 8, plain prompt) | llama.cpp GGUF q8_0 (1 thread) | 531 MB |
+| **A+B / A+C** | A answers when its cascade score >= tau; otherwise B/C re-ranks A's top-k: `alpha·log pA + (1-alpha)·log pX` | | |
+| **…-safe** | same, but re-ranking only requests A would answer anyway (A's rejections are never turned into answers) | | |
+
+SmolLM2-135M/360M-Instruct were also tried for C: chance-level (15–24%) zero-shot on the option task, Polish is
+essentially unsupported, so they were dropped. basal-1.5-mini was not used.
+
+## Method
+
+* **Same held-out sets as v0.2**: `data/eval` (2384, written independently of training), `data/shell/eval`
+  (336 shell-phrased), relexicalised `data/eval` for end-to-end exact commands (1326, held-out value pools, same seed as
+  `scripts/eval.js`), `data/slots/gold` (208), `data/history/eval` (48), `data/ood_eval` (92).
+* **New blind set** `data/hybrid/blind/` (681 rows: 331 EN, 310 PL, 40 OOD; bash/zsh/sh/PowerShell/fish/cmd with matching OS,
+  Windows paths, typos, Polish without diacritics, slang, gold slot spans). Written by a separate agent that saw only
+  the intent catalog (ids, descriptions, templates), **before any model result was looked at**; never used for training,
+  calibration or any modelling decision. 59 of its texts turned out to also occur in A's training data (short generic
+  queries such as "install htop"); B/C training drops them, and the "blind, novel texts only" rows (527) exclude every
+  blind text that occurs in any training file.
+* **Private real-history set** (`/workspace/tellsh-data`, not committed, aggregate numbers only): 6865 PL/EN paraphrases of
+  real shell-history commands whose catalog intent was assigned by an LLM pipeline (labels not human-verified; many
+  rows are short or literal command-like texts). Treat as a noisy robustness signal.
+* **Calibration on training data only.** A 10% group-wise *dev split* of the training sentences (`export_data.js`, hash of
+  the normalised text) is never used to fit B or C. Because the shipped A was trained on those sentences, a shadow
+  **A_dev** (`scripts/hybrid/train_a_dev.sh`: identical pipeline minus the dev split) provides honest cascade scores on
+  dev; tau / k / alpha / accept / none / keepNone are grid-searched there (objective: decision accuracy = correct intent,
+  or rejection for out-of-domain) and the resulting policy is applied to the shipped A.
+* *Disclosure:* the first calibration ignored OOD (only 48 of 2669 dev rows) and the first held-out run showed the
+  rerankers answering almost every OOD request (A+B 47.8%, A+C 0% rejection on `data/ood_eval`). Two OOD safeguards were
+  then added to the *procedure* (dev OOD rejection may not drop more than ~2 rows below A_dev's; option to keep A's
+  rejection when stage 1 says `__none__`), plus the "safe" variants. No other change was informed by held-out results.
+* **Rejections stay rejections.** A re-ranked rejection (B's pNone ≥ `none`, or pX below `accept`) sets the decision's
+  top tool to `__none__`, so the pipeline's low-confidence flag composer never answers in its place (the evals here run
+  with the composer off; `test/regressions13.test.js` covers the shipped path with it on).
+* **C cost control:** C was scored (Python, same prompts/weights) on every row A would defer at tau <= 0.9 plus a 10%
+  uniform sample (for "C alone"); calibration of A+C is restricted to tau <= 0.9. "C alone" rows are therefore smaller
+  samples (n shown).
+

+
+## Discussion
+
+**Where the gain comes from.** A+B rescues requests A gets wrong or rejects. Its picks come from A's own top-5, mixed
+50/50 in log space with B's distribution (alpha = 0.5). The two models make different errors: hashed character n-grams
+handle typos, inflection and rare tokens; the encoder handles paraphrase and word order. The largest gains are on
+shell-phrased requests (+3.3 pt) and on the noisy real-history paraphrases (+18.6 pt; these labels are unverified). All six shells
+improve by about 2 points on `data/eval` (95.7–96.3% vs 93.5–94.1%). EN and PL improve alike (EN 94.4 → 96.1, PL 93.6 → 95.7).
+
+**The blind set is near the ceiling for every system** (A 98.8%). The rows were written from the catalog descriptions
+and are therefore closer to the training style than `data/eval`. It still confirms there is no regression from the
+hybrid. With only ~8 wrong rows for A, differences of ±0.3 pt are noise.
+
+**OOD is the real trade-off.** Rescue means "answer when A would have rejected". The 8 extra OOD requests A+B
+accepts (6 of 92 in `data/ood_eval`, 2 of 40 blind) are keyword collisions: "how do I stop procrastinating" → kill_by_name,
+"which phone has the best camera" → which_cmd, "who founded microsoft" → users_logged_in, "kim był alan turing" → whoami,
+"dzięki, to wszystko" → git_add_all. The dev split has only 48 OOD rows, all easy, so it cannot
+calibrate this well; the constraint + `keepNone` safeguards were added after the first held-out run (see Method). Options for v0.3:
+ship `--hybrid` (rescue) as opt-in; users who prefer rejections use `TELLSH_HYBRID=safe`. `--yes` never auto-runs a
+re-ranked answer. Better OOD in B needs more `__none__` training data (only ~400 OOD training rows today).
+
+**C.** One forward pass over a ~100-token prompt is cheap for a GPU but not for one CPU core: 0.24 s with q8_0 (AMX int8
+helps a lot; Q4_K_M is 4× slower on this CPU), plus 1.4 s to load 531 MB. Zero-shot quality is too low (65%, Polish 59%).
+After LoRA fine-tuning C-ft is excellent as a chooser (C-ft alone 95.2% on the `data/eval` sample, 98.4% on blind), but
+inside the hybrid it adds only +1.2 pt over A+B on `data/eval` and nothing elsewhere, at 60–70× B's warm latency and 20× its
+size. C was scored with PyTorch bf16; the q8_0 GGUF used for latency was not re-validated for accuracy (q8_0 is usually
+lossless at this scale, but this was not measured).
+
+**Quantisation matters for B.** Standard dynamic int8 (per-tensor activations) cost 9 points of accuracy (83.7% → 74.7% on dev).
+Weight-only 8-bit `MatMulNBits` with `accuracy_level=4` (int8 compute) + int8 embeddings keeps fp32 accuracy at 26.7 MB and 4.3 ms
+(smoke test) / 3.5 ms (bench). 4-bit weights shrink it to 16 MB but lose 2 points. Pruning the vocabulary to Polish+English pieces
+(250k → 36k; segmentation identical on all corpus texts) and keeping 6 of 12 layers took the encoder from 117.6M to 25M parameters.
+
+**Runtime packaging is the main cost of B, not the model.** `onnxruntime-node` is a 113.5 MB download (all platforms in
+one tarball), and on linux-x64 its postinstall fetches another 272 MB of CUDA providers unless
+`--onnxruntime-node-install=skip` is given. `onnxruntime-web` (33 MB, WASM) also works but is ~9× slower (33 ms
+inference, 1.1 s session load), which is still acceptable for a fallback that runs on ~30% of requests.
+
+**Caveats.** The machine was shared and heavily loaded (load average 30–65 on 8 vCPUs) during all runs, so absolute
+latencies are pessimistic and p95 is noisy; relative comparisons were run back-to-back. B was trained once
+(no seed variance). The "C alone" rows are 10% uniform samples (n shown). C was not scored on the history-reference queries
+(those rows fall back to A), so the C/C-ft history column equals A's.
+
+## Recommendation for v0.3
+
+1. **Default stays A** (pure JS, zero dependencies, 2.7 MB, 0.3 ms, best OOD rejection). Nothing changes for users who don't opt in.
+2. **Ship B as an opt-in fallback**: `tellsh --hybrid` / `TELLSH_HYBRID=1` (A+B rescue, calibrated: tau 0.9, top-5,
+   alpha 0.5, keepNone, B none < 0.5) and `TELLSH_HYBRID=safe` (no rescue).
+   * Model as a separate package `tellsh-model-enc` (22 MB .tgz; skeleton in `hybrid/package/`) or a one-time download into
+     `~/.cache/tellsh/enc-v1` (`scripts/hybrid/fetch_model.js`, sha256-verified, offline afterwards).
+   * `onnxruntime-node` as an **optional peer dependency** (already set in `package.json`; not installed by default).
+     Recommend `npm i -g tellsh-model-enc onnxruntime-node --onnxruntime-node-install=skip`. `onnxruntime-web` also works.
+   * The CLI falls back to A when either is missing; re-ranked answers are never auto-run with `--yes`.
+3. **Don't ship C in v0.3.** Keep `scripts/hybrid/lm_rerank.py` / `train_lm_gpu.py`, and use C-ft as a **teacher**:
+   label real-history / unlabelled requests with A+C-ft and distil into B (and A's training data) for v0.4. That should
+   capture most of the remaining +1.2 pt at B's cost.
+4. Before promoting `--hybrid` to default: add `__none__` training data for B (OOD), verify the private real-history labels,
+   and train the encoder on a GPU (12 layers, several seeds) to check whether the 6-layer truncation leaves accuracy on the table.
+
+## Reproduce
+
+v0.4 (needs the private dataset for the real-usage parts; everything else runs on public data):
+
+```sh
+TELLSH_REAL_DATA=/path/to/dataset.jsonl node scripts/real/prepare_real.js   # -> build/real/ (gitignored)
+npm run train                                              # A (+ real train split when build/real exists)
+node scripts/hybrid/export_data.js && build/hybrid/run_enc.sh   # B (resumable), then export_encoder.py as below
+scripts/hybrid/train_a_dev.sh && node scripts/hybrid/dump_cascade.js --model=build/adev/model/model.bin --tag=adev --sets=dev
+node scripts/hybrid/eval_hybrid.js --calibrate             # A+B policy
+rm -f build/hybrid/lm_adev_qwenft.jsonl   # score resumes from an existing output: stale scores for old candidates
+python3 scripts/hybrid/lm_rerank.py score --model build/hybrid/lm-qwen05-lora/final --plain --dtype bfloat16 \
+  --cands build/hybrid/cands_adev.jsonl --sets dev --max-conf 0.9 --sample 0.1 --out build/hybrid/lm_adev_qwenft.jsonl
+node scripts/hybrid/eval_hybrid.js --calibrate --lm=adev:qwenft --tag=_ft   # A+C policy (C-ft scores for A_dev's candidates)
+node scripts/hybrid/eval_hybrid.js --lm=ship:qwenft --tag=_ft --systems=A,C,A+C,A+C-safe   # -> v04_after_ft.json
+node scripts/hybrid/eval_hybrid.js                         # -> build/hybrid/results.json (copy to hybrid/results/v04_after.json)
+BENCH_SET=real BENCH_OUT=hybrid/results/v04_bench_after_real.json taskset -c 0 node scripts/hybrid/bench_hybrid.js
+node scripts/real/report_v04.js                            # tables above + EVAL.md
+```
+The v0.3 numbers come from the same scripts run in a worktree of the merge commit (`42aee65`) with the v0.3 bundle.
+
+v0.3:
+
+```sh
+node scripts/hybrid/export_data.js                         # raw-text training data + dev split -> build/hybrid/
+python3 scripts/hybrid/prune_vocab.py                      # PL+EN vocabulary pruning of multilingual-e5-small
+python3 scripts/hybrid/train_encoder.py --layers 6 --epochs 2.5   # B (resumable; ~1.2 h on 2 busy CPU threads)
+python3 scripts/hybrid/export_encoder.py --wq 8 --gather --acc-level 4 --out hybrid/models/enc
+node scripts/hybrid/fetch_model.js --manifest hybrid/models/enc   # + `--from <dir|https-url>` installs to ~/.cache/tellsh/enc-v2
+scripts/hybrid/train_a_dev.sh                              # A_dev (cascade without the dev split) for calibration
+node scripts/hybrid/dump_cascade.js --tag=ship             # A's top-k for every set (and --model=build/adev/model/model.bin --tag=adev)
+python3 scripts/hybrid/lm_rerank.py zeroshot|train|score   # C (see build/hybrid/run_lm_*.sh); GPU: scripts/hybrid/train_lm_gpu.py
+node scripts/hybrid/eval_hybrid.js --calibrate --lm=adev:qwenfs && node scripts/hybrid/eval_hybrid.js --lm=ship:qwenfs
+node scripts/hybrid/eval_hybrid.js --calibrate --lm=adev:qwenft --tag=_ft && node scripts/hybrid/eval_hybrid.js --lm=ship:qwenft --tag=_ft --systems=A,C,A+C,A+C-safe
+taskset -c 0 node scripts/hybrid/bench_hybrid.js           # LLAMA_BIN=… LLAMA_MODELS=…gguf for C
+node scripts/hybrid/report_hybrid.js                       # tables above
+```
+Runtime: `tellsh --hybrid …` (or `TELLSH_HYBRID=1`) uses A+B with the encoder loaded lazily only when the cascade defers;
+without `onnxruntime-node` / the bundle it silently falls back to A. Re-ranked answers are never auto-run with `--yes`.

+At the prompt: **Enter** runs a safe command, **e** edits (prefilled readline), **n** aborts. A medium-risk command never
+runs on a plain Enter: it needs **y**. High-risk and composed commands need `yes`; catastrophic patterns (`rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, `Format-Volume`, …) need the whole command retyped. The command
 runs in the target shell (`$SHELL -c`, `fish -c`, `pwsh -NoProfile -Command`, `cmd /d /s /c`). Without a TTY tellsh
 only prints. Exit codes: command's own · `0` printed · `2` usage · `3` not understood · `4` `--yes` refused ·
 `5` no rendering for this shell · `130` aborted.
 
+Quoting: the whole request may be one argument (`tellsh "delete folder /tmp/x"`). Among several arguments, one with a
+space is a value when it starts like a path (`tellsh delete folder "/tmp/a b"`) or, after the first argument, looks
+like a file name (`"My Notes.txt"`, `"data/my notes.txt"`), and request text when it comes first
+(`tellsh "delete folder" /tmp/x`). Anything else is unclear: `tellsh delete folder "my data"`, and arguments that mix
+request words with a path (`delete "folder /tmp/x"`, `delete "the file notes.txt"`, `usuń "plik raport.pdf"`, a space
+before the first `/`). A changing command leaves that path (or name) as a placeholder, with a warning.
+
+Unquoted paths with spaces (v0.3 close4): a path or name is never cut at its first space. `delete the folder ~/Old
+Projects` gives `rm -r ~/'Old Projects'`: the words after a path up to the end of its span (the end of the request, a
+connector like `to` / `do`, a modifier like `recursively` / `please`, a noun like `folder` / `files`) are part of its
+name. When that end is unclear (another file name follows, `delete file /tmp/a.txt b.txt`, or name words run into other
+words of the request) a changing command shows the path as a placeholder with a warning. A read-only command takes an
+explicit path to the end of the request (`list files in ~/Old Projects`) and otherwise keeps the first reading
+(`which folder in node_modules is the largest`). Quote the path to be sure.
+

 * **Slots**: the tagger is primary; every value is validated (paths not generic nouns, ports 1–65535, branch/user
   syntax, …). If the tagger misses a slot or its value fails validation, the v0.1 regex extractor fills/wins. Values are
   normalised by the same parsers (`~/Pobrane`, "katalog domowy" → `~`, "1,5 GB" → `1536M`, "ostatnie 2 godziny" → 120 min).

+  a place reference such as "there") stays `<PATH>`; it is never silently replaced by the default `.`.
