+feature/login`, also quoted, `merge pull request "feature/login"`, never a bare `gh pr merge` for the current branch's
+pull request; a word that may not be a branch, `merge pr main`, gives `gh pr merge <PR>`, while `feature/apply` or
+`hotfix/weekly` are kept; a number counts only next to "pr" (`pr 45`, `pr #45`) or as `#45` right after the verb: `merge pr with 2 approvals`,
+`merge pr for issue #45` and `merge the pr that closes #12` give `gh pr merge <PR>`; so do a pull request picked out by
+a word before "pr" or by a label or title (`merge the dependabot pr`, `merge dependabot pr`, `merge alice's pr`, `merge said pr`,
+`merge the pr with label urgent`, `merge the pr with title "fix-login"`) or after "pr" (`merge pr for the login fix`,
+`merge pr: fix login`, `merge pr with dependabot`), and a related pull request's URL (`merge the pr that depends on
+https://github.com/o/r/pull/12`); plain `merge the pr`, `merge pr on github` stay `gh pr merge`); "merge that pr" after `gh pr view 45`
+gives `gh pr merge 45`, after any other command, a trailing `cd` or under `GH_REPO` `gh pr merge <PR>`; `merge the other pr`
+or `merge my last pr` give `gh pr merge <PR>`; a named repository is kept, `merge pr 45 in repo a/b` -> `gh pr merge 45 --repo a/b`). A package version constraint is kept
+(`install requests==2.32.0 with pip` -> `python3 -m pip install requests==2.32.0`). "Install the project dependencies"
+is `npm install` (never `npm install dependencies` / `project` / `npm`), "npm ci" / "a clean install" is `npm ci`.
+
+**Selector rule (v0.3, gh and wrangler).** A gh / wrangler request is read against a closed vocabulary: every word must
+be a command word of the tool family (`merge`, `pr`, `worker`, `deploy`, `logs`, …), a function word, a shell name, or
+part of a value that was read (pull request number / URL / branch, `--repo` repository, environment, secret name). A
+word that nothing explains — a description, a picked-out item, a quoted or uncertain name — withholds the selector
+as a placeholder you fill before running, never a guess and never a bare command: `merge the pr about auth` ->
+`gh pr merge <PR>`, `deploy worker in preview2` -> `npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>`, `create a pr into develop` /
+`list closed prs` -> `gh pr create --fill <ARGS>` / `gh pr list <ARGS>`. An explicit value stays unless another one
+competes with it (`merge pr 45 or 46` -> `<PR>`), and an environment the request excludes is never the target
+(`deploy worker but not to production` -> `--env <WENV>`).
+
+**Contested selectors (v0.3 close3).** When a request offers an alternative for a selector or negates one (`or`, `albo`,
+`lub`, `either`, `instead`, `zamiast`, `not`, `but not`, `don't`, `never`, `nie`, `oprócz`, `poza`, `except`,
+`without`, …: the selector value nearest after it within five words of the same clause, and for an alternative also
+the one nearest before it), or names two candidate values for one slot, that slot is rendered as a placeholder,
+never one of the candidates: `merge pr 4 or 44` -> `gh pr merge <PR>`, `merge pr 42 but not in repo acme/app` ->
+`gh pr merge 42 --repo <REPO>`, `deploy worker --env prod --env prodprod` / `deploy to prod, not staging` /
+`wdróż na produkcję, nie na staging` -> `--env <WENV>`, `install axios or lodash with npm` -> `npm install <PKG>`. Slots:
+pull request, run number, environment, repository and secret name (gh / wrangler), the package of `npm install` /
+`npm install -g` / `pip install` and the `npm run` script. A negation that describes a state (`co poszło nie tak`,
+`not passing`) is not one; `… and don't delete the branch` gives no `--delete-branch`. `--env` is kept for `wrangler dev/tail/secret put` too,
+`--repo` for `gh pr create/list` and `gh run list/view`, and `merge pr 45 and delete the branch` gives
+`gh pr merge 45 --delete-branch`. Installs, project scripts (also every `npx wrangler` command: `npx` prefers a project-local binary,
+and `wrangler dev` runs the project's build command), deploys, merges, secrets and tunnels are `medium` risk, so `--yes`
+never runs them.
+
+**Scope options (v0.3 close4).** A dev-tool request that says where its command acts keeps it or gets a placeholder,
+never the default scope: an npm workspace (`--workspace api`, `-w api`, `in workspace api`) is rendered as
+`--workspace api`; a repository (`--repo a/b`, `-R a/b`, `in repo a/b`, `in project a/b`) as gh `--repo` (`merge pr 42
+in project acme/backend` -> `gh pr merge 42 --repo acme/backend`, an unreadable one `--repo <REPO>`); a wrangler
+environment as `--env`. A scope the command cannot express (`npm run deploy --env prod`, `--prefix`, `--config`, `in
+project api` for npm, `--env` for gh) is a `<SCOPE>` placeholder (`<ARGS>` for wrangler), never dropped.
+
+### Optional neural fallback (`--hybrid`)
+
+`tellsh --hybrid …` (or `TELLSH_HYBRID=1`) keeps the cascade's answer when it is confident (≥ 0.9, most requests) and
+otherwise re-ranks its top-5 with a small int8 encoder (pruned multilingual-e5-small, 6 layers, 27 MB, ~4 ms on one
+core). It needs `onnxruntime-node` and the `tellsh-model-enc` 0.4 bundle (`enc-v2`, not in this repo); without them
+tellsh silently uses the cascade. `TELLSH_HYBRID=safe` never turns a rejection into an answer. Re-ranked answers are
+never auto-run with `--yes`. Details, numbers and the trade-off (fewer rejections of requests outside the catalog):
+[HYBRID.md](HYBRID.md).
+
 ### History context
 
 `--history` (or `TELLSH_HISTORY=1`) reads the **tail** (last 32 KB) of `$HISTFILE` / `~/.bash_history` /
 `~/.zsh_history` (extended format and zsh metafication handled) / fish history / PSReadLine
-`ConsoleHost_history.txt`, keeps the last 10 commands **in memory for this one request** and never prints, logs or
-stores them. Earlier `tellsh <query>` lines are re-interpreted, raw commands are parsed (template inversion + per-tool
-rules: `docker run --name`, `systemctl … X`, `kill N`, `ps -p N`, `lsof -i :P`, `git checkout`, file arguments, …).
-Lines are split with a shell-aware tokenizer (`a\ b.txt`, quoted `;`/`|`, redirections; PowerShell `''`/backtick
-escapes and native cmdlets such as `Get-Content -LiteralPath`, `Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process -Id`, `Restart-Service`).
-If the latest value of the referenced type depends on the shell state (`cat $F`, `rm *.log`), comes from a line that
-cannot be parsed, or from an unknown command naming a path, the reference is **refused** (the slot stays a
-placeholder) rather than resolved to an older value.
+`ConsoleHost_history.txt`, keeps the last 2 lines **in memory for this one request** and never prints, logs or
+stores them. **Only the single most recent command is a reference target**: "delete it", "same for /var", "there"
+always mean the previous command, never an older line (the second line is read only because zsh, fish and PSReadLine
+write the running `tellsh …` call to the file before it runs; that line is dropped when it is exactly this request,
+and never for bash, which writes it afterwards). When the previous command does
+not name a value of the needed type ("delete it" after `ls`, "logs of that container" after `git status`, "same for
+/var" after `clear`), or it cannot be read (an unparseable line, `cat $F`, `rm *.log`, an unknown command naming a
+path), the reference is **refused**: the slot stays a placeholder, never an older value or a catalog default.
+An earlier `tellsh <query>` line is re-interpreted (words keep their quoting, so `tellsh delete folder "/tmp/a b"`
+names `/tmp/a b`); a slot it left as a placeholder is not a usable value. Raw commands are parsed (template inversion +
+per-tool rules: `docker run --name`, `systemctl … X`, `kill N`, `ps -p N`, `lsof -i :P`, `git checkout`, file
+arguments, global options such as `git -C DIR`/`docker --context X`, …) with a shell-aware tokenizer (`a\ b.txt`,
+quoted `;`/`|`, redirections; PowerShell `''`/backtick escapes and native cmdlets such as `Get-Content -LiteralPath`,
+`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process -Id`, `Restart-Service`).
+
+Within that one line, later segments win (`cat old.txt; cat new.txt` → `new.txt`). A changing command (rm, mv, cp
+source or destination, kill, chmod, git branch -d/checkout/restore, docker stop/exec, service restart, …) takes the
+value only when it is unambiguous; otherwise the slot stays a placeholder:
+  * a directory that was searched, filtered or listed (`find /var/log -name '*.gz'`, `grep -rl TODO src`, `ls /tmp/build`,
+    `du -d 1 DIR`, `Get-ChildItem DIR`, `ls DIR | sort | grep pdf`, `ls -S DIR | head -1`) is never the target, for
+    "it" as well as "them": the user saw entries inside it;
+  * a later listing of the same type in the line (`cat a.txt; ls`, `pgrep foo; ps aux`, `docker logs web; docker ps`,
+    `cat a.txt; git -C /tmp status`) means "it" may be one of the listed values;
+  * the directory of a `cd` is a target only when nothing ran after the `cd` in that line (`cd DIR && make`: refused);
+  * the request names something else ("delete that backups folder" after `mkdir /srv/current`), or is about the
+    entries of the directory ("everything in it", "its contents", "what is in it", "usuń jego zawartość"); a request
+    about entries keeps its own intent (`find <PATH> … -delete`, never `rm -r .` for "delete all log files in this folder");
+  * the checked-out branch is never the one deleted;
+  * the command ran against another repository, directory or daemon (`git -C /repo blame notes.txt`, `git -C/repo …`,
+    `git --work-tree=…`, `docker --context prod logs web`, `docker -H …`/`-Htcp://…`, `DOCKER_HOST=… docker …`) or under
+    another root (`chroot /srv …`, `sudo --chroot=/srv …`, `systemd-run -p RootDirectory=/srv …`, also `BindPaths=`,
+    `PrivateTmp=` and similar unit properties) or in other namespaces (`nsenter -t 1234 -p ps -p 42`,
+    `nsenter -n lsof -i :8080`, `unshare …`) or on another machine / host (`systemd-run --machine=web …`, `systemd-run -H …`,
+    `run0 --machine=…`, `machinectl shell …`; "kill it" would hit another pid / port here): "delete it", "stop it",
+    "kill it" and "same for api" are refused, here
+    they would hit something else; after a wrapper that changes the working directory (`env -C /repo cat notes.txt`,
+    `sudo -D /repo …`, a login shell: `sudo -i …`, `sudo -iu bob …`, `runuser -l …`, `pkexec …`, `run0 --chdir=/srv …`,
+    `run0 --user=bob …`) or a `cd` inside a `( … )` subshell (`(cd /repo && cat notes.txt)`, also a redirection there:
+    `(cd /repo && echo hi > notes.txt)`; a `{ … }` group or a plain `cd` moves the user's own shell and resolves as before)
+    relative paths are refused the same way (absolute ones still resolve);
+  * the command has several operands (`touch a.txt b.txt`, `python3 script.py data.csv`): "it" may be any of them.
+Place references ("there", "over there", "in there", a final "inside", "in the same folder", "in the previous/last
+folder", "the directory I listed", "tam", "stamtąd", "w tym samym / poprzednim katalogu") are the directory of the
+previous command under the same rules, only as the place a command runs in (`find DIR … -delete`, `ls DIR`, a
+`cp`/`mv` destination), never as the object of `rm -r`/`mv`; a path named next to one ("delete notes.txt there") is
+withheld too, with or without history, and without a usable directory the place stays `<PATH>`, never `.`. ("is there
+…" / "there are …" / "still there" are not references.) "Move it there" names both ends by reference and is refused.
+Wrapped commands (`sudo -u root ls`, `env ls`, `command ls`, `nice -n 5 ps aux`) are read as the command they run.
+"Same for X" / "same but …" repeat the previous command only; they are refused when it cannot be repeated, when a
+later segment of its line ran after the repeatable command, or when X names nothing it takes. A slot of the previous
+command that depends on the shell state (`find "$DIR" …`) or fails validation (a 300-character path) stays a
+placeholder, and a slot the new request withheld (`same but … in /tmp/new!`) is never refilled. A single named path
+after "to"/"into"/"do" ("move them to /tmp/old", with or without history) is the destination and the source stays
+`<SRC>`; with a reference in destination position ("copy notes.txt to it / into that folder / do niego"), the named
+path is the source. A quoted `'~/x'` from history stays the literal directory `./~/x`.

 ## Safety model
 
+* **Trust rule (v0.3 close3).** A command is rated **safe only** when it is byte-identical to tellsh's own render of a
+  catalog template whose intent is `risk=safe`, with slot values that are plain literals: no quote characters (tellsh's
+  own single quotes are the only ones), no `$`, backticks or `$'…'`, no `;` `|` `&` `<` `>`, no control characters, no
+  find action (`-exec`, `-ok`, `-delete`, …), no leading `-` (a path is rendered `./-x`; a raw value must pass its
+  validator), and a program slot (`{cmd} --version`) is a plain program name, never a path or `source` / `.` / `eval` /
+  a shell. Everything else is **at least high** and needs an explicit `yes`; `--yes` never runs it: a command you edit
+  (any change; an unchanged one keeps its rating), a composed command, a command resolved from history (a replay), and
+  any typed text with an unknown program (`diskutil …`), construct or sed script. A catalog render of a medium / high
+  intent with plain values keeps its intent's risk; with other values it is high. The parser below (deny rules,
+  allowlist) only ever raises risk, never lowers it: it gives the reasons and decides what must be retyped
+  (critical), but finding nothing wrong does not make a command safe. It reads bash `$'…'` quoting (so
+  `echo $'\''; rm -rf ~ #'` is critical) and flags sed scripts that run a command or write a file (`e`, `w`, `W`, `-f`).
 * Every intent has a base risk: **safe** (read-only), **medium** (modifies state: archives, git checkout/pull/stash,
   chmod, mv, sudo, …), **high** (destructive: rm, kill, prune, discard). v0.2 raised 10 intents from safe to medium after
   the teacher review (see `EVAL.md`).
-* `src/danger.js` scans the **final** command — also edited ones — and can only escalate. It tokenizes each simple
-  command (quotes, `--`, long options, `sudo`/`xargs`/`env` wrappers, `bash -c '…'`/`eval`/`'…' | bash` payloads) and
+* **Project code (v0.3 close4).** A tool that loads code of the project it starts in is at least **medium**, also for
+  `--help` / `--version`: `pytest` (imports `conftest.py`), `make`, `cargo`, `npx`, `wrangler`, `yarn` (`yarnPath`),
+  `tox`, `gradle`, `mvn`, `rake`, `just`; `npm` / `pnpm` / `bun` / `poetry` / `uv` / `bundle` / … with a subcommand
+  (`npm run …`, `npm test`, `poetry run …`); `go` with
+  a subcommand other than `version` / `help` / `env`; `node` / `python` with a script or `-m`. So `show the help for
+  pytest` is `pytest --help`, medium, and `--yes` does not run it; `node --version`, `npm --help` stay safe.
+* **Allowlist (v0.3).** Only the commands, subcommands and flags tellsh itself renders are trusted
+  (`src/allowlist-data.js`, generated from every catalog template for every shell by `scripts/build_allowlist.js`; a test
+  fails when it is stale). Any **wrapper** (`sudo`, `env CMD`, `timeout`, `nohup`, `xargs`, `bash -c`, `ssh host CMD`,
+  …), an environment assignment in front of a command (`FOO=1 cmd`), an **unknown program** (`mywrap`, `cowsay`), an
+  **unknown subcommand** (`git filter-branch`, `npx cowsay`, `gh pr close`) or an **unknown flag** for a known command
+  (`gh pr merge --admin`, `git push --force-with-lease`, `rm -P`) makes the command **high** risk, with the reason, so
+  it needs an explicit `yes`. Known option clusters (`ls -la` when `-l` and `-a` are known) and attached numbers
+  (`tail -n5`) count as known. The composer's commands add the flags it validated against its tool vocabulary. Under
+  the trust rule it no longer decides whether a typed or edited command is safe (none is); it raises catalog renders
+  and adds reasons. Consequence: every catalog command that goes through `sudo` (service start/stop,
+  `apt install`, `chown`, `dmesg`, …) is high and needs `yes`.
+* `src/danger.js` also scans the **final** command — also edited ones — with deny rules, and can only escalate. It tokenizes each simple
+  command (quotes, `--`, long options) and checks every command it may run: after a wrapper (`sudo`, `doas`, `su`,
+  `runuser`, `pkexec`, `flock`, `nice`, `ionice`, `timeout`, `stdbuf`, `nohup`, `setsid`, `env`, `xargs`, `chrt`, `cgexec`,
+  `eatmydata`, `torsocks`, `catchsegv`, `parallel`, `tmux`, …) the command starting at **every** later non-option word,
+  so unknown wrapper options cannot hide it; the remote command of `ssh host …` and `docker/kubectl exec …`; and any
+  `-c`/`--command`/`--command=` string (`bash -lc '…'`, `su -c '…'`, `script -c '…'`, `find … -exec sh -c '…'`,
+  `env -S '…'`, `eval`, `cmd /c`, `pwsh -Command`). Unsure is high: a command name or a runner's command string that
+  depends on the shell state (`$CMD -rf /`, `sh -c "$X"`, `eval "$X"`), `pwsh -EncodedCommand`, and text piped into a
+  shell (`… | sh`, `… | iex`), inline interpreter code (`python3 -c`, `perl -e`, `ruby -e`, `node -e`, `php -r`, awk
+  programs calling `system()`; their string literals are checked as commands and `shutil.rmtree('/')`-style calls on
+  `/`, `~` or system directories are critical), and an unknown program followed by a destructive command
+  (`mywrap rm -rf /`). `chmod`/`chown` of `/` or a top-level system directory (even without `-R`) and `tee`/`cp` onto a
+  whole disk device (`… | sudo tee /dev/sda`) are critical, and so is deleting, overwriting or editing in place a
+  system file under `/etc`, `/boot`, `/usr`, `/bin`, `/sbin`, `/lib*` (`rm`, `unlink`, `sed -i`, `perl -i`, `tee`
+  without `-a`, `dd of=`, `cp`/`install`/`mv`/`ln -f` onto it, `chmod 000`). Switching user (`su`, `runuser`, `pkexec`) is at least medium, like `sudo` (high by the allowlist). It
   strips `git`/`docker` global options (`git -C dir -c k=v reset --hard` = `git reset --hard`). POSIX: `rm -rf` /
   `rm --recursive --force` on `/`, `~`, `~/*`, `"/"`, `/usr`, …, `mkfs`, `dd of=/dev/…`, fork bombs, `curl | sh`,
   `bash <(curl …)`, `sh -c "$(curl …)"`, force-push (incl. `+branch`), redirects into `/etc` (`>>`, `1>`, `&>`),
@@ -179,31 +350,42 @@ compression from the archive name, `bash -n` and an allowed-flag check validate
 * Raw slots (numbers, find flags) are validated before insertion; paths starting with `-` get `./`; other values
   (names, hosts, URLs, containers, …) may not start with `-`, and URLs must be `scheme://…` or `user@host:path`.
   Values taken from history pass the same validation.
-* `--yes` only runs `safe` commands that come straight from the catalog: never history-resolved, composed, incomplete
-  or medium/high-risk ones. Non-TTY use prints only.
+* `--yes` only runs `safe` commands, i.e. fresh catalog renders with plain values (the trust rule): never

 ## Data & licenses
 
+**Private real-usage data (v0.4).** The shipped weights were also trained on a private set of real shell commands
+(EN/PL requests written for each command, labels partly by command pattern, partly by an LLM pipeline; see
+[HYBRID.md](HYBRID.md#v04-real-usage)). The data and anything verbatim derived from it stay outside git: it is read
+from `$TELLSH_REAL_DATA` by `scripts/real/prepare_real.js` into `build/real/` (gitignored); only model weights and
+aggregate numbers are committed. Without the file every script trains and evaluates on public data only

-## Known gaps
-
+~60 paraphrases in `data/intents/`, ~16 eval rows written by someone else (`data/eval_v04/` for the v0.4 intents);
+retrain; `npm test && npm run eval`.
+
+## Known limits
+
+* **The selector rule trades recall for safety.** Its vocabulary is closed and hand-written (English and Polish): a
+  harmless paraphrase with a word it does not list (`deploy the api worker to cloudflare`, `run the worker on
+  localhost:8787`) gets a placeholder (`<ARGS>`, `<WENV>`) you have to fill or delete. On the 1097 gh / wrangler
+  phrasings of the training and dev-tools eval data, 103 now end in a placeholder (57 before). Options the commands do
+  not render (`--draft`, `--base`, `--label`, `--state`, `--squash`, `--port`, `--hostname`) are never added: their
+  requests get `<ARGS>`. Words the vocabulary does list are trusted, so a selector hidden in one of them (e.g.
+  "merge the pr into main" reads "main" as the merge base, not as a pull request) is not caught.
+* The selector rule covers gh and wrangler only (plus `npm install` dependency words). Other intents still read their
+  slots with the per-slot parsers: a descriptive word can still become a value there (`install the testing library`
+  -> `python3 -m pip install testing`). Read the command before running it.
+* `<ARGS>`, `<WENV>` and `<SCOPE>` are placeholders, not values: tellsh never runs an incomplete command; edit it (`e`) first.
+* **Unquoted paths with spaces are read with word lists (close4).** Request words that are not on the lists can become
+  part of a name (`delete folder /tmp/build output` -> `rm -r '/tmp/build output'`, a name that most likely does not
+  exist), and a noun right after a path ends it (`extract a.tar.gz to /tmp/my dir` -> `-C /tmp/my`). A name with an
+  extension is taken as whole (`rm /tmp/notes.txt` for `… notes.txt permanently`). Quote paths with spaces.
+* **Scope options are read for npm, pip, gh and wrangler only**, from `--workspace` / `--repo` / `--env` / `--config` /
+  `--prefix` / `--filter` / `--cwd` / `--project` (plus `-w` npm, `-R` gh, `-e` / `-c` wrangler) and "in workspace /
+  repo / project / environment / config X"; other phrasings of a scope (`for the api package`) are not seen.
+* **The trust rule is deliberately blunt.** Every edit, however harmless (`ls -la` -> `ls -l`), every history replay
+  (`same for /var`, `count lines in it`) and every composed command is high and needs `yes`; a safe request with an
+  unusual value (a file name with a quote, `$` or `&`, a grep pattern starting with `-`) is high too.
+* **The allowlist knows only what the catalog renders.** A command you type or edit with a flag tellsh never emits
+  (`ls --color=never`, `git log --stat`) gets an extra "unknown option" reason. PowerShell expressions
+  are tokenized with the same light tokenizer: parts of an expression (`$_.Length -gt 1MB`, `.Count`) are not judged
+  by the allowlist (a `$`-named program stays high by the deny rules). Payload strings of a runner (`forfiles /c "…"`,
+  `bash -c '…'`) are checked by the deny rules; the wrapper itself already makes the command high.
+* **sudo is a wrapper.** Every `sudo` catalog command (and the `bash -c` fallback for PowerShell on Linux/macOS without a
+  native variant, and `… | xargs kill`) is high risk by the allowlist; the deny rules alone would call most of them medium.
 * fish / cmd renders are not syntax-checked here (no fish/pwsh in CI); PowerShell variants are hand-written and only
   linted structurally — `pwsh` parser checks run automatically where `pwsh` is installed.
 * zsh is validated with `bash -n` (no zsh in CI); zsh-only behaviour (e.g. `NOMATCH` on unquoted globs) is avoided by quoting.
@@ -237,6 +448,12 @@ To add an intent: template in `src/catalog.js` (+ shell variants in `src/variant
 * History: bash writes history late (see above); references are resolved to the most recent matching entity, there is no
   multi-turn memory of tellsh's own suggestions beyond the history file.
 * Composer: closed vocabulary, POSIX only, no pipelines, no `--format`/`-o` style arguments; it is a safety net, not a generator.
+* Negation is only read for pull request merges (`do not merge pr 45` is refused) and wrangler environments (an excluded
+  environment is withheld, `--env <WENV>`); elsewhere it is not (`do not delete a.txt` still suggests `rm a.txt`). Always
+  read the command before running it.
+* The real-usage split's command groups keep some operands (`npm install express` ≠ `npm install react`): 552 of 2957
+  eval rows share an operand-masked skeleton with train; A scores ~1 pt higher on those, ~0.2 pt overall
+  ([HYBRID.md](HYBRID.md#v04-real-usage)).
 * Slot F1 gold set is small (208 requests); relexicalised end-to-end numbers use silver spans for unreplaced values.

@@ -1,6 +1,9 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env node
 import { main } from '../src/cli.js';
 
+// `tellsh … | head -1`: a closed pipe is not an error
+for (const s of [process.stdout, process.stderr]) s.on('error', (e) => { if (e.code === 'EPIPE') process.exit(process.exitCode ?? 0); throw e; });
+
 main().then((code) => { process.exitCode = code; }, (err) => {
   console.error(`tellsh: ${err?.stack || err}`);
   process.exitCode = 1;

+// Optional: onnxruntime is lazy-loaded (onnxruntime-node, else onnxruntime-web/WASM) and the model bundle is looked up
+// in $TELLSH_MODEL_DIR, ~/.cache/tellsh/enc-v2, the `tellsh-model-enc` package, or hybrid/models/enc (development).
+// Nothing here touches the network: the bundle has to be installed once (scripts/hybrid/fetch_model.js or npm).
+import { readFileSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+import { homedir } from 'node:os';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
+import { UnigramTokenizer } from './tokenizer.js';
+import { allowedTags } from '../tagger.js';
+
+const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
+export const BUNDLE = 'enc-v2'; // v0.4 labels (173 intents); enc-v1 was the v0.3 bundle (149)
+
+export function findModelDir(explicit) {
+  const cands = [explicit, process.env.TELLSH_MODEL_DIR, join(homedir(), '.cache', 'tellsh', BUNDLE)];
+  try { cands.push(join(require.resolve('tellsh-model-enc/package.json'), '..')); } catch { /* not installed */ }
+  cands.push(fileURLToPath(new URL('../../hybrid/models/enc', import.meta.url)));
+  return cands.find((d) => d && existsSync(join(d, 'encoder.int8.onnx')) && existsSync(join(d, 'vocab.json'))) || null;
+}
+
+async function loadOrt(prefer) {
+  const order = prefer === 'web' ? ['onnxruntime-web', 'onnxruntime-node'] : ['onnxruntime-node', 'onnxruntime-web'];
+  for (const m of order) {
+    try { const ort = await import(m); return { ort: ort.default ?? ort, name: m }; } catch { /* try next */ }
+  }
+  return null;
+}
+
+const softmax = (a) => { const m = Math.max(...a); const e = a.map((v) => Math.exp(v - m)); const s = e.reduce((x, y) => x + y, 0); return e.map((v) => v / s); };
+
+export class Encoder {
+  static async load({ dir, ort: prefer, threads = 1 } = {}) {
+    const d = findModelDir(dir);
+    if (!d) return null;
+    const rt = await loadOrt(prefer);
+    if (!rt) return null;
+    const t0 = performance.now();
+    const v = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(d, 'vocab.json'), 'utf8'));
+    const labels = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(d, 'labels.json'), 'utf8'));
+    const tok = new UnigramTokenizer({ vocab: v.pieces.map((p, i) => [p, v.scores[i]]), unkId: v.unk });
+    if (rt.name === 'onnxruntime-web' && rt.ort.env?.wasm) rt.ort.env.wasm.numThreads = threads;
+    const opts = { executionProviders: [rt.name === 'onnxruntime-web' ? 'wasm' : 'cpu'], intraOpNumThreads: threads, interOpNumThreads: 1, graphOptimizationLevel: 'all' };
+    const model = rt.name === 'onnxruntime-web' ? readFileSync(join(d, 'encoder.int8.onnx')) : join(d, 'encoder.int8.onnx');
+    const session = await rt.ort.InferenceSession.create(model, opts);
+    const e = new Encoder(rt, session, tok, labels, d);
+    e.loadMs = performance.now() - t0;
+    return e;
+  }
+
+  constructor(rt, session, tok, labels, dir) {
+    Object.assign(this, { ort: rt.ort, runtime: rt.name, session, tok, labels, dir });
+    this.T = labels.tagLabels;
+    this.cache = new Map();
+  }

+  /** -> { tools: {tool: p}, intents: {intent: p}, topIntent, topTool, pNone, tagger(text, tool) -> {spans} } */
+  async infer(text, env = {}) {
+    const key = `${env.shell}|${env.os}|${text}`;
+    if (this.cache.has(key)) return this.cache.get(key);
+    const ctx = this.labels.context.replace('{shell}', env.shell || 'bash').replace('{os}', env.os || 'linux');
+    const enc = this.tok.encodePair(text, ctx, this.labels.maxLen);
+    const n = enc.ids.length;
+    const T = this.ort.Tensor;
+    const feeds = { input_ids: new T('int64', BigInt64Array.from(enc.ids, BigInt), [1, n]), attention_mask: new T('int64', new BigInt64Array(n).fill(1n), [1, n]) };
+    const out = await this.session.run(feeds);
+    const pt = softmax(Array.from(out.tool.data));
+    const pi = softmax(Array.from(out.intent.data));
+    const tools = Object.fromEntries(this.labels.tools.map((t, i) => [t, pt[i]]));
+    const intents = Object.fromEntries(this.labels.intents.map((t, i) => [t, pi[i]]));
+    const C = this.T.length;
+    const tagLogits = [];
+    for (let j = 0; j < enc.nA; j++) tagLogits.push(Array.from(out.tags.data.subarray((j + 1) * C, (j + 2) * C)));
+    const res = {
+      tools, intents,
+      topTool: this.labels.tools[pt.indexOf(Math.max(...pt))],
+      topIntent: this.labels.intents[pi.indexOf(Math.max(...pi))],
+      pNone: tools.__none__ ?? 0,
+      tagger: (t, tool) => ({ spans: decodeSpans(t, enc.tokens, tagLogits, this.T, tool) }),
+    };
+    if (this.cache.size > 256) this.cache.clear();
+    this.cache.set(key, res);
+    return res;
+  }
+}
+
+/** Constrained Viterbi over sub-word BIO logits (tags allowed for the tool; I-X only after B-X/I-X), then spans
+ *  widened to whole words (sub-word pieces of one word belong to one span). */
+export function decodeSpans(text, toks, logits, L, tool) {
+  const n = toks.length;
+  if (!n) return [];
+  const allowed = allowedTags(tool);
+  const ok = L.map((l) => l === 'O' || allowed.has(l.slice(2)));
+  const C = L.length;
+  const sc = logits.map((z) => {
+    let m = -Infinity;
+    for (let c = 0; c < C; c++) if (ok[c] && z[c] > m) m = z[c];
+    let s = 0;
+    for (let c = 0; c < C; c++) if (ok[c]) s += Math.exp(z[c] - m);
+    const lse = m + Math.log(s);
+    return z.map((v, c) => (ok[c] ? v - lse : -Infinity));
+  });
+  const follow = (p, c) => !L[c].startsWith('I-') || (p >= 0 && L[p] !== 'O' && L[p].slice(2) === L[c].slice(2));
+  const dp = sc.map(() => new Float64Array(C).fill(-Infinity));
+  const bp = sc.map(() => new Int16Array(C).fill(-1));
+  for (let c = 0; c < C; c++) if (follow(-1, c)) dp[0][c] = sc[0][c];
+  for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) {
+    for (let c = 0; c < C; c++) {
+      if (sc[i][c] === -Infinity) continue;
+      let best = -Infinity; let arg = -1;
+      for (let p = 0; p < C; p++) if (dp[i - 1][p] > best && follow(p, c)) { best = dp[i - 1][p]; arg = p; }
+      if (arg >= 0) { dp[i][c] = best + sc[i][c]; bp[i][c] = arg; }
+    }
+  }
+  let last = 0;
+  for (let c = 1; c < C; c++) if (dp[n - 1][c] > dp[n - 1][last]) last = c;
+  const path = new Array(n);
+  path[n - 1] = last;
+  for (let i = n - 1; i > 0; i--) path[i - 1] = Math.max(0, bp[i][path[i]]);
+  const spans = [];
+  let cur = null;
+  path.forEach((c, i) => {
+    const l = L[c];
+    const t = toks[i];
+    if (l === 'O') { cur = null; return; }
+    if (l.startsWith('B-') || !cur || cur.type !== l.slice(2)) { cur = { type: l.slice(2), start: t.start, end: t.end }; spans.push(cur); } else cur.end = t.end;
+  });
+  // widen to word boundaries, trim trailing punctuation, merge spans that now overlap
+  const out = [];
+  for (const s of spans) {
+    let a = s.start; let b = s.end;
+    while (a > 0 && !/\s/.test(text[a - 1])) a--;
+    while (b < text.length && !/\s/.test(text[b])) b++;
+    let w = text.slice(a, b);
+    const lead = w.match(/^["'„“`(]+/)?.[0].length || 0;
+    const trail = w.match(/["'”`),.;:!?]+$/)?.[0].length || 0;
+    const quoted = lead > 0 && /["'„“`]/.test(w[0]);
+    if (!quoted) { a += lead; b -= trail; } else {
+      // quoted value: the whole quoted string (may contain spaces)
+      const q = w[0] === '„' ? '”' : w[0];
+      const close = text.indexOf(q === '“' ? '”' : q, a + 1);
+      if (close > a) b = close + 1;
+    }
+    if (b <= a) continue;
+    const prev = out[out.length - 1];
+    if (prev && a < prev.end) { if (prev.type === s.type) prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, b); continue; }
+    out.push({ type: s.type, start: a, end: b, quoted });
+  }
+  for (const s of out) s.text = text.slice(s.start, s.end);
+  return out;
+}
diff --git a/src/rerank/hybrid.js b/src/rerank/hybrid.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..3d3731f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/rerank/hybrid.js
@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+// Hybrid policy: the linear cascade (A) answers when it is confident; otherwise a neural model re-ranks A's top-k.
+//
+//   A conf >= tau                      -> A (fast path, ~0.3 ms)
+//   A stage 1 says __none__ (keepNone)  -> keep A's rejection
+//   else  B (encoder) / C (tiny LM)    -> score_i = alpha*log pA_i + (1-alpha)*log pX_i over A's top-k candidates
+//                                         answer if pX(best) >= accept and pX(__none__) < none (B only), else reject
+//
+// suggestHybrid() wraps pipeline.suggest(): it runs the cheap pipeline first and only computes the neural model when
+// the cascade asks for help, then re-runs the pipeline with the re-ranked decision (history rules are never re-ranked).
+import { suggest } from '../pipeline.js';
+import { detectEnv } from '../env.js';
+import { FAMILY_OF, NONE } from '../tools.js';
+
+// calibrated on the training dev split (scripts/hybrid/eval_hybrid.js --calibrate); see HYBRID.md
+export const POLICY = {
+  // v0.4 (enc-v2 retrained without held-out augmented rows, recalibrated with an A_dev that excludes the dev split
+  // from every training source, OOD included); with the OOD-leaking A_dev A+B had tau 0.8, alpha 0.75; the first v0.4
+  // encoder had tau 0.9, alpha 0.5, none 0.3 (both); v0.3 had none: 0.5 and k: 5 for the safe variant
+  'A+B': { tau: 0.9, k: 5, alpha: 0.5, accept: 0, none: 0.5, keepNone: true, tagger: 'A' },
+  'A+B-safe': { tau: 0.9, k: 3, alpha: 0.5, accept: 0, none: 0.5, rescue: false, tagger: 'A' },
+  // A+C: C-ft rescored for the leak-free A_dev's candidates (before: tau 0.9)
+  'A+C': { tau: 0.8, k: 5, alpha: 0.75, accept: 0, keepNone: true },
+  'A+C-safe': { tau: 0.8, k: 5, alpha: 0.75, accept: 0, rescue: false },
+  B: { tau: Infinity, k: 0, alpha: 0, accept: 0, none: 0.3, keepNone: true, tagger: 'B' },
+  C: { tau: Infinity, k: 3, alpha: 0, accept: 0, keepNone: true },
+};
+
+const LOG = (p) => Math.log(Math.max(p, 1e-6));
+
+/**
+ * Re-rank a cascade result with model probabilities. pX: {intent: p} over (a superset of) the candidates;
+ * k = 0 means "all intents pX knows" (B alone). Returns a cascade-shaped object; `confidence` is pushed above/below
+ * the pipeline's accept threshold according to the policy's own accept rule.
+ */
+export function rerank(c, pX, P, { thr, pNone = 0 } = {}) {
+  if (c.confidence >= P.tau) return c;
+  // keepNone: the cascade's stage 1 says "not a shell request" -> keep its rejection (OOD safety)
+  if (P.keepNone && c.topTool === NONE && c.confidence < thr) return c;
+  // safe (rescue: false): only re-rank requests A answers anyway; A's rejections stay rejections
+  if (P.rescue === false && c.confidence < thr) return c;
+  const pa = Object.fromEntries(c.top.map((t) => [t.intent, t.p]));
+  const cands = P.k > 0 ? c.top.slice(0, P.k).map((t) => t.intent) : Object.keys(pX);
+  let best = null;
+  let bestS = -Infinity;
+  for (const i of cands) {
+    const s = P.alpha * LOG(pa[i] ?? 0) + (1 - P.alpha) * LOG(pX[i] ?? 0);
+    if (s > bestS) { bestS = s; best = i; }
+  }
+  if (!best) return c;
+  const px = pX[best] ?? 0;
+  const ok = px >= P.accept && pNone < (P.none ?? 1);
+  const conf = ok ? Math.max(thr, px) : Math.min(thr - 1e-6, px);
+  const tool = FAMILY_OF[best];
+  const top = [{ intent: best, tool, p: conf, pTool: pa[best] ?? 0, pIntent: px }, ...c.top.filter((t) => t.intent !== best)];
+  // an explicit model rejection (pNone >= none, or pX below accept) stays a rejection through the whole pipeline:
+  // topTool __none__ keeps the low-confidence composer from answering in its place
+  if (!ok) return { ...c, intent: best, tool, confidence: conf, top, reranked: true, topTool: NONE, rejected: true };
+  return { ...c, intent: best, tool, confidence: conf, top, reranked: true, topTool: tool };
+}
+
+/**
+ * opts: suggest() options + { system: 'A'|'B'|'C'|'A+B'|'A+C', encoder (src/rerank/encoder.js Encoder),
+ *        lm: async (text, env, candidateIntents) -> {intent: p}, policy }
+ * -> suggest() result + { hybrid: { system, deferred, model, ms } }
+ */
+export async function suggestHybrid(query, opts = {}) {
+  const system = opts.system || 'A+B';
+  const env = opts.env || detectEnv({ shell: opts.shell, os: opts.os });
+  const base = { ...opts, env };
+  if (system === 'A') return { ...suggest(query, base), hybrid: { system, deferred: false } };
+  const P = { ...POLICY[system], ...(opts.policy || {}) };
+  // the policy's k candidates are re-ranked whatever --top displays (k = 0: B alone, no cascade candidates needed)
+  base.rerankTop = P.k;
+  let seen = null;
+  const first = suggest(query, { ...base, rerank: (c) => { seen = c; return c; } });
+  if (!seen || seen.confidence >= P.tau) return { ...first, hybrid: { system, deferred: false } };
+  const t0 = performance.now();
+  let pX; let pNone = 0; let tagger;
+  if (/B/.test(system)) {
+    if (!opts.encoder) return { ...first, hybrid: { system, deferred: false, unavailable: 'encoder' } };
+    const b = await opts.encoder.infer(query, env);
+    pX = b.intents;
+    pNone = b.pNone;
+    if (P.tagger === 'B') tagger = b.tagger;
+  } else {
+    if (!opts.lm) return { ...first, hybrid: { system, deferred: false, unavailable: 'lm' } };
+    pX = await opts.lm(query, env, seen.top.slice(0, P.k).map((t) => t.intent));
+    if (!pX) return { ...first, hybrid: { system, deferred: true, unavailable: 'lm' } };
+  }
+  const ms = performance.now() - t0;
+  const res = suggest(query, { ...base, tagger, rerank: (c, { thr }) => rerank(c, pX, P, { thr, pNone }) });
+  return { ...res, hybrid: { system, deferred: true, ms, pNone } };
+}
+
+/** CLI entry: A+B with the encoder loaded lazily (only when the cascade defers); falls back to A when the optional
+ *  runtime or model bundle is missing (result.hybrid.unavailable says why). */
+let ENC = null;
+export async function suggestLazy(query, opts = {}) {
+  const encoder = { infer: async (t, env) => {
+    if (ENC === null) { const { Encoder } = await import('./encoder.js'); ENC = (await Encoder.load({ threads: 1 })) || false; }
+    if (!ENC) throw Object.assign(new Error('unavailable'), { unavailable: true });
+    return ENC.infer(t, env);
+  } };
+  try {
+    return await suggestHybrid(query, { ...opts, system: opts.system || 'A+B', encoder });
+  } catch (e) {
+    if (!e.unavailable) throw e;
+    return { ...suggest(query, opts), hybrid: { system: 'A', deferred: false, unavailable: 'encoder (install onnxruntime-node + tellsh-model-enc)' } };
+  }
+}
+
+export { NONE };

@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+// SentencePiece-Unigram tokenizer (XLM-R style) for the hybrid encoder, no dependencies.
+// Reproduces HF `tokenizers` for the pruned multilingual-e5 vocabulary: NFKC normalisation, whitespace split,
+// '▁' prepended to every word, Viterbi over piece log-probabilities, unknown characters -> <unk> (consecutive
+// unknowns fused), offsets into the original string.
+const UNK_PENALTY = 10;
+
+export class UnigramTokenizer {
+  /** vocab: [[piece, score], ...] in id order; unkId; special ids */
+  constructor({ vocab, unkId = 3, bos = 0, eos = 2, pad = 1 }) {
+    this.pieces = new Map();
+    this.maxLen = 1;
+    let min = Infinity;
+    vocab.forEach(([p, s], i) => {
+      if (i <= 3) return; // specials are never produced by segmentation
+      this.pieces.set(p, [i, s]);
+      const n = [...p].length;
+      if (n > this.maxLen) this.maxLen = n;
+      if (s < min) min = s;
+    });
+    this.unkScore = min - UNK_PENALTY;
+    Object.assign(this, { unkId, bos, eos, pad, size: vocab.length });
+  }
+
+  /** segment one word ('▁' + word) -> [{id, start, end}] with offsets in code points of the piece string */
+  segment(word) {
+    const chars = [...word];
+    const n = chars.length;
+    const best = new Float64Array(n + 1).fill(-Infinity);
+    const from = new Int32Array(n + 1).fill(-1);
+    const tokId = new Int32Array(n + 1).fill(-1);
+    best[0] = 0;
+    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
+      if (best[i] === -Infinity) continue;
+      let s = '';
+      let hit = false;
+      for (let j = i; j < Math.min(n, i + this.maxLen); j++) {
+        s += chars[j];
+        const e = this.pieces.get(s);
+        if (e) {
+          if (j === i) hit = true;
+          const v = best[i] + e[1];
+          if (v > best[j + 1]) { best[j + 1] = v; from[j + 1] = i; tokId[j + 1] = e[0]; }
+        }
+      }
+      if (!hit) { // single unknown character
+        const v = best[i] + this.unkScore;
+        if (v > best[i + 1]) { best[i + 1] = v; from[i + 1] = i; tokId[i + 1] = this.unkId; }
+      }
+    }
+    const out = [];
+    for (let k = n; k > 0; k = from[k]) out.push({ id: tokId[k], start: from[k], end: k });
+    out.reverse();
+    const fused = [];
+    for (const t of out) {
+      const last = fused[fused.length - 1];
+      if (last && last.id === this.unkId && t.id === this.unkId) last.end = t.end; else fused.push(t);
+    }
+    return fused;
+  }
+
+  /** -> [{id, start, end}] offsets are UTF-16 indices into `text` (the '▁' of a word maps to the word start) */
+  tokenize(text) {
+    const out = [];
+    const re = /\S+/gu;
+    let m;
+    while ((m = re.exec(text))) {
+      const raw = m[0];
+      const norm = raw.normalize('NFKC');
+      const same = norm === raw;
+      const cps = [...norm];
+      // code point index -> UTF-16 offset in raw (only exact when NFKC did not change the word)
+      const cu = [0];
+      for (const c of cps) cu.push(cu[cu.length - 1] + c.length);
+      for (const p of this.segment('▁' + norm.replace(/\s+/g, '▁'))) {
+        const s = Math.max(0, p.start - 1);
+        const e = Math.max(0, p.end - 1);
+        out.push({ id: p.id, start: m.index + (same ? cu[s] : 0), end: m.index + (same ? cu[e] : raw.length) });
+      }
+    }
+    return out;
+  }
+
+  /** XLM-R pair encoding: <s> A </s></s> B </s>; A truncated to fit maxLen. -> {ids, offsets (A only), nA} */
+  encodePair(a, b, maxLen = 64) {
+    const ta = this.tokenize(a);
+    const tb = this.tokenize(b);
+    const room = Math.max(1, maxLen - tb.length - 4);
+    const A = ta.slice(0, room);
+    const ids = [this.bos, ...A.map((t) => t.id), this.eos, this.eos, ...tb.map((t) => t.id), this.eos];
+    return { ids, tokens: A, nA: A.length };
+  }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+// The allowlist of the danger checker (src/allowlist-data.js) is generated from the catalog: it must match the templates.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { ALLOW } from '../src/allowlist-data.js';
+import { allowlistTable } from '../scripts/lib/allowlist_table.js';
+
+test('src/allowlist-data.js is up to date with the catalog (node scripts/build_allowlist.js)', () => {
+  assert.deepEqual(ALLOW, allowlistTable());
+});
diff --git a/test/compose.test.js b/test/compose.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..925834e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/compose.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+// Composer (second pass) regressions: review r1 Major 2 / Minor 10 and v0.3 composer fixes.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { compose, validateComposed } from '../src/compose.js';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { extractSlots } from '../src/slots.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const comp = (q, tool, extra = {}) => compose(q, [{ tool, p: 1 }], { ...extractSlots(q), ...extra }, { patternOf: () => extractSlots(q).quoted[0] ?? null, nameOf: () => null });
+
+test('composer: an operand starting with - never becomes an option (r1 Major 2)', () => {
+  const r = comp("spakuj notes.txt i '--use-compress-program=sh x.sh' do backup.tar szczegolowo", 'tar');
+  if (r && !r.invalid) {
+    assert.doesNotMatch(r.command, /\s'?--use-compress-program/, r.command);
+    assert.match(r.command, /\.\/--use-compress-program|-- /);
+  }
+  const s = suggest("spakuj notes.txt i '--use-compress-program=sh x.sh' do backup.tar szczegolowo", { env: BASH });
+  assert.ok(!/(^|\s)'?--use-compress-program/.test(s.command || ''), s.command);
+});
+
+test('composer validation unquotes words: a quoted option is still an option', () => {
+  assert.equal(validateComposed("tar -c -f a.tar '--use-compress-program=sh x.sh'", 'tar').ok, false);
+  assert.equal(validateComposed('grep -i -n -- error app.log', 'grep').ok, true); // `--` ends options
+  assert.equal(validateComposed("grep -i -- '-e' app.log", 'grep').ok, true);
+  assert.equal(validateComposed('grep -A', 'grep').ok, false);
+});
+
+test('composer: user filter value (duplicate case removed, r1 Minor 10)', () => {
+  assert.match(comp('find files in /tmp owned by user bob', 'find').command, /-user bob\b/);
+  assert.match(comp('show processes of user postgres', 'ps').command, /-u postgres\b/);
+  assert.equal(comp('find files owned by -rf', 'find')?.command?.includes('-user -rf') ?? false, false);
+});
+
+test('composer: file names do not trigger flags; numbers bind to their trigger', () => {
+  assert.equal(comp('count lines of words.txt without filename', 'wc').command, 'wc -l < words.txt');
+  assert.match(comp('show 3 lines after each match of timeout in server.log', 'grep', { quoted: ['timeout'] })?.command || 'grep -A 3', /-A 3/);
+  assert.equal(comp('first 100 bytes of dump.bin', 'head').command, 'head -c 100 dump.bin');
+});
+
+test('composer: grep compositions validate (`--` before the pattern)', () => {
+  const s = suggest('grep case-insensitive for error in app.log and show line numbers', { env: BASH });
+  assert.equal(s.method, 'composed');
+  assert.match(s.command, /^grep -i -n -- error app\.log$/);
+});
+
+test('CLI: output piped into a closed pipe exits cleanly (no EPIPE crash)', async () => {
+  const { spawnSync } = await import('node:child_process');
+  const r = spawnSync('sh', ['-c', 'node bin/tellsh.js --dry-run show disk usage | head -c 1 >/dev/null; echo $?'], { encoding: 'utf8' });
+  assert.doesNotMatch(r.stderr, /EPIPE/);
+});

diff --git a/test/devtools.test.js b/test/devtools.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..3f021b3
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/devtools.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+// v0.4 developer-tool intents: slot extraction (EN/PL), per-shell rendering, risk.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { buildCommand } from '../src/fill.js';
+import { BY_ID } from '../src/catalog.js';
+import { FAMILY_OF } from '../src/tools.js';
+import { NEW_INTENTS } from '../scripts/hybrid/sets.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const cmd = (id, text, env = BASH) => buildCommand(id, text, { env }).command;
+
+test('every v0.4 intent is in the catalog and a tool family', () => {
+  for (const id of NEW_INTENTS) {
+    assert.ok(BY_ID[id], id);
+    assert.ok(FAMILY_OF[id], id);
+  }
+});
+
+const CASES = [
+  ['npm_run_script', 'run the dev server with npm', 'npm run dev'],
+  ['npm_run_script', 'npm run build', 'npm run build'],
+  ['npm_run_script', 'odpal skrypt lint', 'npm run lint'],
+  ['npm_run_script', 'odpal serwer deweloperski', 'npm run dev'],
+  ['npm_run_script', 'odpal testy', 'npm run test'],
+  ['npm_run_script', 'run the storybook script', 'npm run storybook'],
+  ['npm_run_script', 'run my thing with npm', 'npm run <SCRIPT>'],
+  ['npm_run_script', 'run the "test:e2e" script', 'npm run test:e2e'],
+  ['npm_install', 'npm install', 'npm install'],
+  ['npm_install', 'install axios in this project', 'npm install axios'],
+  ['npm_install', 'yarn add zod', 'npm install zod'],
+  ['npm_install_global', 'install typescript globally', 'npm install -g typescript'],
+  ['npm_install_global', 'zainstaluj globalnie pakiet vercel', 'npm install -g vercel'],
+  ['npm_install_global', 'npm i -g @angular/cli', 'npm install -g @angular/cli'],
+  ['pip_install', 'pip install requests', 'python3 -m pip install requests'],
+  ['pip_install', 'install numpy with pip', 'python3 -m pip install numpy'],
+  ['pip_install', 'pip3 install pillow==10.4.0', 'python3 -m pip install pillow==10.4.0'],
+  ['tool_version', 'what version of node do I have', 'node --version'],
+  ['tool_version', 'jaka mam wersje pythona3? python3', 'python3 --version'],
+  ['cli_help', 'show help for wrangler', 'wrangler --help'],
+  ['print_line_range', 'show lines 120-180 of src/app.js', "sed -n '120,180p' src/app.js"],
+  ['print_line_range', 'pokaż linie od 10 do 25 w config.yaml', "sed -n '10,25p' config.yaml"],
+  ['print_line_range', 'lines 40 to 12 of main.py', "sed -n '12,40p' main.py"],
+  ['ssh_port_forward', 'forward port 5432 from db.example.com', 'ssh -N -L 5432:localhost:5432 db.example.com'],
+  ['ssh_port_forward', 'tunel ssh na port 8080 do ola@10.0.0.5', 'ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:8080 ola@10.0.0.5'],
+  ['gh_pr_view', 'show PR 42', 'gh pr view 42'],
+  ['gh_pr_view', 'show the current pull request', 'gh pr view'],
+  ['gh_pr_checks', 'czy CI przeszło na PR 7', 'gh pr checks 7'],
+  ['gh_run_view', 'show workflow run 81234567', 'gh run view 81234567'],
+  ['wrangler_secret_put', 'set the API_KEY secret on my worker', 'npx wrangler secret put API_KEY'],
+  ['activate_venv', 'activate the venv', '. .venv/bin/activate'],
+  ['activate_venv', 'activate the virtualenv in ./env', '. ./env/bin/activate'],
+];
+for (const [id, text, want] of CASES) {
+  test(`${id}: ${text}`, () => assert.equal(cmd(id, text), want));
+}
+
+test('installer words are not package names; apt installs keep working', () => {
+  assert.equal(cmd('install_package', 'install npm'), 'sudo apt install npm');
+  assert.equal(cmd('install_package', 'zainstaluj mi htop'), 'sudo apt install htop');
+  assert.equal(cmd('install_package', 'apt install vim'), 'sudo apt install vim');
+});
+
+test('per-shell renders of the new intents', () => {
+  const R = { script: 'dev', pkg: 'requests', cmd: 'node', start: 10, end: 20, file: 'app.log', port: 5432, target: 'db.example.com', num: 42, pr: 42 };
+  const r = (id, env) => buildCommand(id, '', { env, resolved: { ...R } });
+  const PS = { shell: 'powershell', os: 'win32' };
+  const CMD = { shell: 'cmd', os: 'win32' };
+  const FISH = { shell: 'fish', os: 'linux' };
+  assert.equal(r('pip_install', PS).command, "py -m pip install 'requests'");
+  assert.equal(r('pip_install', CMD).command, 'py -m pip install requests');
+  assert.equal(r('tool_version', PS).command, "& 'node' --version");
+  assert.equal(r('print_line_range', PS).command, "Get-Content -LiteralPath 'app.log' | Select-Object -Index ((10 - 1)..(20 - 1))");
+  assert.equal(r('print_line_range', CMD).command, null);
+  assert.match(r('print_line_range', CMD).gap, /cmd\.exe/);
+  assert.equal(r('activate_venv', FISH).command, 'source .venv/bin/activate.fish');
+  assert.equal(r('activate_venv', PS).command, "& (Join-Path '.venv' 'Scripts/Activate.ps1')");
+  assert.equal(r('activate_venv', { shell: 'powershell', os: 'linux' }).command, "& (Join-Path '.venv' 'bin/Activate.ps1')");
+  assert.equal(r('activate_venv', CMD).command, 'call .venv\\Scripts\\activate.bat');
+  assert.equal(r('gh_pr_view', PS).command, 'gh pr view 42');
+});
+
+test('risk: installs, project scripts, deploys, merges and tunnels are never safe', () => {
+  for (const id of ['npm_run_script', 'npm_install', 'npm_install_global', 'pip_install', 'activate_venv', 'wrangler_deploy',
+    'wrangler_secret_put', 'wrangler_tail', 'wrangler_login', 'wrangler_whoami', 'gh_pr_create', 'gh_pr_merge', 'ssh_port_forward']) assert.notEqual(BY_ID[id].risk, 'safe', id);
+  for (const id of ['gh_pr_list', 'gh_auth_status', 'tool_version', 'cli_help', 'print_line_range']) {
+    assert.equal(BY_ID[id].risk, 'safe', id);
+  }
+  // a rendered safe command stays safe (no danger warnings)
+  const r = buildCommand('print_line_range', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { file: 'a.txt', start: 1, end: 5 } });
+  assert.equal(r.risk, 'safe');
+});
+
+test('raw numeric slots never take non-numbers', () => {
+  const r = buildCommand('print_line_range', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { file: 'a.txt', start: '1;rm -rf /', end: 5 } });
+  assert.doesNotMatch(r.command || '', /rm -rf/);
+  const g = buildCommand('gh_pr_view', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { num: '$(id)' } });
+  assert.doesNotMatch(g.command || '', /\$\(id\)/);
+});

diff --git a/test/hybrid.test.js b/test/hybrid.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..41d841c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/hybrid.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggestHybrid, rerank, POLICY } from '../src/rerank/hybrid.js';
+import { NONE } from '../src/tools.js';
+
+const env = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux' };
+// fake encoder: puts all mass on one intent, so the re-ranked decision is fully determined by the policy
+const fake = (intent, pNone = 0) => ({ infer: async () => ({ intents: { [intent]: 0.99 }, pNone, tagger: undefined }) });
+
+test('confident cascade answers alone (encoder never called)', async () => {
+  let called = false;
+  const enc = { infer: async () => { called = true; return { intents: {}, pNone: 0 }; } };
+  const r = await suggestHybrid('show git status', { env, encoder: enc });
+  assert.equal(r.intent, 'git_status');
+  assert.equal(r.hybrid.deferred, false);
+  assert.equal(called, false);
+});
+
+test('rerank only picks among the cascade top-k', () => {
+  const c = { confidence: 0.5, topTool: 'fs', intent: 'a', tool: 'fs', tools: [], top: [{ intent: 'a', p: 0.5 }, { intent: 'b', p: 0.3 }] };
+  const r = rerank(c, { b: 0.9, zzz: 0.99 }, POLICY['A+B'], { thr: 0.3 });
+  assert.equal(r.intent, 'b');
+  assert.ok(r.reranked);
+});
+
+test('keepNone keeps the cascade rejection; safe never rescues', () => {
+  const none = { confidence: 0.1, topTool: NONE, intent: 'a', tool: 'fs', tools: [], top: [{ intent: 'a', p: 0.1 }] };
+  assert.equal(rerank(none, { a: 0.99 }, POLICY['A+B'], { thr: 0.3 }), none);
+  const low = { ...none, topTool: 'fs' };
+  assert.equal(rerank(low, { a: 0.99 }, POLICY['A+B-safe'], { thr: 0.3 }), low);
+  // encoder says "not a shell request" -> rejection
+  assert.ok(rerank(low, { a: 0.99 }, POLICY['A+B'], { thr: 0.3, pNone: 0.9 }).confidence < 0.3);
+});
+
+test('re-ranked dangerous answers keep the danger checks of the normal pipeline', async () => {
+  const r = await suggestHybrid('get rid of everything in /', { env, encoder: fake('delete_dir') });
+  assert.equal(r.intent, 'delete_dir');
+  assert.equal(r.risk, 'high');
+  assert.equal(r.critical, true);
+  assert.equal(r.hybrid.deferred, true);
+});
+
+test('missing encoder falls back to the cascade', async () => {
+  const r = await suggestHybrid('zrób coś z plikami chyba', { env });
+  assert.ok(r.hybrid.unavailable === 'encoder' || r.hybrid.deferred === false);
+});

diff --git a/test/regressions10.test.js b/test/regressions10.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b9eba1b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions10.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,145 @@
+// Regression tests for round 9: the round-8 findings (review/r8-claude.md, review/r8-codex.md). A quoted argument
+// after the first that mixes request words with a path or file name is unclear, not a path; history values of
+// `git -C` / `docker --context` commands belong to another repository / daemon; a script and its arguments are
+// several operands; bash does not write the running call to its history first; system files written by dd, cp,
+// install, mv, ln -f, perl -i or chmod 000 are critical; unclear arguments are checked against every operand slot;
+// the A_dev calibration model excludes the hybrid dev split from every training source.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { checkDanger } from '../src/danger.js';
+import { joinArgs } from '../src/shellwords.js';
+import { analyzeCommand, isAmbiguous } from '../src/history.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history, o = {}) => suggest(q, { env: BASH, ...(history ? { history } : {}), ...o });
+const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url));
+const BIN = join(ROOT, 'bin', 'tellsh.js');
+const cliJson = (...words) => JSON.parse(spawnSync(process.execPath, [BIN, '--json', '--shell', 'bash', '--os', 'linux', ...words],
+  { encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, NO_COLOR: '1' } }).stdout);
+const refused = (r, ph, why) => {
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${why}: ${JSON.stringify(r.context)} -> ${r.command}`);
+  assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes(ph), `${why}: ${r.command}`);
+};
+
+test('major: a quoted argument mixing request words with a path or file name is unclear, not the path', () => {
+  assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['delete', 'folder /tmp/x']), { text: 'delete "folder /tmp/x"', unclear: ['folder /tmp/x'] });
+  assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['delete', 'the file notes.txt']), { text: 'delete "the file notes.txt"', unclear: ['the file notes.txt'] });
+  assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['usuń', 'plik raport.pdf']), { text: 'usuń "plik raport.pdf"', unclear: ['plik raport.pdf'] });
+  assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['delete', 'all files in /tmp/x']).unclear, ['all files in /tmp/x']);
+  assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['usuń', 'katalog /tmp/x']).unclear, ['katalog /tmp/x']);
+  // the space before the separator: a request word and a path, or a directory with a space? unclear
+  assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['delete', 'my data/a.txt']).unclear, ['my data/a.txt']);
+  // genuine names stay values
+  for (const v of ['My Notes.txt', 'data/my notes.txt', '/tmp/my data', '~/My Documents', './a b/c.txt']) {
+    assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['delete', v]), { text: `delete "${v}"`, unclear: [] }, v);
+  }
+  // the first word is still the request
+  assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['delete folder', '/tmp/x']), { text: 'delete folder /tmp/x', unclear: [] });
+
+  const cases = [
+    [['delete', 'folder /tmp/x'], '<PATH>', /\/tmp\/x/],
+    [['delete', 'the file notes.txt'], '<FILE>', /notes\.txt/],
+    [['usuń', 'plik raport.pdf'], '<FILE>', /raport/],
+    [['delete', 'all files in /tmp/x'], '<PATH>', /\/tmp\/x/],
+  ];
+  for (const [args, ph, bad] of cases) {
+    const r = cliJson(...args);
+    assert.ok(r.command.includes(ph) && !bad.test(r.command), `${args}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.ok(r.warnings.some((w) => /quoted argument is a name or part of the request/.test(w)), `${args}: ${r.warnings}`);
+  }
+  assert.equal(cliJson('delete', 'My Notes.txt').command, "rm 'My Notes.txt'");
+});
+
+test('major: the history copy of such a call is not read as the path', () => {
+  for (const h of ['tellsh delete "folder /tmp/x"', 'tellsh delete "the file notes.txt"', "tellsh usuń 'plik raport.pdf'"]) {
+    for (const q of ['show it', 'delete it']) {
+      const r = run(q, [h]);
+      assert.ok(!/folder|the file|plik/.test(r.command ?? ''), `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    }
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['tellsh show "My Notes.txt"']).command, "rm 'My Notes.txt'");
+});
+
+test('major: history values of a command scoped to another repository, directory or daemon are refused', () => {
+  refused(run('delete it', ['git -C /repo blame notes.txt']), '<FILE>', 'git -C blame');
+  refused(run('delete it', ['git --work-tree=/srv/app diff a.txt']), '<FILE>', 'git --work-tree=');
+  refused(run('stop it', ['docker --context production logs web']), '<CONTAINER>', 'docker --context');
+  refused(run('stop it', ['docker -H tcp://prod:2375 logs web']), '<CONTAINER>', 'docker -H');
+  refused(run('stop it', ['DOCKER_HOST=tcp://prod:2375 docker logs web']), '<CONTAINER>', 'DOCKER_HOST=');
+  // and the command is not repeated without its scope
+  for (const q of ['do it again', 'same for api']) {
+    const r = run(q, ['docker --context production logs web']);
+    assert.ok(!/^docker (?:logs|stop)\b/.test(r.command ?? '') || r.command.includes('<'), `${q}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  const a = analyzeCommand('docker --context production logs web');
+  assert.ok(isAmbiguous(a.ents.container) && (a.intent == null || a.ambiguous), JSON.stringify(a));
+  // without a scope option nothing changes
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['git blame notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('stop it', ['docker logs web']).command, 'docker stop web');
+  assert.equal(run('stop it', ['docker --debug logs web']).command, 'docker stop web');
+});
+
+test('minor: a script and its arguments are several operands', () => {
+  for (const h of ['python3 script.py data.csv', 'node build.js out/', 'bash deploy.sh prod.env']) {
+    const r = run('delete it', [h]);
+    assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes('<'), `${h}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['python3 script.py']).command, 'rm script.py');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['node build.js --watch']).command, 'rm build.js');
+});
+
+test('nit: bash does not write the running call first, so an identical last tellsh line is the previous command', () => {
+  const h = (shell) => Object.assign(['cat secret.txt', 'tellsh delete it'], { kind: 'posix', shell });
+  assert.ok(!/secret/.test(run('delete it', h('bash')).command ?? ''), 'bash');
+  // zsh / fish / PSReadLine write it first: the line is this call, the previous command is the one before it
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', h('zsh')).command, 'rm secret.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', h('fish')).command, 'rm secret.txt');
+});
+
+test('minor: dd, cp, install, mv, ln -f, perl -i and chmod 000 onto a system file are critical', () => {
+  for (const c of ['dd if=/dev/zero of=/etc/passwd', 'sudo dd if=x of=/boot/vmlinuz', 'cp /tmp/x /etc/passwd', 'install -m 644 x /etc/passwd',
+    'sudo mv /tmp/x /etc/shadow', 'ln -sf /tmp/x /etc/passwd', 'perl -pi -e s/a/b/ /etc/passwd', 'perl -i.bak -pe 1 /etc/fstab', 'chmod 000 /etc/passwd',
+    'sudo sh -c "cp x /etc/passwd"']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.ok(d.critical && d.risk === 'high', `${c}: ${JSON.stringify(d)}`);
+  }
+  // reading a system file, copying into a system directory, ordinary dd / chmod: not critical
+  for (const c of ['cp /etc/passwd /tmp/x', 'sudo cp x.service /etc/systemd/system/', 'dd if=a.iso of=out.img', 'chmod 644 /etc/hosts',
+    'ln -s /etc/passwd x', 'perl -pi -e s/a/b/ notes.txt', 'cp -t /etc/nginx a.conf']) {
+    assert.ok(!checkDanger(c).critical, c);
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: an unclear argument blanks every operand slot it contains, not only path slots', () => {
+  const r = run('stop service nginx', null, { unclearArgs: ['nginx please'] });
+  assert.ok(r.command.includes('<SERVICE>') && !/nginx/.test(r.command), r.command);
+  assert.ok(r.warnings.some((w) => /^value left as a placeholder/.test(w)), r.warnings.join('; '));
+  const c = run('stop container web', null, { unclearArgs: ['web now'] });
+  assert.ok(c.command.includes('<CONTAINER>'), c.command);
+  // text slots (a commit message) are not operands
+  assert.ok(/fix the bug/.test(run('commit "fix the bug"', null, { unclearArgs: ['fix the bug'] }).command));
+  // unrelated unclear arguments change nothing
+  assert.equal(run('stop service nginx', null, { unclearArgs: ['my data'] }).command, 'sudo systemctl stop nginx');
+});
+
+test('major: A_dev excludes the hybrid dev split from every training source (OOD, tldr, anaphora too)', () => {
+  const sh = readFileSync(join(ROOT, 'scripts/hybrid/train_a_dev.sh'), 'utf8');
+  const gen = readFileSync(join(ROOT, 'scripts/gen_data.js'), 'utf8');
+  // the lines the script rewrites exist in gen_data.js, and the script fails when a rewrite did not happen
+  assert.ok(gen.includes('if (heldOut.has(r0.text)) { dropped++; continue; }'));
+  assert.ok(/^ {2}const leaks = excl\.has;$/m.test(gen));
+  assert.ok(gen.includes("import { ctxFeatures } from '../src/history.js';"));
+  assert.ok(sh.includes("grep -q 'const leaks = (t) => excl.has(t) || isDevText(t);'"));
+  // every source goes through leaks(): the OOD and tldr loaders and every emitted row
+  for (const re of [/for \(const r of ood\) \{\s*if \(leaks\(r\.text\)\) continue;/, /if \(leaks\(r\.text\)\) continue;\s*const key = r\.tool/, /const emit = [^\n]*\n\s*if \(leaks\(text\)\)/]) {
+    assert.ok(re.test(gen), String(re));
+  }
+  // the rewrite applied to gen_data.js produces the expected line
+  const sed = spawnSync('sh', ['-c', `sed -n -e "s#^  const leaks = excl.has;\\$#  const leaks = (t) => excl.has(t) || isDevText(t);#p" "${join(ROOT, 'scripts/gen_data.js')}"`], { encoding: 'utf8' });
+  assert.equal(sed.stdout.trim(), 'const leaks = (t) => excl.has(t) || isDevText(t);');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions11.test.js b/test/regressions11.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..71d6252
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions11.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+// Regression tests for round 10: the round-9 findings (review/r9-codex.md). `wrangler dev` runs the project's build
+// command, so it is not safe (never auto-run with --yes); attached short-option values (`git -C/repo`,
+// `docker -Htcp://…`) scope a history command like the separate form; a wrapper that changes the working directory
+// (`env -C`, `sudo -D`) or the root (`chroot`) keeps that scope; the hybrid export drops train rows equal to a dev
+// text and A_dev excludes the complete exported dev split.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { BY_ID } from '../src/catalog.js';
+import { analyzeCommand, isAmbiguous } from '../src/history.js';
+import { normalize } from '../src/features.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history) => suggest(q, { env: BASH, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url));
+const BIN = join(ROOT, 'bin', 'tellsh.js');
+const refused = (r, ph, why) => {
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${why}: ${JSON.stringify(r.context)} -> ${r.command}`);
+  assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes(ph), `${why}: ${r.command}`);
+};
+
+test('major: wrangler dev runs project build commands: medium risk, never auto-run with --yes', () => {
+  assert.equal(BY_ID.wrangler_dev.risk, 'medium');
+  assert.equal(BY_ID.wrangler_dev.risk, BY_ID.npm_run_script.risk);
+  const r = run('start wrangler dev');
+  assert.equal(r.intent, 'wrangler_dev');
+  assert.notEqual(r.risk, 'safe');
+  // nothing can run even if the gate regressed: no npx on PATH
+  const c = spawnSync(process.execPath, [BIN, '--yes', '--shell', 'bash', '--os', 'linux', 'start', 'wrangler', 'dev'],
+    { encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, NO_COLOR: '1', PATH: '/nonexistent' } });
+  assert.equal(c.status, 4, c.stdout + c.stderr);
+  assert.match(c.stdout, /only auto-runs safe/);
+});
+
+test('major: attached short-option values scope a history command like the separate form', () => {
+  refused(run('delete it', ['git -C/repo blame notes.txt']), '<FILE>', 'git -C/repo');
+  refused(run('stop it', ['docker -Htcp://prod:2375 logs web']), '<CONTAINER>', 'docker -Htcp://');
+  refused(run('stop it', ['docker -cprod logs web']), '<CONTAINER>', 'docker -cprod');
+  refused(run('stop it', ['docker --host=tcp://prod:2375 logs web']), '<CONTAINER>', 'docker --host=');
+  for (const h of ['git -C/repo blame notes.txt', 'docker -Htcp://prod:2375 logs web']) {
+    const a = analyzeCommand(h);
+    assert.ok(a.scoped, h);
+    assert.ok(Object.values(a.ents).every((v) => v == null || isAmbiguous(v)), `${h}: ${JSON.stringify(a.ents)}`);
+    for (const q of ['do it again', 'show it']) {
+      const r = run(q, [h]);
+      assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes('<'), `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    }
+  }
+  // git -c (config) is not a scope, attached or not; neither is a plain docker flag
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['git -ccolor.ui=false blame notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['git -c color.ui=false blame notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('stop it', ['docker -D logs web']).command, 'docker stop web');
+});
+
+test('major: a wrapper that changes the working directory or root keeps that scope', () => {
+  for (const h of ['env -C /repo cat notes.txt', 'sudo -D /repo cat notes.txt', 'env --chdir=/repo cat notes.txt', 'env -C/repo cat notes.txt',
+    'sudo -D/repo cat notes.txt', 'sudo --chdir /repo cat notes.txt', 'sudo -u root -D /repo cat notes.txt', 'env -i -C /repo cat notes.txt',
+    'nice -n 5 env -C /repo cat notes.txt', 'unshare --wd=/repo cat notes.txt', 'systemd-run --working-directory=/repo cat notes.txt']) {
+    for (const q of ['delete it', 'show it']) refused(run(q, [h]), '<FILE>', `${q} after ${h}`);
+  }
+  // an absolute path names the same file from any directory
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['env -C /repo cat /tmp/abs.txt']).command, 'rm /tmp/abs.txt');
+  // another root: every path names something else
+  for (const h of ['chroot /srv cat /etc/x', 'sudo chroot /srv cat notes.txt', 'unshare -R /srv cat /etc/x', 'nsenter --root=/srv cat /etc/x']) {
+    refused(run('delete it', [h]), '<FILE>', h);
+  }
+  // wrappers that keep the directory change nothing
+  for (const h of ['sudo -u root cat notes.txt', 'nice -n 5 cat notes.txt', 'env FOO=1 cat notes.txt', 'env -i cat notes.txt', 'doas -C /etc/doas.conf cat notes.txt']) {
+    assert.equal(run('delete it', [h]).command, 'rm notes.txt', h);
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: hybrid export drops train rows equal to a dev text; A_dev excludes the complete dev split', () => {
+  const ex = readFileSync(join(ROOT, 'scripts/hybrid/export_data.js'), 'utf8');
+  assert.ok(ex.includes("r.split === 'dev' || !devTexts.has(normalize(r.text))"));
+  assert.ok(ex.includes("'dev_texts.json'"));
+  const sh = readFileSync(join(ROOT, 'scripts/hybrid/train_a_dev.sh'), 'utf8');
+  assert.ok(sh.includes("grep -q '_devIndex.has(normalize(t))'"));
+  // the rewritten import line parses and uses the dev index
+  const sed = spawnSync('sh', ['-c', `DEV_TEXTS=/x.json; sed -n -e "s#^import { ctxFeatures } from '../src/history.js';#&\\nconst _devIndex = new Set(JSON.parse(readFileSync('$DEV_TEXTS', 'utf8')));#p" "${join(ROOT, 'scripts/gen_data.js')}"`], { encoding: 'utf8' });
+  assert.match(sed.stdout, /const _devIndex = new Set\(JSON\.parse\(readFileSync\('\/x\.json', 'utf8'\)\)\);/);
+  // when the export exists, no train row has a dev text
+  const p = join(ROOT, 'build/hybrid/train.jsonl');
+  let rows;
+  try { rows = readFileSync(p, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean).map((l) => JSON.parse(l)); } catch { return; }
+  const dev = new Set(rows.filter((r) => r.split === 'dev').map((r) => normalize(r.text)));
+  assert.equal(rows.filter((r) => r.split === 'train' && dev.has(normalize(r.text))).length, 0);
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions12.test.js b/test/regressions12.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..468f273
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions12.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+// Regression tests for round 11: the round-10 findings (review/r10-claude.md, review/r10-codex.md). A login shell
+// (`sudo -i`, `sudo --login`, `sudo -iu bob`, `runuser -l`) runs in the target user's home and `sudo --chroot` under
+// another root, so history values keep that scope; a `cd` inside a `( … )` subshell does not outlast it, so relative
+// values after it name files elsewhere (a `{ … }` group runs in the user's shell and stays as it was); every
+// `npx wrangler` intent may run a project-local binary, so none is safe (never auto-run with --yes).
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { BY_ID, INTENTS } from '../src/catalog.js';
+import { analyzeCommand, isAmbiguous } from '../src/history.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history) => suggest(q, { env: BASH, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url));
+const BIN = join(ROOT, 'bin', 'tellsh.js');
+const refused = (r, ph, why) => {
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${why}: ${JSON.stringify(r.context)} -> ${r.command}`);
+  assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes(ph), `${why}: ${r.command}`);
+};
+
+test('major: sudo -i / --login and runuser -l run in the target home: relative history values are ambiguous', () => {
+  for (const h of ['sudo -i cat notes.txt', 'sudo --login cat notes.txt', 'sudo -u bob -i cat notes.txt', 'sudo -iu bob cat notes.txt',
+    'sudo -n -i cat notes.txt', 'runuser -l bob cat notes.txt', 'runuser --login bob cat notes.txt', 'time sudo -i cat notes.txt']) {
+    refused(run('delete it', [h]), '<FILE>', h);
+    const r = run('show it', [h]);
+    assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes('<'), `show it after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    const a = analyzeCommand(h);
+    assert.ok(a.ents.file == null || isAmbiguous(a.ents.file), `${h}: ${JSON.stringify(a.ents)}`);
+  }
+  // absolute paths name the same file from any directory
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['sudo -i cat /tmp/a.txt']).command, 'rm /tmp/a.txt');
+  // plain sudo / sudo -u keep the user's directory
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['sudo cat notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['sudo -u bob cat notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+});
+
+test('major: sudo --chroot / -R runs under another root: every history value is ambiguous', () => {
+  for (const h of ['sudo --chroot=/srv cat /etc/x', 'sudo --chroot /srv cat /etc/x', 'sudo -R /srv cat /etc/x', 'sudo -R/srv cat notes.txt']) {
+    refused(run('delete it', [h]), '<FILE>', h);
+    const r = run('show it', [h]);
+    assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes('<'), `show it after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: a cd / pushd inside a ( … ) subshell does not outlast it: relative values after it are ambiguous', () => {
+  for (const h of ['(cd /repo && cat notes.txt)', '(cd /repo; cat notes.txt)', '( cd /repo && cat notes.txt )', '(cd /repo && touch notes.txt)',
+    '(pushd /repo && cat notes.txt)', '(cd /repo && (cat notes.txt))', 'true && (cd /repo && cat notes.txt)']) {
+    refused(run('delete it', [h]), '<FILE>', h);
+    const r = run('show it', [h]);
+    assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes('<'), `show it after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  // absolute paths are fine; so is a segment after the subshell closed (back in the user's directory)
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['(cd /repo && cat /tmp/a.txt)']).command, 'rm /tmp/a.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['(cd /repo); cat notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['(cd /repo && make) && cat notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+  // a { … } group and a plain cd run in the user's own shell: the user is now in /repo
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['{ cd /repo && cat notes.txt; }']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cd /repo && cat notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+});
+
+test('major: every npx wrangler intent is at least medium risk, never auto-run with --yes', () => {
+  const ids = INTENTS.filter((t) => /^npx wrangler\b/.test(t.template)).map((t) => t.id);
+  for (const id of ['wrangler_tail', 'wrangler_login', 'wrangler_whoami', 'wrangler_dev', 'wrangler_deploy']) assert.ok(ids.includes(id), id);
+  for (const id of ids) assert.notEqual(BY_ID[id].risk, 'safe', id);
+  for (const [q, id] of [['wrangler whoami', 'wrangler_whoami'], ['stream cloudflare worker logs', 'wrangler_tail'], ['log in to cloudflare with wrangler', 'wrangler_login']]) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.equal(r.intent, id, q);
+    assert.notEqual(r.risk, 'safe', q);
+    // nothing can run even if the gate regressed: no npx on PATH
+    const c = spawnSync(process.execPath, [BIN, '--yes', '--shell', 'bash', '--os', 'linux', ...q.split(' ')],
+      { encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, NO_COLOR: '1', PATH: '/nonexistent' } });
+    assert.equal(c.status, 4, q + ': ' + c.stdout + c.stderr);
+    assert.match(c.stdout, /only auto-runs safe/);
+  }
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions13.test.js b/test/regressions13.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..17dc0c8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions13.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+// Regression tests for round 12: the round-11 findings (review/r11-claude.md, review/r11-codex.md). `pkexec` always
+// runs the command in the target user's home and `run0 --chdir=… / --user=…` in another directory, so relative history
+// values keep that scope; a redirection inside a `( … )` subshell after a `cd` opened its file in that directory, not
+// here; an explicit encoder rejection (high pNone) stays a rejection, the composer never answers in its place.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { analyzeCommand, isAmbiguous } from '../src/history.js';
+import { suggestHybrid, rerank, POLICY } from '../src/rerank/hybrid.js';
+import { NONE } from '../src/tools.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history) => suggest(q, { env: BASH, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const refused = (r, ph, why) => {
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${why}: ${JSON.stringify(r.context)} -> ${r.command}`);
+  assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes(ph), `${why}: ${r.command}`);
+};
+
+test('major: pkexec and run0 --chdir / --user run elsewhere: relative history values are ambiguous', () => {
+  for (const h of ['pkexec cat notes.txt', 'pkexec --user bob cat notes.txt', 'pkexec --disable-internal-agent cat notes.txt',
+    'nohup pkexec cat notes.txt', 'run0 --chdir=/srv cat notes.txt', 'run0 -D /srv cat notes.txt', 'run0 -D/srv cat notes.txt',
+    'run0 --user=bob cat notes.txt', 'run0 -u bob cat notes.txt', 'run0 --chdir /srv cat notes.txt', 'run0 --nice=5 --user=bob cat notes.txt']) {
+    refused(run('delete it', [h]), '<FILE>', h);
+    const r = run('show it', [h]);
+    assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes('<'), `show it after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    const a = analyzeCommand(h);
+    assert.ok(a.ents.file == null || isAmbiguous(a.ents.file), `${h}: ${JSON.stringify(a.ents)}`);
+  }
+  // an absolute path names the same file from any directory
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['pkexec cat /tmp/abs.txt']).command, 'rm /tmp/abs.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['run0 --chdir=/srv cat /tmp/abs.txt']).command, 'rm /tmp/abs.txt');
+  // run0 as root without --chdir keeps the directory
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['run0 cat notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
