+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['run0 --nice=5 cat notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+});
+
+test('major: a redirection inside a ( … ) subshell after a cd names a file in that directory', () => {
+  for (const h of ['(cd /repo && echo hi > notes.txt)', '(cd /repo; echo hi >> notes.txt)', '(cd /repo && sort a.txt > notes.txt)',
+    '(pushd /repo && echo hi > notes.txt)', 'ls; (cd /repo && echo hi 2> notes.txt)']) {
+    refused(run('delete it', [h]), '<FILE>', h);
+    const a = analyzeCommand(h);
+    assert.ok(a.ents.file == null || isAmbiguous(a.ents.file), `${h}: ${JSON.stringify(a.ents)}`);
+  }
+  // absolute targets and redirections opened by the calling shell still resolve
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['(cd /repo && echo hi > /tmp/abs.txt)']).command, 'rm /tmp/abs.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['(cd /repo && cat notes.txt) > out.txt']).command, 'rm out.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['(cd /repo && make); echo hi > out.txt']).command, 'rm out.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['{ cd /repo && echo hi > notes.txt; }']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['echo hi > notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+});
+
+test('major: an explicit encoder rejection (high pNone) is never overridden by the composer', async () => {
+  const env = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux' };
+  const q = 'list directories recursively with sizes';
+  const rejecting = { infer: async () => ({ intents: { list_files: 0.6, disk_usage: 0.3 }, pNone: 0.99 }) };
+  const r = await suggestHybrid(q, { env, encoder: rejecting });
+  assert.equal(r.hybrid.deferred, true);
+  assert.equal(r.understood, false, `${r.method}: ${r.command}`);
+  assert.equal(r.command ?? null, null);
+  assert.notEqual(r.method, 'composed');
+  // the same encoder without the rejection lets the pipeline answer
+  const accepting = { infer: async () => ({ intents: { list_files: 0.6, disk_usage: 0.3 }, pNone: 0 }) };
+  assert.equal((await suggestHybrid(q, { env, encoder: accepting })).understood, true);
+  // rerank itself marks the rejection
+  const c = { confidence: 0.5, topTool: 'ls', intent: 'a', tool: 'ls', tools: [], top: [{ intent: 'a', p: 0.5 }] };
+  const rr = rerank(c, { a: 0.99 }, POLICY['A+B'], { thr: 0.3, pNone: 0.9 });
+  assert.equal(rr.topTool, NONE);
+  assert.ok(rr.rejected);
+  assert.ok(rr.confidence < 0.3);
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions14.test.js b/test/regressions14.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0360323
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions14.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+// Regression tests for round 13: the round-12 findings (review/r12-codex.md). An explicit pull request (number, URL or
+// branch) is kept in `gh pr merge/view/checks`, or withheld as a placeholder, never dropped for the current branch's
+// pull request; a command run in another namespace (`nsenter -t 1234 -p …`, `unshare -n …`) leaves pid/port/process
+// values ambiguous; a package's version constraint is kept; the GPU LM trainer processes a partial batch.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { analyzeCommand, isAmbiguous } from '../src/history.js';
+
+const ROOT = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+
+test('major: an explicit pull request target is kept or withheld, never dropped', () => {
+  const cases = {
+    'merge pull request https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123': 'gh pr merge https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123',
+    'merge pull request feature/login': 'gh pr merge feature/login',
+    'merge pull request 123': 'gh pr merge 123',
+    'merge pr #45': 'gh pr merge 45',
+    'merge the pr for branch fix-1': 'gh pr merge fix-1',
+    'show checks of pull request https://github.com/o/r/pull/9': 'gh pr checks https://github.com/o/r/pull/9',
+    'view pull request 12': 'gh pr view 12',
+  };
+  for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(cases)) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+  assert.equal(run('merge pull request feature/login', null, { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' }).command, 'gh pr merge feature/login');
+  // a selector that is not a PR number, URL or branch: placeholder, not a bare `gh pr merge`
+  for (const q of ['merge pull request https://gitlab.com/x/y/-/merge_requests/3', 'merge pull request foo;rm', 'merge pull request ../x', 'merge pull request -rf']) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.equal(r.command, 'gh pr merge <PR>', q);
+    assert.deepEqual(r.missing, ['pr'], q);
+  }
+  // no selector named: the current branch's pull request
+  for (const q of ['merge the pull request', 'merge pr now']) assert.equal(run(q).command, 'gh pr merge', q);
+  // v0.3: "and delete the branch" is kept as --delete-branch
+  assert.equal(run('merge the pull request and delete the branch').command, 'gh pr merge --delete-branch');
+  assert.equal(run('view run 123456').command, 'gh run view 123456');
+});
+
+test('major: values a command saw in another namespace stay ambiguous', () => {
+  for (const h of ['nsenter -t 1234 -p ps -p 42', 'nsenter --target 1234 --pid ps -p 42', 'nsenter --target=1234 --pid -- ps -p 42',
+    'sudo nsenter -t 1234 -p ps -p 42', 'unshare -p -f ps -p 42', 'sudo -E nsenter -t 1 -p kill -0 42']) {
+    const r = run('kill it', [h]);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.ok(r.command.includes('<PID>'), `${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    const a = analyzeCommand(h);
+    assert.ok(a.ents.pid == null || isAmbiguous(a.ents.pid), `${h}: ${JSON.stringify(a.ents)}`);
+  }
+  for (const h of ['nsenter -t 1234 -n lsof -i :8080', 'nsenter -a -t 1 lsof -i :8080', 'nsenter --net=/run/netns/blue lsof -i :8080',
+    'nsenter -t 1234 -n -- lsof -i :8080', 'unshare -n lsof -i :8080']) {
+    for (const q of ['kill it', 'what is using that port']) {
+      const r = run(q, [h]);
+      assert.ok(r.command == null || !r.command.includes('8080'), `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    }
+    const a = analyzeCommand(h);
+    assert.ok(a.ents.port == null || isAmbiguous(a.ents.port), `${h}: ${JSON.stringify(a.ents)}`);
+  }
+  // the same commands in the caller's namespaces still resolve
+  assert.equal(run('kill it', ['ps -p 42']).command, 'kill 42');
+  assert.equal(run('kill it', ['sudo ps -p 42']).command, 'kill 42');
+});
+
+test('minor: a package version constraint is kept (or withheld), never dropped', () => {
+  const cases = {
+    'install requests==2.32.0 with pip': 'python3 -m pip install requests==2.32.0',
+    'pip install requests==2.32.0': 'python3 -m pip install requests==2.32.0',
+    'install requests>=2 with pip': "python3 -m pip install 'requests>=2'",
+    'install django>=4,<5 with pip': "python3 -m pip install 'django>=4,<5'",
+    'install requests[socks]==2.32.0 with pip': "python3 -m pip install 'requests[socks]==2.32.0'",
+    'install typescript@^5.4 with npm': "npm install 'typescript@^5.4'",
+    'install requests with pip': 'python3 -m pip install requests',
+  };
+  for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(cases)) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+  const r = run('install requests==2.32.0;rm with pip');
+  assert.equal(r.command, 'python3 -m pip install <PKG>');
+});
+
+test('minor: the GPU LM trainer runs the partial batch (fewer rows than --bs never loops forever)', () => {
+  const src = readFileSync(join(ROOT, 'scripts/hybrid/train_lm_gpu.py'), 'utf8');
+  assert.ok(src.includes('for i in range(0, len(train), a.bs):'));
+  assert.ok(!src.includes('len(train) - a.bs + 1'));
+  assert.ok(src.includes('if not train:'));
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions15.test.js b/test/regressions15.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..00cfc9d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions15.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+// Regression tests for round 14: the round-13 findings (review/r13-codex.md, review/r13-claude.md). A quoted pull
+// request target is kept (or withheld as <PR>), never dropped for a bare `gh pr merge`; a describing word after "pr"
+// is not a target, an unmarked bare word is withheld; values a command saw on another machine / host
+// (`systemd-run --machine=…`, `run0 --machine=…`) stay ambiguous; pip extras without a version are accepted.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { analyzeCommand, isAmbiguous } from '../src/history.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' }, { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' }];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+
+test('major: a quoted pull request target is kept or withheld, never dropped', () => {
+  const cases = {
+    'merge pull request "feature/login"': 'gh pr merge feature/login',
+    "merge pull request 'feature/login'": 'gh pr merge feature/login',
+    'merge pull request "feature/login" now': 'gh pr merge feature/login',
+    'merge pr "123"': 'gh pr merge 123',
+    'view pull request "https://github.com/o/r/pull/9"': 'gh pr view https://github.com/o/r/pull/9',
+    'merge the "feature/login" pull request': 'gh pr merge feature/login',
+  };
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(cases)) {
+      const r = run(q, null, env);
+      assert.equal(r.command, cmd, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+      assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    // a quoted value that is not a PR number, URL or branch: placeholder
+    for (const q of ['merge pull request "foo bar"', 'merge pull request "x;rm -rf /"', 'merge pull request ""']) {
+      const r = run(q, null, env);
+      assert.equal(r.command, 'gh pr merge <PR>', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+      assert.deepEqual(r.missing, ['pr'], `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: a describing word after "pr" is not a target; a bare unmarked word is withheld', () => {
+  const plain = {
+    'check pr status': 'gh pr checks', 'show pr status': 'gh pr checks', 'view pull request on github': 'gh pr view',
+    'merge PR by bob': 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'merge pull request quickly': 'gh pr merge', 'merge pull request for me': 'gh pr merge',
+    'merge pr now': 'gh pr merge', 'merge the pull request': 'gh pr merge',
+  };
+  for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(plain)) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+  const kept = {
+    'merge pull request from bob': 'gh pr merge bob', 'merge pull request for branch bob': 'gh pr merge bob',
+    'merge pr fix-1': 'gh pr merge fix-1', 'merge pull request feature/login': 'gh pr merge feature/login', 'merge pr #45': 'gh pr merge 45',
+  };
+  for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(kept)) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+  const r = run('merge pr main');
+  assert.equal(r.command, 'gh pr merge <PR>');
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, ['pr']);
+});
+
+test('major: values a command saw on another machine / host stay ambiguous', () => {
+  for (const h of ['systemd-run --machine=web ps -p 42', 'systemd-run --machine web ps -p 42', 'systemd-run -H user@host ps -p 42',
+    'systemd-run --host=user@host ps -p 42', 'run0 --machine=web ps -p 42', 'sudo systemd-run --machine=web ps -p 42',
+    'sudo --host=web ps -p 42', 'machinectl shell web ps -p 42', 'systemd-run -M web ps -p 42']) {
+    const r = run('kill it', [h]);
+    assert.ok(!/\b42\b/.test(r.command), `${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    const a = analyzeCommand(h);
+    assert.ok(a.ents.pid == null || isAmbiguous(a.ents.pid), `${h}: ${JSON.stringify(a.ents)}`);
+  }
+  for (const h of ['systemd-run --machine=web lsof -i :8080', 'run0 --machine=web lsof -i :8080', 'systemd-run -H web lsof -i :8080']) {
+    for (const q of ['kill it', 'what is using that port']) {
+      const r = run(q, [h]);
+      assert.ok(r.command == null || !r.command.includes('8080'), `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    }
+  }
+  // the same wrappers on this machine still resolve
+  for (const h of ['systemd-run ps -p 42', 'run0 ps -p 42', 'systemd-run --user ps -p 42', 'sudo -H ps -p 42']) {
+    assert.equal(run('kill it', [h]).command, 'kill 42', h);
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: pip extras without a version are accepted (and still validated)', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('install requests[socks] with pip').command, "python3 -m pip install 'requests[socks]'");
+  assert.equal(run('pip install uvicorn[standard]').command, "python3 -m pip install 'uvicorn[standard]'");
+  assert.equal(run('install requests[socks,security] with pip').command, "python3 -m pip install 'requests[socks,security]'");
+  assert.equal(run('install requests[a;rm] with pip').command, 'python3 -m pip install <PKG>');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions16.test.js b/test/regressions16.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..480a152
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions16.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+// Regression tests for round 15: the round-14 findings (review/r14-claude.md, review/r14-codex.md). An explicit pull
+// request selector (`feature/apply`, `hotfix/weekly`, `#12-only`, `from feature-only`) is kept, never dropped by the
+// describing-word list; a describing word after "branch" is withheld; a quoted target ends at its matching quote;
+// values a command saw under `systemd-run -p WorkingDirectory=…` / `-p RootDirectory=…` stay ambiguous.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' }, { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' }];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+
+test('major: an explicit branch selector ending in a describing word is kept', () => {
+  const kept = {
+    'merge pr feature/apply': 'gh pr merge feature/apply', 'merge pull request fix-reply': 'gh pr merge fix-reply',
+    'merge pr hotfix/weekly': 'gh pr merge hotfix/weekly', 'merge pull request release/monthly': 'gh pr merge release/monthly',
+    'view pr fix/assembly': 'gh pr view fix/assembly', 'merge pr #12-only': 'gh pr merge 12-only',
+    'merge pull request from feature-only': 'gh pr merge feature-only', 'merge pr from nightly': 'gh pr merge nightly',
+  };
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(kept)) {
+      const r = run(q, null, env);
+      assert.equal(r.command, cmd, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+      assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    // named but unclear: withheld, never a bare `gh pr merge`
+    for (const q of ['merge pull request for branch status', 'merge pr nightly', 'merge pull request "bob\'s fix"', "merge pr 'it''s'"]) {
+      const r = run(q, null, env);
+      assert.equal(r.command, 'gh pr merge <PR>', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+      assert.deepEqual(r.missing, ['pr'], `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: a quoted target ends at its matching quote; time / review words are not targets', () => {
+  // the apostrophe no longer cuts the value ("bob"): the whole value fails validation and is withheld
+  for (const q of ['merge pull request "bob\'s-fix"', 'merge pull request "don\'t-merge-yet"']) {
+    assert.equal(run(q).command, 'gh pr merge <PR>', q);
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('merge pull request “feature/x”').command, 'gh pr merge feature/x');
+  for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries({ 'view pr from yesterday': 'gh pr view <PR>', 'merge pr for review': 'gh pr merge',
+    'merge pr from fork': 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'merge pull request quickly': 'gh pr merge' })) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+});
+
+test('major: systemd-run unit properties that move the filesystem keep history paths ambiguous', () => {
+  for (const h of ['systemd-run -p WorkingDirectory=/srv cat notes.txt', 'systemd-run --property=WorkingDirectory=/srv cat notes.txt',
+    'systemd-run --property WorkingDirectory=/srv cat notes.txt', 'systemd-run -pWorkingDirectory=/srv cat notes.txt',
+    'systemd-run -p RootDirectory=/srv cat /etc/example.conf', 'systemd-run --property=RootDirectory=/srv cat /etc/example.conf',
+    'sudo systemd-run -p BindPaths=/a:/etc cat /etc/example.conf', 'run0 --property=RootDirectory=/srv cat /etc/example.conf']) {
+    const r = run('delete it', [h]);
+    assert.equal(r.command, 'rm <FILE>', h);
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('kill it', ['systemd-run -p PrivatePIDs=yes ps -p 42']).command, 'kill <PID>');
+  // other properties, and an absolute path under another working directory, still resolve
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['systemd-run -p Nice=5 cat notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['systemd-run -p WorkingDirectory=/srv cat /etc/example.conf']).command, 'rm /etc/example.conf');
+  assert.equal(run('kill it', ['systemd-run -p Nice=5 ps -p 42']).command, 'kill 42');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions17.test.js b/test/regressions17.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e07ee06
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions17.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+// Regression tests for round 16: the round-15 findings (review/r15-claude.md, review/r15-codex.md). A number elsewhere
+// in the request is never the pull request to merge (only `pr 45`, `pr #45`, `pr number 45`, `#45`); a request that names
+// a pull request the parser cannot read (`bob's`, `in repo v2`) is withheld as `<PR>`, never a bare `gh pr merge`; an
+// optional operand withheld by history replay keeps its placeholder; clustered / root-changing systemd-run properties.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' }, { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' }];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const withheld = (r, cmd, slot, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [slot], msg);
+};
+
+test('major: a number that is not next to "pr" is never the pull request', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['merge pr with 2 approvals', 'merge my pr from 2 days ago', 'merge the pr in 2 minutes', 'merge the 2 open prs',
+      'merge pr with squash and delete 1 branch']) withheld(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries({ 'merge pr 45': 'gh pr merge 45', 'merge pr #45': 'gh pr merge 45',
+      'merge pr number 45': 'gh pr merge 45', 'merge #45': 'gh pr merge 45', 'merge pull request 45': 'gh pr merge 45',
+      'merge pr no. 7': 'gh pr merge 7', 'merge pull request #12 now': 'gh pr merge 12', 'show checks for pr 12': 'gh pr checks 12' })) {
+      const r = run(q, null, env);
+      assert.equal(r.command, cmd, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+      assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+  }
+  withheld(run('view pr for 3 days'), 'gh pr view <PR>', 'pr');
+});
+
+test('major: a named pull request that does not parse is withheld, never a bare merge', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ["merge pr feature/x's", "merge pr it's-fix", "merge pr bob's", 'merge pr bob’s']) {
+      withheld(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    // (round 18: the unreadable repository is withheld as well)
+    const r = run('merge pr in repo v2', null, env);
+    assert.equal(r.command, 'gh pr merge <PR> --repo <REPO>', env.shell);
+    assert.deepEqual(r.missing.sort(), ['pr', 'repo'], env.shell);
+  }
+  // nothing named: the current branch's pull request, as before
+  for (const q of ['merge pr', 'merge the pr', 'merge pr now', 'merge pr for review']) assert.equal(run(q).command, 'gh pr merge', q);
+});
+
+test('major: history replay keeps the placeholder of an optional operand it withholds', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    const r = run('same but merge', ['tellsh merge pr nightly'], env);
+    withheld(r, 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', env.shell);
+    assert.equal(r.understood, true);
+  }
+  withheld(run('same for foo/bar', ['npm install lodash']), 'npm install <PKG>', 'pkg');
+  // a valid value still replays
+  assert.equal(run('same but merge', ['tellsh merge pr 45']).command, 'gh pr merge 45');
+  assert.equal(run('same for express', ['npm install lodash']).command, 'npm install express');
+});
+
+test('minor: abbreviations, hosts and issues are not pull request selectors', () => {
+  for (const q of ['merge pr e.g. main', 'merge pr w/o checks', 'merge pr on github.com']) withheld(run(q), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', q);
+  // (round 18: closing a pull request is not supported: refused, never `gh pr view`)
+  assert.equal(run('close pr for issue 45').understood, false);
+});
+
+test('minor: clustered -p and more root-changing systemd-run properties keep history paths ambiguous', () => {
+  for (const h of ['systemd-run -tp WorkingDirectory=/srv cat notes.txt', 'systemd-run -tpWorkingDirectory=/srv cat notes.txt',
+    'systemd-run -p ProtectHome=tmpfs cat /home/u/a.txt', 'systemd-run -p PrivateDevices=yes cat /etc/example.conf',
+    'systemd-run -p PrivateIPC=yes cat /etc/example.conf']) assert.equal(run('delete it', [h]).command, 'rm <FILE>', h);
+  for (const [h, cmd] of Object.entries({ 'systemd-run -t cat notes.txt': 'rm notes.txt',
+    'systemd-run -p ProtectHome=read-only cat /home/u/a.txt': 'rm /home/u/a.txt' })) assert.equal(run('delete it', [h]).command, cmd, h);
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions18.test.js b/test/regressions18.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ab5b8ef
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions18.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+// Regression tests for round 17: the round-16 findings (review/r16-claude.md, review/r16-codex.md). An issue, ticket or
+// bug number is never the pull request to merge, and `#45` alone names it only right after the verb; "merge that pr"
+// reads the pull request of a previous `gh pr view/checkout N` or is withheld, never the current branch's; a branch
+// named as "from the branch main" is read, an unreadable one withheld.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' }, { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' }];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const withheld = (r, cmd, slot, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [slot], msg);
+};
+const exact = (r, cmd, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], msg);
+};
+
+test('major: an issue number or a #N in another clause is never the pull request', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['merge pr for issue #45', 'squash merge the pr for issue #8', 'merge the pr in issue #4', 'merge the pr that closes #12',
+      'merge pr which fixes #12', 'merge the pr, see #99', 'merge the pull request for ticket #3', 'merge pr for bug #3',
+      'merge the pr for #12', 'merge pr for fix #12', 'merge pr for issue 45']) withheld(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries({ 'merge #45': 'gh pr merge 45', 'squash merge #45': 'gh pr merge 45', 'please merge #45': 'gh pr merge 45',
+      'merge pr #45': 'gh pr merge 45', 'merge pull request #12 now': 'gh pr merge 12', 'merge #45 for issue #3': 'gh pr merge 45',
+      'merge pr number 45': 'gh pr merge 45' })) exact(run(q, null, env), cmd, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: "merge that pr" uses the pull request of the previous gh pr command or is withheld', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge 45', env.shell);
+    exact(run('merge this pull request', ['gh pr checkout 45'], env), 'gh pr merge 45', env.shell);
+    exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view feature/x'], env), 'gh pr merge feature/x', env.shell);
+    for (const h of [['git checkout feat'], ['cat a.txt'], ['ls'], ['gh pr list'], ['gh pr view'], ['gh pr view 12 --repo a/b'], ['gh pr view 1 2'], null]) {
+      for (const q of ['merge that pr', 'merge this pull request']) withheld(run(q, h, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+    }
+  }
+  exact(run('show checks for that pr', ['gh pr view 45']), 'gh pr checks 45');
+  // nothing referred to: the current branch's pull request, as before
+  for (const q of ['merge pr', 'merge the pr']) exact(run(q, ['gh pr view 45']), 'gh pr merge', q);
+  // a pull request in history does not change what the model sees
+  assert.equal(run('git status', ['gh pr view 45']).command, 'git status');
+});
+
+test('major: a branch named as "from the branch X" is read, an unreadable one is withheld', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries({ 'merge pr from the branch main': 'gh pr merge main', 'merge pr for the branch develop': 'gh pr merge develop',
+      'merge the pull request from the branch release': 'gh pr merge release', 'merge pr from my branch foo': 'gh pr merge foo',
+      'merge pr from branch main': 'gh pr merge main' })) exact(run(q, null, env), cmd, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    for (const q of ['merge pr from the feature branch', 'merge pr from the branch']) withheld(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+  }
+  exact(run('merge pr and delete the branch'), 'gh pr merge --delete-branch');
+});
+
+test('minor: an amount after "pr" and a zero or zero-padded number are not pull requests', () => {
+  for (const q of ['merge pr 2 days old', 'merge pr 3 times', 'merge pr 0', 'merge pr 007']) withheld(run(q), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', q);
+  exact(run('merge pr 12'), 'gh pr merge 12');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions19.test.js b/test/regressions19.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8dad85a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions19.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+// Regression tests for round 18: the round-17 findings (review/r17-claude.md, review/r17-codex.md). A pull request (or
+// branch) read from history is ambiguous after a trailing cd/pushd/popd or under GH_REPO/GH_HOST; "the other pr", "the
+// latest pr", "my last pr" never become the current branch's pull request; a repository the request names is kept as
+// `--repo` or withheld, never dropped; "close that pr" is refused instead of `gh pr create`.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' }, { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' }];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const withheld = (r, cmd, slots, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual([...r.missing].sort(), [slots].flat().sort(), msg);
+};
+const exact = (r, cmd, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], msg);
+};
+
+test('major: a cd after `gh pr view N` makes the pull request ambiguous (another repository)', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const h of ['gh pr view 7 && cd ../other', 'gh pr view 7 && cd /', 'gh pr view 7; popd', 'gh pr checkout 7; pushd /srv/x',
+      'gh pr view feature/x && cd ~/other']) {
+      for (const q of ['merge that pr', 'merge this pull request']) withheld(run(q, [h], env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+    }
+    // a cd before the gh command: the pull request is one of the repository the user is in now
+    exact(run('merge that pr', ['cd ../other && gh pr view 7'], env), 'gh pr merge 7', env.shell);
+    exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view 7'], env), 'gh pr merge 7', env.shell);
+  }
+  // a branch is repository-scoped as well
+  for (const h of ['git checkout -b feat && cd ../other', 'git merge feat; cd /']) withheld(run('delete that branch', [h]), 'git branch -d <BRANCH>', 'branch', h);
+  exact(run('delete that branch', ['git merge feat']), 'git branch -d feat');
+});
+
+test('major: GH_REPO / GH_HOST scope the pull request of the previous command', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const h of ['GH_REPO=other/repo gh pr view 45', 'env GH_REPO=other/repo gh pr view 45', 'GH_HOST=ghe.example.com gh pr view 45',
+      'export GH_REPO=other/repo; gh pr view 45', 'export GH_REPO=other/repo && gh pr checkout 45']) {
+      withheld(run('merge that pr', [h], env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${h}`);
+    }
+  }
+  // other variables do not scope gh
+  exact(run('merge that pr', ['FOO=1 gh pr view 45']), 'gh pr merge 45');
+});
+
+test('major: a pull request picked out among several is never the current branch\'s', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['merge the other pr', 'merge the latest pr', 'merge the newest pr', 'merge the most recent pr', 'merge my last pr',
+      'merge another pr', 'merge the other pull request', 'merge our previous pr', 'merge the latest open pr', 'merge the first pr',
+      'view the newest pr']) {
+      const r = run(q, null, env);
+      assert.match(r.command, /^gh pr (?:merge|view) <PR>$/, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+      assert.deepEqual(r.missing, ['pr'], `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    // also with a pull request in history: "the other pr" is not that one, "my last pr" is not the one viewed
+    for (const q of ['merge the other pr', 'merge my last pr', 'merge the latest pr']) withheld(run(q, ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+  }
+  // a named pull request wins; nothing named is still the current branch's
+  exact(run('merge pr 45, the latest one'), 'gh pr merge 45');
+  for (const q of ['merge the pr', 'merge pr', 'merge the current pr', 'first merge the pr']) exact(run(q), 'gh pr merge', q);
+});
+
+test('major: a repository the request names is kept as --repo or withheld, never dropped', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    const cases = {
+      'merge pr 45 in repository other/repo': 'gh pr merge 45 --repo other/repo',
+      'merge pr 45 --repo other/repo': 'gh pr merge 45 --repo other/repo',
+      'merge pr 45 --repo=other/repo': 'gh pr merge 45 --repo other/repo',
+      'merge pr 45 -R other/repo': 'gh pr merge 45 --repo other/repo',
+      'merge pr 45 in repo other/repo': 'gh pr merge 45 --repo other/repo',
+      'merge pr 45 in the other/repo repository': 'gh pr merge 45 --repo other/repo',
+      'merge pr #12 in repo acme/web': 'gh pr merge 12 --repo acme/web',
+      'view pr 45 in repo a/b': 'gh pr view 45 --repo a/b',
+    };
+    for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(cases)) exact(run(q, null, env), cmd, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    // a repository that cannot be read: placeholder
+    for (const q of ['merge pr 45 in another repo', 'merge pr 45 in the other repository', 'merge pr 45 in repo v2', 'merge pr 45 --repo',
+      'merge pr 45 in repo "a/b;rm"']) withheld(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge 45 --repo <REPO>', 'repo', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    // gh needs the pull request named together with --repo
+    withheld(run('merge pr --repo other/repo', null, env), 'gh pr merge <PR> --repo other/repo', 'pr', env.shell);
+    withheld(run('merge the pr in repo other/repo', null, env), 'gh pr merge <PR> --repo other/repo', 'pr', env.shell);
+    // "that pr" was one of this repository's: not the pull request of another one
+    withheld(run('merge that pr in repo a/b', ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge <PR> --repo a/b', 'pr', env.shell);
+  }
+  // the working directory's repository is no qualifier
+  for (const q of ['merge pr 45 in this repo', 'merge pr 45 in the current repository', 'merge pr 45']) exact(run(q), 'gh pr merge 45', q);
+  // a lowercase -r is not gh's -R
+  withheld(run('merge pull request -rf'), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr');
+});
+
+test('minor: closing a pull request is refused, never `gh pr create` or `gh pr view`', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['close that pr', 'close the pr', 'close pr 45', 'close pull request 45', 'zamknij ten pr']) {
+      const r = run(q, null, env);
+      assert.equal(r.understood, false, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+      assert.ok(!r.command, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    assert.equal(run('close that pr', ['gh pr view 45'], env).command ?? null, null, env.shell);
+  }
+  for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries({ 'create a pr': 'gh pr create --fill', 'show closed prs': 'gh pr list <ARGS>', 'view pr 45': 'gh pr view 45' })) {
+    assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: switches of gh pr subcommands are not read as taking a value', () => {
+  for (const h of ['gh pr view -c 7', 'gh pr review -a 7', 'gh pr review -c 7', 'gh pr comment -e 7']) exact(run('merge that pr', [h]), 'gh pr merge 7', h);
+  withheld(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr checkout -b local 7 --repo a/b']), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions2.test.js b/test/regressions2.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ff0ac63
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions2.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,326 @@
+// Regression tests for the round-1 review findings (review/r1-claude.md, review/r1-codex.md):
+// path truncation, history references, composer/PowerShell/cmd quoting, danger checker gaps, CLI
+// argument validation, model loading, and the whole-disk location phrases.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { mkdtempSync, writeFileSync, readFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+import { suggest, validSlot } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { extractSlots, trimPathPunct } from '../src/slots.js';
+import { normPath, exFromSpans, tagFeatureSets } from '../src/tagger.js';
+import { tagTokens, tagFeatures } from '../src/features.js';
+// the parser on its own (it only raises risk); the trust rule (a non-catalog command is high) is in regressions27.test.js
+import { assessCommand as checkDanger } from '../src/danger.js';
+import { buildCommand, finalizeSlots } from '../src/fill.js';
+import { BY_ID } from '../src/catalog.js';
+import { shQuote, psQuote, cmdQuote, pwshNativeSlots } from '../src/render.js';
+import { shellInvocation } from '../src/cli.js';
+import { splitCommand, isAmbiguous } from '../src/shellwords.js';
+import { buildContext } from '../src/history.js';
+import { parseModel, getModel, DEFAULT_MODEL } from '../src/model.js';
+
+const BIN = fileURLToPath(new URL('../bin/tellsh.js', import.meta.url));
+const cli = (args, opts = {}) => spawnSync(process.execPath, [BIN, ...args], { encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, NO_COLOR: '1' }, ...opts });
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PS_WIN = { shell: 'powershell', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const CMD = { shell: 'cmd', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PS_LINUX = { shell: 'powershell', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, history });
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// r1-claude blocker 1 / codex 4: paths were cut back to a parent directory
+
+test('paths with ( , ; : keep every character (no parent directory is deleted)', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('delete folder ~/Downloads/backup(2)').command, "rm -r ~/'Downloads/backup(2)'");
+  assert.equal(run('delete the folder /home/me/photos,2019').command, 'rm -r /home/me/photos,2019');
+  assert.equal(run('remove directory /var/www/site;old').command, "rm -r '/var/www/site;old'");
+  assert.equal(run('delete file /srv/a:b.txt').command, 'rm /srv/a:b.txt');
+});
+
+test('trailing dots are not stripped from a path (only one sentence dot after an extension)', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('delete folder ~/old...').command, 'rm -r ~/old...');
+  assert.equal(run('delete file /tmp/data.').command, 'rm /tmp/data.');
+  const up = run('delete directory /tmp/cache/..');
+  assert.equal(up.command, 'rm -r /tmp/cache/..');
+  assert.ok(up.warnings.some((w) => /\.\./.test(w)));
+  // destructive: `/tmp/a.txt.` may be the name or a sentence dot -> placeholder (test/regressions3.test.js)
+  assert.equal(run('delete file /tmp/a.txt.').command, 'rm <FILE>');
+  assert.equal(run('show file /tmp/a.txt.').command, 'cat /tmp/a.txt');
+  assert.equal(trimPathPunct('/tmp/x),'), '/tmp/x');
+  assert.equal(trimPathPunct('backup(2)'), 'backup(2)');
+  assert.deepEqual(extractSlots('copy /a/b, /c/d').paths, ['/a/b', '/c/d']);
+});
+
+test('tagger span normalisation never accepts a shorter path than the span', () => {
+  // a span the tokenizer cut at `(` / `)` / `.` is widened back to the whole word
+  const text = 'delete folder ~/Downloads/backup(2) now';
+  const at = text.indexOf('~');
+  for (const end of [at + 20, text.indexOf('(') + 2, text.indexOf('Downloads') + 9]) {
+    const start = end === text.indexOf('Downloads') + 9 ? text.indexOf('Downloads') : at;
+    assert.deepEqual(exFromSpans(text, [{ type: 'PATH', start, end, text: text.slice(start, end) }]).paths, ['~/Downloads/backup(2)']);
+  }
+  const t2 = 'delete directory /tmp/cache/..';
+  assert.deepEqual(exFromSpans(t2, [{ type: 'PATH', start: 17, end: 27, text: t2.slice(17, 27) }]).paths, ['/tmp/cache/..']);
+  assert.equal(normPath('~/Downloads/backup(2)'), '~/Downloads/backup(2)');
+  assert.equal(normPath('/srv/a:b.txt'), '/srv/a:b.txt');
+  assert.equal(normPath('Pobrane'), '~/Downloads');
+});
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// feature: whole-disk phrases -> filesystem root
+
+test('whole-disk phrases map to / (C:\\ on Windows shells)', () => {
+  for (const q of ['największe pliki na całym dysku', 'najwieksze pliki na calym dysku', 'największe pliki na dysku', 'największe pliki całego dysku',
+    'largest files on disk', 'largest files on the disk', 'largest files on the whole drive', 'largest files on the entire disk', 'biggest files in the whole system']) {
+    assert.match(run(q).command, /^find \/ -xdev -type f /, q);
+  }
+  assert.match(run('największe pliki na całym dysku', null, PS_WIN).command, /-LiteralPath 'C:\\' /);
+  assert.deepEqual(extractSlots('na calym dysku').paths, ['/']);
+  assert.deepEqual(extractSlots('on the disk').paths, ['/']);
+});
+
+test('deleting on the whole disk is flagged critical', () => {
+  const r = run('delete all log files on disk');
+  assert.match(r.command, /^find \/ /);
+  assert.equal(r.critical, true);
+  const p = run('delete all log files on disk', null, PS_WIN);
+  assert.match(p.command, /'C:\\'.*Remove-Item/);
+  assert.equal(p.critical, true);
+});
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// r1-claude minor 3: danger checker gaps
+
+test('danger: busybox, rsync --delete, /dev/null copies, root bind mounts, chmod -R ~, tar -C /', () => {
+  for (const c of ['busybox rm -rf /', 'rsync -a --delete empty/ /', 'cp /dev/null /etc/passwd', 'docker run -v /:/h alpine rm -rf /h',
+    'chmod -R -v 777 ~', 'tar -x -C / -f a.tar', 'tar -xf a.tar --directory=/', 'find / -name "*.log" -delete', 'find / -type f | xargs rm',
+    "Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath 'C:\\' -Recurse | Remove-Item"]) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', c);
+    assert.equal(d.critical, true, c);
+  }
+  for (const c of ['find . -name "*.log" -delete', 'chmod -R 755 .', 'tar -xzf a.tgz -C ./out', 'rsync -a --delete src/ backup/', 'docker run -v /:/host:ro img']) {
+    assert.equal(checkDanger(c).critical, false, c);
+  }
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('find / -xdev -type f -exec du -h {} +').risk, 'safe');
+});
+
+test('danger: PowerShell typographic quotes do not hide a drive root', () => {
+  for (const c of ['Remove-Item -Recurse -Force ‘C:\\’', 'Remove-Item -Recurse -Force “C:\\”']) assert.equal(checkDanger(c).critical, true, c);
+});
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// history references (r1-claude major 5-9, minor 1/8; codex 1-3)
+
+test('history: a mv/cp destination directory is not "it"', () => {
+  const r = run('delete it', ['mv notes.txt ~/Documents/']);
+  assert.ok(!/Documents/.test(r.command), r.command);
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused');
+  const p = run('delete it', ['Move-Item notes.txt -Destination C:\\Users\\me\\Documents'], PS_WIN);
+  assert.ok(!/Documents/.test(p.command), p.command);
+  // renaming a file: the new name is "it"
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['mv a.txt b.txt']).command, 'rm b.txt');
+});
+
+test('history: a requested type that is not in history is refused, and "gallery" is not a branch', () => {
+  const r = run('delete that branch', ['ls tmp_dir']);
+  assert.ok(!/tmp_dir/.test(r.command), r.command);
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused');
+  const g = run('delete that gallery folder', ['git checkout gallery', 'ls gallery']);
+  assert.ok(!/git branch/.test(g.command), g.command);
+});
+
+test('history: parsers pick the right word (kill -s, grep -v grep, pkill -u, checkout --)', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('kill that process', ['kill -s 9 4242']).command, 'kill 4242');
+  assert.equal(run('kill it', ['ps aux | grep -v grep | grep node']).command, 'pkill -f node');
+  assert.equal(run('kill it', ['pkill nginx -u bob']).command, 'pkill -f nginx');
+  const c = run('switch to that branch', ['git checkout -- app.js']);
+  assert.ok(!/app\.js/.test(c.command), c.command);
+  assert.equal(run('switch to that branch', ['git checkout -b feature/x origin/main']).command, 'git checkout feature/x');
+});
+
+test('history: later segments of a compound line win; redirect targets count', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat old.txt; cat new.txt']).command, 'rm new.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat old.txt && cat new.txt']).command, 'rm new.txt');
+  const amb = run('delete it', ['cat old.txt; cat $F']);
+  assert.ok(!/old\.txt/.test(amb.command), amb.command);
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['echo hi > out.txt']).command, 'rm out.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat a.txt > /dev/null']).command, 'rm a.txt');
+});
+
+test('history: no implicit fill of destructive commands, no fallback past an ambiguous value', () => {
+  const r = run('delete the folder', ['du -sh /var/lib/docker']);
+  assert.ok(!/docker/.test(r.command), r.command);
+  const f = run('delete file', ['cat old.txt', 'frobnicate new.txt']);
+  assert.ok(!/old\.txt/.test(f.command), f.command);
+  // safe intents may still be filled implicitly ...
+  assert.equal(run('count words', ['cat notes.txt']).command, 'wc -w notes.txt');
+  // ... but never from an older value when the newest one is ambiguous
+  const s = run('count words', ['cat notes.txt', 'frobnicate other.txt']);
+  assert.ok(!/notes\.txt/.test(s.command), s.command);
+});
+
+test('history: any history-derived slot marks the result as history (never --yes)', () => {
+  for (const [q, h] of [['show file contents', ['cat secret.txt']], ['count words', ['cat notes.txt']]]) {
+    const r = run(q, h);
+    assert.equal(r.method, 'history-rule', q);
+    assert.ok(Object.values(r.slotSources).includes('history'));
+  }
+  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'tellsh-r2-'));
+  try {
+    const hf = join(dir, 'bash_history');
+    writeFileSync(hf, 'cat secret.txt\n');
+    const out = cli(['--yes', `--history=${hf}`, '--shell', 'bash', '--os', 'linux', 'show', 'file', 'contents'], { cwd: dir });
+    assert.equal(out.status, 4, out.stdout + out.stderr);
+    assert.match(out.stdout, /Not running/);
+  } finally { rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
+});
+
+test('history: relative paths from before a cd are not reused', () => {
+  const r = run('delete it', ['cat notes.txt', 'cd /tmp', 'true']);
+  assert.ok(!/notes\.txt/.test(r.command), r.command);
+  const rel = run('show it', ['cat notes.txt', 'cd sub']);
+  assert.ok(!/notes\.txt|sub/.test(rel.command), rel.command);
+  // absolute paths survive a cd (in the same line; an older line is never a reference target)
+  assert.equal(run('show that file', ['cat /etc/hosts; cd sub']).command, 'cat /etc/hosts');
+  assert.ok(!/hosts/.test(run('show that file', ['cat /etc/hosts', 'cd sub', 'true']).command ?? ''));
+  // same line: `cat a.txt; cd y` makes a.txt stale
+  const same = run('show it', ['cat a.txt; cd y']);
+  assert.ok(!/a\.txt/.test(same.command), same.command);
+});
+
+test('history: the running tellsh call is not the previous command', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('same for /var', ['du -sh /home', 'tellsh --history same for /var']).command, 'du -sh /var');
+  assert.equal(run('same for /var', ['du -sh /home', "tellsh --history 'same for /var'"]).command, 'du -sh /var');
+  assert.equal(run('same for /var', ['du -sh /home', 'node bin/tellsh.js same for /var']).command, 'du -sh /var');
+});
+
+test('history: "same for" does not take pronouns or filler words as values', () => {
+  for (const q of ['what about this', 'and with force', 'what about it']) {
+    const r = run(q, ['rm -r olddir']);
+    assert.notEqual(r.context.rule, 'same-for', q);
+    assert.ok(!r.command || !/\b(this|force|it)\b/.test(r.command), `${q}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('same for build', ['rm -r olddir']).command, 'rm -r build');
+});
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// quoting per shell (r1-claude major 3/4, minor 5/6/7/9)
+
+test('composer is never offered to fish (its single quotes treat \\ as an escape)', () => {
+  const q = 'pokaż pliki w a\\ szczegółowo posortowane po rozmiarze';
+  for (const compose of ['auto', 'force']) {
+    const r = suggest(q, { env: { shell: 'fish', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' }, compose });
+    assert.notEqual(r.method, 'composed', compose);
+  }
+});
+
+test('PowerShell: values with " are refused for native programs, not for cmdlets', () => {
+  const r = buildCommand('git_commit', '', { env: PS_WIN, resolved: { message: 'a" --amend "b' } });
+  assert.equal(r.command, null);
+  assert.match(r.gap, /PowerShell < 7\.3/);
+  for (const [id, s] of [['extract_targz', { file: 'a".tar.gz' }], ['download_file', { url: 'https://x.org/"a' }], ['git_switch_branch', { branch: 'x"y' }]]) {
+    assert.equal(buildCommand(id, '', { env: PS_WIN, resolved: s }).command, null, id);
+  }
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('git_commit', '', { env: PS_WIN, resolved: { message: 'fix it' } }).command, "git add -A; if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { git commit -m 'fix it' }");
+  // cmdlets receive the single-quoted literal unchanged
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('cat_file', '', { env: PS_WIN, resolved: { file: 'a"b.txt' } }).command, "Get-Content -LiteralPath 'a\"b.txt'");
+  assert.deepEqual([...pwshNativeSlots('git add -A; if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { git commit -m {message} }')], ['message']);
+  assert.deepEqual([...pwshNativeSlots("(Get-Content -LiteralPath {file} -Raw).Replace({old}, {new})")], []);
+});
+
+test('cmd: values starting with / are refused (switches); /s /c gets wrapping quotes', () => {
+  const r = suggest('delete directory /q', { env: CMD });
+  assert.equal(r.command, null);
+  assert.match(r.gap, /switch/);
+  assert.throws(() => cmdQuote('/q'), /switch/);
+  assert.deepEqual(shellInvocation('"C:\\Program Files\\x.exe" "a b"', 'cmd'), ['cmd.exe', ['/d', '/s', '/c', '""C:\\Program Files\\x.exe" "a b""']]);
+});
+
+test('function templates: only path values get ./, other values starting with - become placeholders', () => {
+  const b = buildCommand('base64_encode', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { text: '-n hello' } });
+  assert.ok(!/\.\/-n/.test(b.command), b.command);
+  assert.ok(b.missing.includes('text'));
+  const f = buildCommand('grep_text', '', { env: CMD, resolved: { pattern: '-x', path: 'src' } });
+  assert.ok(!/\.\/-x/.test(f.command || ''), f.command);
+  const k = buildCommand('kill_by_name', '', { env: CMD, resolved: { name: '-f' } });
+  assert.ok(!/\.\/-f/.test(k.command || ''), k.command);
+  // a path still gets ./
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('base64_encode', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { file: '-x.txt' } }).command, 'base64 ./-x.txt');
+});
+
+test('tilde expansion only for path slots', () => {
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('git_commit', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { message: '~' } }).command, "git add -A && git commit -m '~'");
+  assert.match(buildCommand('grep_text', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { pattern: '~/x', path: '~/src' } }).command, /-- '~\/x' ~\/src/);
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('git_commit', '', { env: PS_LINUX, resolved: { message: '~' } }).command.includes("'~'"), true);
+  assert.match(buildCommand('replace_text', '', { env: PS_WIN, resolved: { file: 'a.txt', old: '~', new: 'x' } }).command, /\.Replace\('~', 'x'\)/);
+  assert.equal(shQuote('~/a b'), "~/'a b'");
+  assert.equal(shQuote('~', { tilde: false }), "'~'");
+  assert.equal(psQuote('~/x', { tilde: false }), "'~/x'");
+});
+
+test('"kill process named -9" is not kill 9; sed old text with a newline is escaped/refused', () => {
+  const r = run('kill process named -9');
+  assert.ok(!/\b9\b/.test(r.command), r.command);
+  const s = buildCommand('replace_text', '', { env: BASH, resolved: finalizeSlots(BY_ID.replace_text, { file: 'a.txt', old: 'a\nb', new: 'c' }) });
+  assert.ok(!s.command.includes('\n'), s.command);
+  assert.equal(validSlot('old', 'a\nb'), false);
+});
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// CLI / parsing / model robustness (r1-claude minor 2, 4, 11, 13)
+
+test('--threshold must be a number in [0, 1]', () => {
+  for (const v of ['foo', 'NaN', '2', '-1', '']) {
+    const r = cli(['--threshold', v, '--json', 'bake', 'me', 'a', 'cake']);
+    assert.equal(r.status, 2, v);
+    assert.match(r.stderr, /--threshold/);
+  }
+  assert.equal(cli(['--threshold=0.5', '--json', 'list', 'files']).status, 0);
+});
+
+test('shellwords: &> is a redirection, $(...) and backticks are one ambiguous word', () => {
+  const r = splitCommand('cat a.txt &> log.txt', 'posix', { keepRedirects: true });
+  assert.deepEqual(r.segments.map((s) => s.words), [['cat', 'a.txt', '&>', 'log.txt']]);
+  const d = splitCommand('echo $(cat a; ls) done', 'posix');
+  assert.equal(d.segments.length, 1);
+  assert.equal(d.segments[0].words.length, 3);
+  assert.ok(isAmbiguous(d.segments[0].words[1]));
+  const b = splitCommand('echo `cat a; ls` x', 'posix');
+  assert.equal(b.segments.length, 1);
+  assert.ok(isAmbiguous(b.segments[0].words[1]));
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['make &> build.log']).command, 'rm build.log');
+});
+
+test('history parsing does not backtrack exponentially on long \\ or quote runs', () => {
+  for (const [line, kind] of [['cat ' + '\\\\'.repeat(300) + ' ;', 'posix'], ['Get-Content -LiteralPath ' + "''".repeat(300) + ' ;', 'pwsh'], ['Get-Content -LiteralPath ' + '""'.repeat(300) + ' ;', 'pwsh']]) {
+    const t = Date.now();
+    buildContext([line], { kind });
+    assert.ok(Date.now() - t < 2000, `${kind}: ${Date.now() - t} ms`);
+  }
+});
+
+test('model.bin is validated: truncated or corrupt files give a clear error', () => {
+  const buf = readFileSync(DEFAULT_MODEL);
+  assert.ok(parseModel(buf).models.tagger);
+  assert.throws(() => parseModel(buf.subarray(0, 6)), /bad model file/);
+  assert.throws(() => parseModel(buf.subarray(0, buf.length - 1000)), /exceeds the file/);
+  const hdr = Buffer.from(buf);
+  hdr.writeUInt32LE(buf.length * 2, 4);
+  assert.throws(() => parseModel(hdr), /header length/);
+  const junk = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('TSH2'), Buffer.from([3, 0, 0, 0]), Buffer.from('{x}')]);
+  assert.throws(() => parseModel(junk), /not valid JSON/);
+});
+
+test('tagger features are deduplicated per token like training (set of indices)', () => {
+  const dim = getModel().tagDim;
+  for (const q of ['pokaż 10 największych plików w ~/Pobrane', 'kill nginx nginx', 'grep -rn foo foo /etc /etc']) {
+    const toks = tagTokens(q);
+    const raw = tagFeatures(toks, 'grep', dim);
+    const sets = tagFeatureSets(toks, 'grep', dim);
+    sets.forEach((f, i) => { assert.equal(new Set(f).size, f.length); assert.deepEqual([...new Set(raw[i])].sort(), [...f].sort()); });
+  }
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions20.test.js b/test/regressions20.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..5e30dc3
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions20.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+// Regression tests for round 19: the round-18 findings (review/r18-claude.md, review/r18-codex.md). "close pr 45 …" is
+// refused also when the classifier picks gh_pr_merge (and a negated merge is never `gh pr merge`); a repository named
+// without the word "repo" (`in org/repo`, `on github.com/org/repo`, `org/repo#7`) is kept as `--repo`; an export of
+// GH_REPO after `gh pr view N`, or a later `gh pr view` / `gh pr list`, makes N ambiguous; a refused reference keeps
+// `<PR>`; a pull request picked out by who or when ("by alice", "from yesterday") is withheld.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' }, { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' }];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const withheld = (r, cmd, slots, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual([...r.missing].sort(), [slots].flat().sort(), msg);
+};
+const exact = (r, cmd, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], msg);
+};
+const refused = (r, re, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.understood, false, msg);
+  assert.ok(!r.command, msg);
+  assert.match(r.hint, re, msg);
+};
+
+test('major: closing a pull request is refused also when the classifier picks gh_pr_merge', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['close pr 45 and delete branch', 'close pr 45 without merge', 'close pr 45, do not merge', 'close the pull request 45 without merging',
+      'decline and close pr 45 and delete the branch', 'close pr 45', 'close the pull request', 'cancel pr 45']) {
+      refused(run(q, null, env), /closing a pull request is not supported/, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    // a merge the request asks for
+    exact(run('merge and close pr 45', null, env), 'gh pr merge 45', env.shell);
+    exact(run('merge pr 45 and close the issue', null, env), 'gh pr merge 45', env.shell);
+  }
+  // a negated or undone merge is never `gh pr merge`
+  for (const q of ['do not merge pr 45', "don't merge pr 45", 'unmerge pr 45', 'undo the merge of pr 45']) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.ok(!r.command || !/^gh pr merge/.test(r.command), q);
+  }
+  refused(run('revert pr 45'), /reverting a pull request is not supported/);
+  exact(run('merge pr 45'), 'gh pr merge 45');
+  exact(run('squash merge pr 45'), 'gh pr merge 45');
+});
+
+test('major: a repository named as OWNER/REPO after a preposition is kept as --repo', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const [q, repo] of [['merge pr 7 in other/repo', 'other/repo'], ['merge pr 7 of org/repo', 'org/repo'], ['merge pr 7 from org/repo', 'org/repo'],
+      ['merge pr 7 to org/repo', 'org/repo'], ['merge pr 7 for org/repo', 'org/repo'], ['merge pull request 7 at org/repo', 'org/repo'],
+      ['merge pr 7 on github.com/org/repo', 'github.com/org/repo'], ['merge pr 7 on https://github.com/org/repo', 'github.com/org/repo'],
+      ['merge pr org/repo#7', 'org/repo']]) {
+      exact(run(q, null, env), `gh pr merge 7 --repo ${repo}`, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+  }
+  // right after "pr for" / "pr from": the branch of the pull request
+  exact(run('view the pr for feature/login'), 'gh pr view feature/login');
+  exact(run('merge pr from feature/x'), 'gh pr merge feature/x');
+});
+
+test('minor: a repository starting with "-" is withheld; "the repo", "my current repo" are the working directory\'s', () => {
+  for (const q of ['merge pr 45 --repo -x/y', 'merge pr 45 -R=-x/y', 'merge pr 45 in repository -o/x', 'merge pr 45 --repo x/-y']) {
+    withheld(run(q), 'gh pr merge 45 --repo <REPO>', 'repo', q);
+  }
+  exact(run('merge pr 45 for the repo'), 'gh pr merge 45');
+  const r = run('show checks of the pr in my current repo');
+  assert.ok(!/--repo/.test(r.command), r.command);
+});
+
+test('major: an export of GH_REPO / GH_HOST after `gh pr view N` makes N ambiguous', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const h of ['gh pr view 45; export GH_REPO=other/repo', 'gh pr view 45 && export GH_HOST=ghe.example.com', 'gh pr checkout 45; declare -x GH_REPO=a/b']) {
+      withheld(run('merge that pr', [h], env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${h}`);
+    }
+  }
+  withheld(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view 45; $env:GH_REPO="a/b"'], SHELLS[1]), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr');
+  withheld(run('merge that pr', ['$env:GH_REPO="a/b"; gh pr view 45'], SHELLS[1]), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr');
+  // another variable, or a GIT_* one, does not scope gh
+  exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view 45; export FOO=1']), 'gh pr merge 45');
+  exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view 45; export GIT_DIR=/x']), 'gh pr merge 45');
+  // a branch is scoped by an exported GIT_DIR
+  withheld(run('delete that branch', ['git merge feat; export GIT_DIR=/srv/other.git']), 'git branch -d <BRANCH>', 'branch');
+});
+
+test('major: a later `gh pr view` / `gh pr list` replaces an earlier pull request selector', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const h of ['gh pr view 45; gh pr view', 'gh pr view 45; gh pr list', 'gh pr view 45 && gh pr status', 'gh pr view 45; gh pr view --web',
+      'gh pr view 45; gh pr list --state open']) {
+      withheld(run('merge that pr', [h], env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${h}`);
+    }
+    exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge 45', env.shell);
+    exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr list; gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge 45', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: a refused pull request reference keeps <PR>, never a bare `gh pr merge`', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const h of ['gh pr view 45; env', 'gh pr view', 'gh pr list', 'ls', 'clear']) {
+      const r = run('merge that pr', [h], env);
+      withheld(r, 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${h}`);
+      assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${env.shell}: ${h}`);
+    }
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: a pull request picked out by who or when is withheld', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['merge the pull request by alice', 'merge the pr from yesterday', 'merge the pr opened by bob', 'merge the pr that fixes login',
+      'merge the pr created last week', 'merge pr from 2 days ago']) {
+      withheld(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    // nothing picked out: the current branch's pull request
+    for (const q of ['merge the pr', 'merge pr now', 'merge pull request quickly']) exact(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    exact(run('merge the pr and delete the branch', null, env), 'gh pr merge --delete-branch', env.shell);
+  }
+  exact(run('view pull request on github'), 'gh pr view');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions21.test.js b/test/regressions21.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b4ad11c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions21.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+// Regression tests for round 20: the round-19 findings (review/r19-codex.md). With history, a pull request the request
+// names but that cannot be read ("the pr that fixes login", `that pr "bob's"`) stays withheld, as without history; a
+// scope variable removed after `gh pr view N` (`unset GH_REPO`, `Remove-Item Env:GH_REPO`, ...) makes N ambiguous; the
+// structural command grouping masks operands.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { group } from '../scripts/real/group.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PWSH = { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' };
+const CMD = { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, PWSH, CMD];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const withheld = (r, cmd, slots, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual([...r.missing].sort(), [slots].flat().sort(), msg);
+};
+const exact = (r, cmd, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], msg);
+};
+
+test('major: history never overwrites a pull request the request names but cannot read', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['merge the pr that fixes login', 'merge that pr "bob\'s"', 'merge the pr by alice', 'merge that pr from yesterday', 'merge that pr main']) {
+      for (const h of [null, ['gh pr view 45'], ['gh pr merge 45'], ['gh pr checks 45']]) {
+        withheld(run(q, h, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+      }
+    }
+    // a reference with nothing else named still reads the history
+    exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge 45', env.shell);
+    // a pull request the request names readably wins over the history's
+    exact(run('merge pr 7', ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge 7', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: removing a repository scope after `gh pr view N` makes N ambiguous', () => {
+  const lines = {
+    bash: ['gh pr view 45; unset GH_REPO', 'gh pr view 45 && unset GH_HOST', 'gh pr view 45; unset -v GH_REPO', 'gh pr view 45; export -n GH_REPO',
+      'gh pr view 45; unset FOO GH_REPO', 'gh pr view 45; export GH_REPO=a/b'],
+    pwsh: ['gh pr view 45; Remove-Item Env:GH_REPO', 'gh pr view 45; Remove-Item -Path Env:\\GH_REPO', 'gh pr view 45; rm env:GH_HOST',
+      'gh pr view 45; [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("GH_REPO", $null)', 'gh pr view 45; $env:GH_REPO=$null'],
+    cmd: ['gh pr view 45 & set GH_REPO=', 'gh pr view 45 && set GH_HOST='],
+  };
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const h of lines[env.shell]) {
+      for (const q of ['merge that pr', 'merge that pull request']) withheld(run(q, [h], env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+    }
+  }
+  // the scope is dropped before the pull request is named: it is one of the repository tellsh runs in
+  exact(run('merge that pr', ['unset GH_REPO; gh pr view 45']), 'gh pr merge 45');
+  exact(run('merge that pr', ['Remove-Item Env:GH_REPO; gh pr view 45'], PWSH), 'gh pr merge 45');
+  // an unrelated variable changes nothing
+  exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view 45; unset FOO']), 'gh pr merge 45');
+  exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view 45; Remove-Item Env:FOO'], PWSH), 'gh pr merge 45');
+});
+
+test('minor: the structural command grouping masks operands, the v04 one reproduces the shipped split', () => {
+  for (const [a, b] of [['npm install express', 'npm install react'], ['cat alpha', 'cat beta'], ['git checkout feat', 'git checkout main'],
+    ['gh pr view 12 --repo a/b', 'gh pr view 40 --repo c/d'], ['docker compose up web', 'docker compose up db'], ['sudo apt install curl', 'apt install jq']]) {
+    assert.equal(group(a, 'structural'), group(b, 'structural'), `${a} / ${b}`);
+  }
+  for (const [a, b] of [['gh pr view 12', 'gh pr merge 12'], ['git checkout feat', 'git branch feat'], ['npm install express', 'npm install -g express'],
+    ['docker compose up', 'docker compose down']]) {
+    assert.notEqual(group(a, 'structural'), group(b, 'structural'), `${a} / ${b}`);
+  }
+  assert.notEqual(group('npm install express'), group('npm install react'));
+  assert.equal(group('gh pr view 12 --repo a/b'), 'gh pr view --repo #2');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions22.test.js b/test/regressions22.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e7e80a9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions22.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+// Regression tests for round 21: the round-20 findings (review/r20-claude.md, review/r20-codex.md). A pull request picked
+// out by a word before "pr" ("the dependabot pr", "said pr", "the above pr") or by a label / title ("the pr with label
+// urgent") is withheld, never a bare `gh pr merge` (the current branch's), also with history; a when-word after "from" /
+// "for" is not a branch; Polish "ten pr" / "that one pr" read the history again; wrangler deploy keeps a dry run and an
+// environment instead of deploying to the default target.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PWSH = { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' };
+const CMD = { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, PWSH, CMD];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const withheld = (r, cmd, slots, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual([...r.missing].sort(), [slots].flat().sort(), msg);
+};
+const exact = (r, cmd, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], msg);
+};
+
+test('major: a pull request picked out by a word before "pr" is withheld, with or without history', () => {
+  const qs = ['merge the dependabot pr', 'merge the renovate pr', 'merge the docs pr', 'merge the draft pr', 'merge the green pr',
+    'merge the big pr', 'merge the above pr', 'merge said pr', 'merge the aforementioned pr', 'merge the mentioned pr',
+    'merge the dependabot pull request', 'merge the open pr'];
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of qs) {
+      for (const h of [null, ['gh pr view 45']]) withheld(run(q, h, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+    }
+    // nothing between the determiner and "pr", or a word that keeps the current branch's: still bare
+    for (const q of ['merge the pr', 'merge pr', 'merge the current pr', 'merge my pr', 'merge the github pr', 'merge the pull request']) {
+      exact(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: Polish "to pr" is a reference: the history\'s pull request, else withheld', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    withheld(run('zmerguj to pr', null, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', env.shell);
+    exact(run('zmerguj to pr', ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge 45', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: a pull request picked out by a label or a title is withheld', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['merge the pr with label urgent', 'merge the pull request with title fix login', 'merge the pr with the label bug',
+      'merge the pr labeled urgent', 'zmerguj pr z etykietą pilne']) {
+      for (const h of [null, ['gh pr view 45']]) withheld(run(q, h, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+    }
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: a when-word after "from" / "for" is not a branch', () => {
+  for (const q of ['merge the pr from last week', 'merge the pr from monday', 'merge the pr from before', 'merge the pr from ages ago',
+    'merge the pr from previously']) {
+    for (const h of [null, ['gh pr view 45']]) withheld(run(q, h), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${q} after ${h}`);
+  }
+  withheld(run('view that pr from before'), 'gh pr view <PR>', 'pr');
+  // a branch after "from" / "for" is still read
+  exact(run('merge pull request from bob'), 'gh pr merge bob');
+  exact(run('merge pr for main'), 'gh pr merge main');
+});
+
+test('minor: Polish "ten pr" and "that one pr" read the history again', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    // ("scal ten pr" on cmd is classified as gh_pr_create before any slot is read: a known classifier gap, checked on bash)
+    for (const q of [...(env === BASH ? ['scal ten pr'] : []), 'merge ten pr', 'zmerguj ten pr', 'zmerguj ten pull request', 'merge that one pr', 'merge this one pr', 'zmerguj tego pr']) {
+      exact(run(q, ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge 45', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+      withheld(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    // a real number is still not read as the history's
+    withheld(run('merge the 2 open prs', ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: wrangler deploy keeps a dry run and an environment', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    const cases = {
+      'do a dry run of wrangler deploy': 'npx wrangler deploy --dry-run',
+      'wrangler deploy --dry-run': 'npx wrangler deploy --dry-run',
+      'wdróż workera na sucho': 'npx wrangler deploy --dry-run',
+      'deploy worker to staging': 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging',
+      'deploy worker to the staging environment': 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging',
+      'wrangler deploy --env staging': 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging',
+      'deploy worker to env qa1': 'npx wrangler deploy --env qa1',
+      'deploy the worker to staging dry run': 'npx wrangler deploy --dry-run --env staging',
+      'deploy the worker': 'npx wrangler deploy',
+      'wrangler deploy': 'npx wrangler deploy',
+    };
+    for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(cases)) exact(run(q, null, env), cmd, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    // an environment named but not readable: withheld, never the default target
+    for (const q of ['deploy worker to my env', 'wdróż workera na produkcję', 'deploy worker to env \'a b\'']) {
+      withheld(run(q, null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>', 'wenv', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+  }
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions23.test.js b/test/regressions23.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a6ee55e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions23.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+// Regression tests for round 22: the round-21 findings (review/r21-claude.md, review/r21-codex.md). wrangler deploy never
+// makes up an environment ("worker env", "with env vars", "for testing") and keeps a custom one whole ("staging-eu",
+// "preview2"); a word before "pr" picks out a pull request also without a determiner ("merge dependabot pr", "merge alice's
+// pr"); a quoted label / title is not the pull request; a negated dry run is a real deploy; English "to pr" is not a
+// reference; "the pr in question" is withheld.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PWSH = { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' };
+const CMD = { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, PWSH, CMD];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const withheld = (r, cmd, slots, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual([...r.missing].sort(), [slots].flat().sort(), msg);
+};
+const exact = (r, cmd, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], msg);
+};
+
+test('major: "X env" never makes up an environment name', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['deploy worker env', 'deploy worker with env vars', 'deploy worker with environment variables',
+      'deploy worker using env file', 'deploy worker, my environment is set']) {
+      withheld(run(q, null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>', 'wenv', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    const cases = {
+      'deploy worker environment staging.': 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging',
+      'deploy worker env staging': 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging',
+      'deploy worker to staging env': 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging',
+      'deploy worker to the production environment': 'npx wrangler deploy --env production',
+      'deploy worker to env called foo': 'npx wrangler deploy --env foo',
+      // "for" + a weak name never makes one up ("for testing", "for the qa team" are withheld: test/regressions24.test.js)
+      'deploy worker to cloudflare': 'npx wrangler deploy',
+    };
+    for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(cases)) exact(run(q, null, env), cmd, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: a custom environment name is kept whole', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    const cases = {
+      'deploy worker to staging-eu': 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging-eu',
+      'deploy worker to preview2': 'npx wrangler deploy --env preview2',
+      'deploy worker to the staging-eu environment': 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging-eu',
+    };
+    for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(cases)) exact(run(q, null, env), cmd, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    // v0.3 selector rule: a time the command does not express is the user's to fill
+    const r = run('deploy worker in 2-3 minutes', null, env);
+    assert.equal(r.command, 'npx wrangler deploy <ARGS>', env.shell);
+    assert.deepEqual(r.missing, ['args'], env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: a word before "pr" picks out a pull request also without a determiner', () => {
+  const qs = ['merge dependabot pr', 'merge renovate pr', 'merge docs pr', 'merge draft pr', 'merge open pr', "merge alice's pr",
+    'merge alices pr', 'merge dependabot pull request', 'show checks for dependabot pr'];
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of qs) {
+      for (const h of [null, ['gh pr view 45']]) {
+        const r = run(q, h, env);
+        assert.match(r.command, /^gh pr \w+ <PR>$/, `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+        assert.deepEqual(r.missing, ['pr'], `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+      }
+    }
+    for (const q of ['merge pr', 'merge my pr', 'squash merge pr', 'squash and merge my pr', 'approve and merge pr', 'please merge pr now',
+      'can you merge the pr']) {
+      exact(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    exact(run('merge that pr', ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr merge 45', env.shell);
+    exact(run('show checks for that pr', ['gh pr view 45'], env), 'gh pr checks 45', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: a quoted label or title is not the pull request', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['merge the pr with label "urgent"', 'merge the pr with title "fix-login"', 'merge the pr titled "fix-login"',
+      'merge the pr by "alice"']) {
+      for (const h of [null, ['gh pr view 45']]) withheld(run(q, h, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+    }
+    exact(run('merge the "feature/login" pull request', null, env), 'gh pr merge feature/login', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: a negated dry run is a real deploy', () => {
+  exact(run('deploy the worker, not a dry run'), 'npx wrangler deploy');
+  exact(run('deploy worker to production without dry run'), 'npx wrangler deploy --env production');
+  exact(run('deploy the worker to staging dry run'), 'npx wrangler deploy --dry-run --env staging');
+});
+
+test('minor: English "to pr" is not a reference; "the pr in question" is withheld', () => {
+  const h = ['gh pr view 45'];
+  withheld(run('merge changes to pr', h), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr');
+  assert.notEqual(run('check out to pr', h).command, 'gh pr checks 45');
+  assert.notEqual(run('view diff to pr', h).command, 'gh pr view 45');
+  exact(run('zmerguj to pr', h), 'gh pr merge 45');
+  for (const x of [null, h]) withheld(run('merge the pr in question', x), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions24.test.js b/test/regressions24.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..6bb14af
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions24.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,121 @@
+// Regression tests for round 23: the round-22 findings (review/r22-claude.md, review/r22-codex.md). After "for" only a
+// strong environment name is taken ("for production", "for qa"), a weak one ("for testing", "for the qa team") is
+// withheld, and a request for prod / qa is never dropped to the default target; a quoted environment is decoded, never
+// dropped; a selector after "pr" ("merge pr for the login fix", "merge pr: fix login") is withheld like one before it; a
+// URL of a related pull request is not the merge target; "approve pr" / "open pr in web" are not `gh pr create`.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PWSH = { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' };
+const CMD = { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, PWSH, CMD];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const withheld = (r, cmd, slots, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual([...r.missing].sort(), [slots].flat().sort(), msg);
+};
+const exact = (r, cmd, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], msg);
+};
+
+test('major: after "for" a strong environment is taken, a weak one is withheld, never made up or dropped', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    const cases = {
+      'deploy worker for production': 'production', 'publish worker for prod': 'prod', 'deploy worker for qa': 'qa',
+      'deploy worker for uat': 'uat', 'deploy worker for canary': 'canary', 'deploy worker for preview': 'preview',
+      'deploy worker for staging': 'staging', 'deploy worker for the sandbox': 'sandbox', 'deploy worker for prod now': 'prod',
+      'deploy worker for production.': 'production',
+    };
+    for (const [q, e] of Object.entries(cases)) exact(run(q, null, env), `npx wrangler deploy --env ${e}`, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    for (const q of ['deploy worker for testing', 'deploy worker for test', 'deploy worker for dev', 'deploy worker for beta',
+      'deploy worker for the qa team', 'deploy worker for prod users', 'deploy worker for staging-eu']) {
+      withheld(run(q, null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>', 'wenv', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    // a word after "for" that is not an environment name leaves the default target
+    exact(run('deploy worker for real', null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy', env.shell);
+    // v0.3 selector rule: a descriptive target is the user's to fill
+    withheld(run('deploy worker for a customer', null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>', 'wenv', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: a quoted environment is decoded, never dropped', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    const cases = {
+      'deploy worker to "preview2"': 'npx wrangler deploy --env preview2',
+      "deploy worker to 'staging'": 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging',
+      'deploy worker to “prod-eu”': 'npx wrangler deploy --env prod-eu',
+      'deploy worker env "staging-eu"': 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging-eu',
+      'deploy worker --env "qa"': 'npx wrangler deploy --env qa',
+      'deploy worker env=staging': 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging',
+    };
+    for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(cases)) exact(run(q, null, env), cmd, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    for (const q of ['deploy worker to "my env"', "deploy worker to 'cloudflare'", "deploy worker env 'staging eu'"]) {
+      withheld(run(q, null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>', 'wenv', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
