+    }
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: a marked word after a preposition is an environment only with a known name in it', () => {
+  exact(run('deploy worker to staging-eu'), 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging-eu');
+  exact(run('deploy worker to qa_1'), 'npx wrangler deploy --env qa_1');
+  for (const q of ['deploy worker to v2', 'deploy to the worker-2 script', 'deploy worker to customer-a']) {
+    withheld(run(q), 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>', 'wenv', q);
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: a dry run asked for after a negated one is still a dry run', () => {
+  exact(run('deploy worker without a dry run first? no, do a dry run'), 'npx wrangler deploy --dry-run');
+  // v0.3 selector rule: "not just" leaves something the command does not express: the user fills it
+  const r = run('deploy worker, not just a dry run');
+  assert.equal(r.command, 'npx wrangler deploy --dry-run <ARGS>');
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, ['args']);
+  exact(run('deploy the worker, not a dry run'), 'npx wrangler deploy');
+});
+
+test('major: a selector after "pr" is withheld, never a bare `gh pr merge`', () => {
+  const qs = ['merge pr for the login fix', 'merge pr for the issue', 'merge pr: fix login', 'merge pr with dependabot',
+    'merge pr of my colleague', 'merge pr in docs', 'merge pr - fix login', 'merge pr dependabot', 'merge pr renovate',
+    'merge pr docs', 'merge pr draft', 'merge pr open', "merge pr dependabot's", "merge pr of alice's", 'merge pr about the login fix'];
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of qs) {
+      for (const h of [null, ['gh pr view 45']]) withheld(run(q, h, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+    }
+    for (const q of ['merge pr', 'merge pr now', 'merge pr on github', 'merge pr in this repo', 'merge pr with squash',
+      'merge pr for review', 'merge pr with --squash', 'merge pr in the browser']) {
+      exact(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr merge', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    exact(run('merge pr for main', null, env), 'gh pr merge main', env.shell);
+    exact(run('merge pr for branch fix-1', null, env), 'gh pr merge fix-1', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: "current branch pr", "the branch pr" are the current branch\'s', () => {
+  for (const q of ['merge current branch pr', 'merge the branch pr', "merge branch's pr"]) {
+    for (const h of [null, ['gh pr view 45']]) exact(run(q, h), 'gh pr merge', `${q} after ${h}`);
+  }
+  withheld(run('merge feature branch pr'), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr');
+});
+
+test('major: the URL of a related pull request is not the merge target', () => {
+  const url = 'https://github.com/acme/app/pull/12';
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of [`merge the pr that depends on ${url}`, `merge the pr blocked by ${url}`, `merge the pr after ${url}`]) {
+      for (const h of [null, ['gh pr view 45']]) withheld(run(q, h, env), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr', `${env.shell}: ${q} after ${h}`);
+    }
+    exact(run(`merge pr ${url}`, null, env), `gh pr merge ${url}`, env.shell);
+    exact(run(`view the pull request at ${url}`, null, env), `gh pr view ${url}`, env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('minor: "approve pr" and "open pr in web" are never `gh pr create`', () => {
+  for (const [q, h] of [['approve pr'], ['open pr in web'], ['approve that pr', ['gh pr view 45']], ['zatwierdź pr']]) {
+    const r = run(q, h);
+    assert.notEqual(r.command, 'gh pr create --fill', q);
+    assert.equal(r.understood, false, q);
+  }
+  exact(run('create a pr'), 'gh pr create --fill');
+  exact(run('open a new pr'), 'gh pr create --fill');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions25.test.js b/test/regressions25.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..24947f4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions25.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,164 @@
+// Regression tests for round 24 (v0.3 close): the round-23 findings (review/r23-codex.md, review/r23-claude.md), fixed by
+// two design rules instead of more special cases.
+//  (1) gh / wrangler selector rule: a request is read against a closed vocabulary; a word that neither the vocabulary nor
+//      a value that was read explains (descriptive, quoted, uncertain) withholds the selector as a placeholder the user
+//      fills (`<PR>`, `<WENV>`, `<NUM>`, `<ARGS>`), never a guess and never a bare command.
+//  (2) the danger checker is an allowlist: only the commands / subcommands / flags the catalog renders are trusted; any
+//      wrapper, environment assignment, unknown program, subcommand or flag is high risk (confirmation needed).
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { checkDanger, allowlistProblems } from '../src/danger.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PWSH = { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' };
+const CMD = { shell: 'cmd', os: 'windows' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, PWSH, CMD];
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const withheld = (r, cmd, slots, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual([...r.missing].sort(), [slots].flat().sort(), msg);
+};
+const exact = (r, cmd, msg) => {
+  assert.equal(r.command, cmd, msg);
+  assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], msg);
+};
+
+test('major: an environment after "in" / "on" is withheld, never dropped for the default target', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['deploy worker in preview2', 'deploy worker on qa_1', 'deploy the worker in customer-a', 'deploy worker on the eu cluster']) {
+      withheld(run(q, null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>', 'wenv', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    // read environments stay as they were
+    exact(run('deploy worker to staging', null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging', env.shell);
+    exact(run('deploy worker to preview2', null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy --env preview2', env.shell);
+    exact(run('deploy the worker', null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: a secret update keeps the environment it names (or withholds it)', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['set worker secret API_KEY --env staging', 'set worker secret API_KEY for staging', 'put secret API_KEY on the staging environment']) {
+      exact(run(q, null, env), 'npx wrangler secret put API_KEY --env staging', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    withheld(run('set worker secret API_KEY in preview2', null, env), 'npx wrangler secret put API_KEY --env <WENV>', 'wenv', env.shell);
+    exact(run('set the API_KEY secret on the worker', null, env), 'npx wrangler secret put API_KEY', env.shell);
+  }
+  // the other wrangler commands take --env too
+  exact(run('tail worker logs for production'), 'npx wrangler tail --env production');
+});
+
+test('major: a dependency install never makes up a package name', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['install the project dependencies with npm', 'install dependencies with npm', 'install npm dependencies',
+      'npm install the deps for this repo', 'zainstaluj zaleznosci projektu', 'install dependencies from package.json']) {
+      exact(run(q, null, env), 'npm install', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    for (const q of ['npm ci', 'do a clean install with npm']) exact(run(q, null, env), 'npm ci', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    exact(run('add express to the project with npm', null, env), 'npm install express', env.shell);
+    exact(run('install lodash via npm', null, env), 'npm install lodash', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: pr creation keeps the repository (or withholds it); anything else it cannot express is a placeholder', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    exact(run('create a pull request in repo acme/app', null, env), 'gh pr create --fill --repo acme/app', env.shell);
+    withheld(run('create a pull request in the other repo', null, env), 'gh pr create --fill --repo <REPO>', 'repo', env.shell);
+    for (const q of ['create a pr into develop', 'create a draft pr', 'create a pr with reviewer bob']) {
+      withheld(run(q, null, env), 'gh pr create --fill <ARGS>', 'args', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+    exact(run('create a pull request', null, env), 'gh pr create --fill', env.shell);
+  }
+});
+
+test('rule 1: descriptive, picked-out or unknown selectors are placeholders for every gh / wrangler command', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const [q, cmd, slot] of [
+      ['merge the pr about auth', 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr'],
+      ['merge the pr from the payments team', 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr'],
+      ['view the pr bob opened', 'gh pr view <PR>', 'pr'],
+      ['show checks of the flaky pr', 'gh pr checks <PR>', 'pr'],
+      ['list prs with label bug', 'gh pr list <ARGS>', 'args'],
+      ['list closed prs', 'gh pr list <ARGS>', 'args'],
+      ['deploy worker in 2-3 minutes', 'npx wrangler deploy <ARGS>', 'args'],
+    ]) withheld(run(q, null, env), cmd, slot, `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    // explicit selectors stay; a word that only describes the command does not withhold them
+    exact(run('merge pr 42', null, env), 'gh pr merge 42', env.shell);
+    exact(run('merge pr 45 in repo acme/app', null, env), 'gh pr merge 45 --repo acme/app', env.shell);
+    exact(run('merge pr 45 and delete the branch', null, env), 'gh pr merge 45 --delete-branch', env.shell);
+    exact(run('list open prs', null, env), 'gh pr list', env.shell);
+    exact(run('merge pr 42 in PowerShell', null, env), 'gh pr merge 42', env.shell);
+  }
+  // a second number competes with an explicit one: withheld
+  withheld(run('merge pr 45 or 46'), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr');
+});
+
+test('rule 1: an environment the request excludes is never the target', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    for (const q of ['deploy worker but not to production', 'deploy worker, not to prod', "don't deploy worker to prod",
+      'deploy worker to staging, not production', 'wdróż workera ale nie na produkcję']) {
+      withheld(run(q, null, env), 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>', 'wenv', `${env.shell}: ${q}`);
+    }
+  }
+  // a negated dry run is still a plain deploy
+  exact(run('deploy worker without a dry run'), 'npx wrangler deploy');
+  exact(run('deploy the worker, not a dry run'), 'npx wrangler deploy');
+});
+
+test('minor (r23): url lead-ins, reopen / ready, merge <url>', () => {
+  const url = 'https://github.com/acme/app/pull/12';
+  exact(run(`show me the pr at ${url}`), `gh pr view ${url}`);
+  exact(run(`can you merge the pr at ${url}`), `gh pr merge ${url}`);
+  exact(run(`merge the pr (${url})`), `gh pr merge ${url}`);
+  exact(run(`merge pr, url: ${url}`), `gh pr merge ${url}`);
+  withheld(run(`merge the pr that depends on ${url}`), 'gh pr merge <PR>', 'pr');
+  for (const q of [`merge ${url}`, `squash merge ${url}`, `i want to merge ${url}`]) exact(run(q), `gh pr merge ${url}`, q);
+  for (const q of ['reopen pr', 'mark pr as ready']) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.notEqual(r.command, 'gh pr create --fill', q);
+    assert.equal(r.understood, false, q);
+  }
+});
+
+test('rule 2: wrappers, assignments, unknown programs, subcommands and flags are high risk', () => {
+  for (const c of ['sudo ls', 'timeout 5 ls', 'env FOO=1 ls', 'nohup node server.js', 'xargs -n1 echo', 'bash -c "ls"', 'FOO=1 ls',
+    'mywrap ls', 'cowsay hi', 'git filter-branch', 'npx cowsay', 'npx wrangler delete', 'gh pr close 3', 'docker compose rm -f',
+    'gh pr merge 12 --admin', 'git push --force-with-lease', 'rm -P f', 'ls --hyperlink=always', 'ssh host uptime', 'git -C /x status']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', `${c}: ${d.warnings.join('; ')}`);
+    assert.ok(allowlistProblems(c).length > 0, c);
+  }
+  // known commands and flags: no allowlist problem (option clusters and attached numbers included)
+  for (const c of ['ls -la', 'ls -lah /tmp', 'git status', 'git push origin main', 'tail -n5 f.txt', 'gh pr merge 12 --repo a/b --delete-branch',
+    'npx wrangler deploy --dry-run --env staging', 'docker compose up -d', 'env | sort', 'ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:8080 example.com',
+    'find /tmp -type f -iname "*.log" -mtime -3', 'grep -rn --include="*.js" -- TODO src', 'npm ci', 'node --version']) {
+    assert.deepEqual(allowlistProblems(c), [], c);
+  }
+  // the allowlist only escalates: a deny rule still fires on a known command
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('rm -rf /').critical, true);
+});
+
+test('rule 2: every catalog command is on the allowlist (only its sudo, bash -c and xargs wrappers and the substitution of a high-risk intent escalate)', async () => {
+  const { INTENTS } = await import('../src/catalog.js');
+  const { buildCommand } = await import('../src/fill.js');
+  const V = { path: 'dir', file: 'f.txt', src: 'a.txt', dst: 'b.txt', dest: 'd', archive: 'x.tar.gz', count: 5, depth: 2, size: '10M',
+    age: '-mtime -3', days: 3, port: 8080, pid: 1234, mode: '755', var: 'FOO', name: 'foo', service: 'nginx', container: 'web', pkg: 'htop',
+    cmd: 'node', branch: 'dev', user: 'bob', pattern: 'err', host: 'example.com', target: 'example.com', message: 'msg', url: 'https://x.org/r.git',
+    text: 'hi', ext: 'log', old: 'a', new: 'b', start: 1, end: 5, num: 7, pr: '12', repo: 'a/b', wenv: 'staging', dryrun: '--dry-run', script: 'dev' };
+  const bad = [];
+  for (const it of INTENTS) {
+    for (const env of [BASH, { shell: 'zsh', os: 'darwin', coreutils: 'bsd' }, { shell: 'fish', os: 'linux' }, { shell: 'powershell', os: 'win32' }, { shell: 'cmd', os: 'win32' }]) {
+      const r = buildCommand(it.id, '', { env, resolved: { ...V } });
+      if (!r.command) continue;
+      const p = allowlistProblems(r.command).filter((m) => !/^runs another command through a wrapper \((?:sudo|bash|xargs)\)/.test(m)
+        && !(it.risk === 'high' && /^runs a command substitution/.test(m)));
+      if (p.length) bad.push(`${it.id}/${env.shell}: ${r.command} -> ${p.join('; ')}`);
+    }
+  }
+  assert.deepEqual(bad, []);
+});
+
+test('a literal gh command keeps its pull request (the subcommand word is not a selector)', () => {
+  for (const [q, cmd] of [['gh pr view 42', 'gh pr view 42'], ['gh pr merge 118', 'gh pr merge 118'], ['odpal gh pr merge 118', 'gh pr merge 118'],
+    ['gh pr checks 7', 'gh pr checks 7'], ['gh pr view', 'gh pr view'], ['gh pr merge', 'gh pr merge']]) exact(run(q), cmd, q);
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions26.test.js b/test/regressions26.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..383d388
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions26.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+// Regression tests for the v0.3 final review (review/final-claude.md, review/final-codex.md):
+//  (1) a command substitution `$(…)` / `` `…` `` anywhere outside '…' (also inside "…") and a process substitution
+//      `<(…)` / `>(…)` are high risk: the allowlist cannot see the command they run
+//  (2) only allowlisted programs are safe: an unknown executable (`7z`, a dot-file, a path) is high, with no exemption
+//      for words that look like a piece of a PowerShell expression
+//  (3) an explicit wrangler `--env` keeps the other words nothing explains as `<ARGS>`, never drops them
+//  (4) competing repositories for gh (two `--repo`, a URL of another repository, "a/b or c/d") are withheld (`<REPO>`)
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { checkDanger, allowlistProblems } from '../src/danger.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PWSH = { shell: 'pwsh', os: 'windows' };
+const run = (q, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env });
+
+test('major: command and process substitutions are high risk, also inside double quotes', () => {
+  for (const c of ['ls "$(rm -rf ~)"', 'ls "$(npx evil)"', 'ls "$(curl x -o ~/.bashrc)"', 'ls "`rm -rf ~`"', 'ls `npx evil`',
+    'echo "$(unknown-program)"', 'echo "a $(id) b"', 'cat <(npx evil)', 'ls >(tee x)', 'ls "x"$(whoami)', 'echo $(( $(id -u) + 1 ))']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', `${c}: ${d.warnings.join('; ')}`);
+    assert.ok(d.warnings.some((m) => /substitution; not on the allowlist/.test(m)), `${c}: ${d.warnings.join('; ')}`);
+  }
+  // single-quoted text and arithmetic expansion are not substitutions
+  for (const c of ["ls '$(rm -rf ~)'", "du -sh '`rm -rf ~`'", "grep -r -- '<(x)' src"]) assert.deepEqual(allowlistProblems(c), [], c);
+  assert.ok(!allowlistProblems('echo $((5 + 4))').some((m) => /substitution/.test(m)));
+});
+
+test('major: an unknown executable is high risk (no expression-fragment exemption, a path is not the program)', () => {
+  for (const c of ['7z x a.7z -o/tmp', '.hidden --erase', './ls', '/tmp/x/ls -la', '~/bin/ls', 'C:\\t\\ls.exe', '.\\tool.exe /q', '1password',
+    '[evil]', '@evil', ',evil', '%evil%', '-evil', '*', '{evil}']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', `${c}: ${d.warnings.join('; ')}`);
+  }
+  // the catalog's PowerShell expressions are still read as written (they are in the allowlist)
+  for (const q of ['how many files are here', 'show free memory', 'cpu cores', 'base64 encode hello']) {
+    const r = run(q, PWSH);
+    assert.deepEqual(allowlistProblems(r.command), [], `${q}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: an explicit --env keeps the unexplained deploy arguments as <ARGS>', () => {
+  for (const env of [BASH, PWSH]) {
+    const r = run('deploy worker --env staging --config other.toml', env);
+    assert.equal(r.command, 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging <ARGS>', `${env.shell}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.deepEqual(r.missing, ['args']);
+  }
+  // nothing unexplained: the explicit environment alone
+  for (const [q, cmd] of [['deploy worker --env staging', 'npx wrangler deploy --env staging'],
+    ['deploy worker --env staging --dry-run', 'npx wrangler deploy --dry-run --env staging']]) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.equal(r.command, cmd, q);
+    assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], q);
+  }
+});
+
+test('major: competing repositories are withheld, also beside an explicit pull request', () => {
+  for (const [q, cmd] of [
+    ['merge pr 42 --repo acme/app or --repo other/repo', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo <REPO>'],
+    ['merge pr 42 --repo acme/app --repo other/repo', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo <REPO>'],
+    ['merge pr 42 in acme/app or other/repo', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo <REPO>'],
+    ['merge pr acme/app#42 --repo other/repo', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo <REPO>'],
+    ['merge https://github.com/acme/app/pull/42 --repo other/repo', 'gh pr merge https://github.com/acme/app/pull/42 --repo <REPO>'],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.equal(r.command, cmd, q);
+    assert.deepEqual(r.missing, ['repo'], q);
+  }
+  // one repository, however often it is named: kept
+  for (const [q, cmd] of [['merge pr 42 --repo acme/app', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo acme/app'],
+    ['merge https://github.com/acme/app/pull/42 --repo acme/app', 'gh pr merge https://github.com/acme/app/pull/42 --repo acme/app'],
+    ['merge pr acme/app#42', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo acme/app']]) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.equal(r.command, cmd, q);
+    assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], q);
+  }
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions27.test.js b/test/regressions27.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..7129ad5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions27.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,167 @@
+// Regression tests for the v0.3 final2 review (review/final2-claude.md, review/final2-codex.md) and the structural rules
+// that replace further parser patches:
+//  (1) trust rule: a command is safe ONLY when it is tellsh's own render of a risk=safe catalog template with plain slot
+//      values; edited, composed, history-replayed and unknown commands are at least high (--yes never runs them). The
+//      parser only raises risk: it still reads $'…' quoting and sed e/w so a destructive payload stays critical.
+//  (2) contested selectors: an alternative or a negation next to a selector (or / albo / lub / not / nie / oprócz /
+//      except …) or two candidate values for one slot give a placeholder for that slot, never one of the candidates.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { buildCommand } from '../src/fill.js';
+import { INTENTS, BY_ID } from '../src/catalog.js';
+import { checkDanger, assessCommand, plainSlotValue, UNTRUSTED } from '../src/danger.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, opts = {}) => suggest(q, { env: BASH, ...opts });
+
+// every command the two final2 reviews reported as safe
+const FINAL2_DANGER = [
+  // final2-claude blocker: $'…' hid the command after it
+  "echo $'\\''; rm -rf ~ #'",
+  "echo $'\\''; npx evil #'",
+  "ls $'\\''`npx evil`'",
+  // final2-claude major: find -exec runs any program
+  'find . -exec ./evil {} +',
+  'find . -exec bash ./evil.sh \\;',
+  'find . -exec npx evil \\;',
+  // final2-claude major: . and source run any file
+  '. /tmp/x',
+  'source ./evil.sh',
+  'source ~/.bashrc',
+  // final2-claude lesser: GNU sed e
+  "sed 's/a/b/e' f",
+  "sed -n '1e cmd' f",
+  // final2-codex major
+  "sed '1e rm -r /tmp/valuable' input.txt",
+  'diskutil eraseDisk APFS New disk2',
+  'source ./deploy.sh',
+];
+
+test('final2: every reported command is high risk (never safe) and needs an explicit yes', () => {
+  for (const c of FINAL2_DANGER) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', `${c}: ${d.warnings.join('; ')}`);
+  }
+});
+
+test("final2 blocker: $'…' is parsed as bash does, so the command after it is seen (rm -rf ~ stays critical)", () => {
+  const d = assessCommand("echo $'\\''; rm -rf ~ #'");
+  assert.equal(d.risk, 'high');
+  assert.equal(d.critical, true, d.warnings.join('; '));
+  assert.ok(assessCommand("echo $'\\''; npx evil #'").warnings.some((m) => /npx evil|unknown subcommand/.test(m)));
+  assert.ok(assessCommand("ls $'\\''`npx evil`'").warnings.some((m) => /substitution/.test(m)));
+  // a closed $'…' with no escape is still one word
+  assert.equal(assessCommand("echo $'a b'").critical, false);
+});
+
+test('final2 lesser: the parser flags sed scripts that run a command or write a file', () => {
+  for (const c of ["sed 's/a/b/e' f", "sed -n '1e cmd' f", "sed 'w out' f", "sed -e 's/a/b/w x' f", 'sed -f script.sed f']) {
+    assert.ok(assessCommand(c).warnings.some((m) => /^sed /.test(m)), c);
+  }
+  for (const c of ["sed -n '120,180p' f", "sed 's/e/w/g' f", "sed '/we/d' f", "readlink /etc/localtime | sed 's#.*/zoneinfo/##'"]) {
+    assert.ok(!assessCommand(c).warnings.some((m) => /^sed /.test(m)), c);
+  }
+});
+
+test('trust rule: any command that is not a catalog render is at least high, however harmless it looks', () => {
+  for (const c of ['ls -la', 'df -h', 'git status', 'diskutil list', 'echo hi']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', c);
+    assert.ok(d.warnings.includes(UNTRUSTED), c);
+    // the same text vouched for as tellsh's own render is judged by the parser alone
+    assert.notEqual(checkDanger(c, 'safe', { rendered: true }).risk, 'high', c);
+  }
+  // a catalog render does not lower a risk the parser finds
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('rm -rf /', 'safe', { rendered: true }).critical, true);
+});
+
+test('trust rule: a safe catalog render is safe only with plain slot values', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('show free disk space').risk, 'safe');
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('count_lines', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { file: 'notes.txt' } }).risk, 'safe');
+  for (const file of ['a;b.txt', "it's.txt", 'a$b', 'a`b`', 'a|b', 'a>b', 'a\nb', 'x’y']) {
+    const r = buildCommand('count_lines', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { file } });
+    assert.equal(r.risk, 'high', JSON.stringify(file));
+    assert.ok(r.warnings.includes(UNTRUSTED), JSON.stringify(file));
+  }
+  // a path starting with - is rendered ./-x (plain); a pattern starting with - is not
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('count_lines', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { file: '-x' } }).risk, 'safe');
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('grep_text', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { pattern: '-e' } }).risk, 'high');
+  // a program slot: never a builtin that runs a file / a string, never a path
+  for (const cmd of ['source', '.', 'eval', './evil', '/tmp/evil']) {
+    assert.equal(buildCommand('tool_version', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { cmd } }).risk, 'high', cmd);
+  }
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('tool_version', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { cmd: 'node' } }).risk, 'safe');
+  assert.equal(plainSlotValue('name', 'x -exec rm {} +'), false);
+  assert.equal(plainSlotValue('age', '-mtime -1', { dashOk: true }), true);
+});
+
+test('trust rule: only risk=safe catalog intents ever render safe, in every shell', () => {
+  const envs = [BASH, { shell: 'zsh', os: 'darwin', coreutils: 'bsd' }, { shell: 'fish', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' },
+    { shell: 'powershell', os: 'win32' }, { shell: 'cmd', os: 'win32' }];
+  for (const it of INTENTS) {
+    for (const env of envs) {
+      let r;
+      try { r = buildCommand(it.id, '', { env, resolved: {} }); } catch { continue; }
+      if (r.command && r.risk === 'safe') assert.equal(BY_ID[it.id].risk, 'safe', `${it.id} ${env.shell}`);
+    }
+  }
+});
+
+test('trust rule: history replays and composed commands are at least high', () => {
+  const h = run('count lines in it', { history: ['cat notes.txt'], compose: 'off' });
+  assert.equal(h.method, 'history-rule');
+  assert.equal(h.risk, 'high');
+  const same = run('same for /var', { history: ['du -sh /home'], compose: 'off' });
+  assert.equal(same.command, 'du -sh /var');
+  assert.equal(same.risk, 'high');
+  // the same request without history is a fresh catalog render: safe
+  assert.equal(run('show the size of /var').risk, 'safe');
+  const c = run('list files sorted by size with human readable sizes in reverse order', { compose: 'force' });
+  assert.equal(c.method, 'composed');
+  assert.equal(c.risk, 'high');
+});
+
+test('final2-codex: competing selectors give a placeholder, never one of the candidates', () => {
+  for (const [q, cmd, missing] of [
+    ['merge pr 4 or 44', 'gh pr merge <PR>', ['pr']],
+    ['deploy worker --env prod --env prodprod', 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>', ['wenv']],
+    ['merge pr 42 but not in repo acme/app', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo <REPO>', ['repo']],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.equal(r.command, cmd, q);
+    assert.deepEqual(r.missing, missing, q);
+  }
+});
+
+test('contested selectors: alternatives / negations (EN, PL) and two candidates for one slot', () => {
+  for (const [q, cmd] of [
+    ['zmerguj pr 42 albo 43', 'gh pr merge <PR>'],
+    ['merge pr 42, not 43', 'gh pr merge <PR>'],
+    ['deploy worker to prod, not staging', 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>'],
+    ['wdróż workera na produkcję, nie na staging', 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>'],
+    ['deploy worker to staging and production', 'npx wrangler deploy --env <WENV>'],
+    ['install axios or lodash with npm', 'npm install <PKG>'],
+    ['view run 8080808, not 123', 'gh run view <NUM>'],
+    // the alternative is about the repository: the pull request stays
+    ['merge pr 42 --repo acme/app or --repo other/repo', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo <REPO>'],
+  ]) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+  // no alternative / negation next to a selector: unchanged
+  for (const [q, cmd] of [
+    ['merge pr 42', 'gh pr merge 42'],
+    ['npm install axios', 'npm install axios'],
+    ['deploy worker to production', 'npx wrangler deploy --env production'],
+    ['deploy worker to prod without a dry run', 'npx wrangler deploy --env prod'],
+    ['co poszło nie tak w runie pipeline 8080808', 'gh run view 8080808'],
+    ['why is run 8080808 not passing', 'gh run view 8080808'],
+  ]) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+});
+
+test('a negated branch delete is no --delete-branch; a withheld run number is a placeholder, never dropped', () => {
+  for (const q of ["merge pr 42 and don't delete the branch", 'zmerguj pr 42 i nie usuwaj brancha', 'merge pr 42 without deleting the branch']) {
+    assert.equal(run(q).command, 'gh pr merge 42', q);
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('merge pr 42 and delete the branch').command, 'gh pr merge 42 --delete-branch');
+  // was `gh run view` (the withheld `?` dropped the optional run number)
+  assert.equal(run('view run 8080808 2').command, 'gh run view <NUM>');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions28.test.js b/test/regressions28.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..529ff60
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions28.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,194 @@
+// Regression tests for the v0.3 final3 review (review/final3-claude.md, review/final3-codex.md) and the rules that replace
+// further parser patches:
+//  (1) paths: an unquoted path or name followed by more words of its name (`~/Old Projects`) is taken to the end of its
+//      span; when that end is unclear (`/tmp/a.txt b.txt`) the path is a placeholder. Never the first word alone.
+//  (2) prompt: a medium-risk command never runs on a plain Enter (it needs "y"); a high-risk one needs "yes".
+//  (3) tools that run project code (pytest, npm/yarn/pnpm run, make, cargo, go test/run, python/node scripts, npx,
+//      wrangler) are at least medium, also for --help / --version.
+//  (4) scope options (--workspace, --repo / "in project X", --env, --config, --prefix) are kept or placeholdered, never
+//      dropped.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest, pathTail } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { assessCommand, checkDanger } from '../src/danger.js';
+import { scopeMentions } from '../src/fill.js';
+import { confirmRule } from '../src/cli.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const SHELLS = [BASH, { shell: 'zsh', os: 'darwin', coreutils: 'bsd' }, { shell: 'fish', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' },
+  { shell: 'powershell', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' }, { shell: 'cmd', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' }];
+const run = (q, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env });
+
+// ---------- (1) paths ----------
+test('final3-claude major: an unquoted path with spaces is never cut at its first space', () => {
+  const whole = {
+    'delete the folder ~/Old Projects': "rm -r ~/'Old Projects'",
+    'delete folder /tmp/my data': "rm -r '/tmp/my data'",
+    'delete all .log files in /var/log old': "find '/var/log old' -type f -iname '*.log' -delete",
+    'chmod 777 /srv/my app': "chmod 777 '/srv/my app'",
+    'move /tmp/old notes to /tmp/archive': "mv -i '/tmp/old notes' /tmp/archive",
+    // the same for a bare name and for Polish
+    'delete the folder Old Projects': "rm -r 'Old Projects'",
+    'usuń folder ~/Stare Projekty': "rm -r ~/'Stare Projekty'",
+    // a modifier or a connector ends the name
+    'delete the folder ~/Old Projects please': "rm -r ~/'Old Projects'",
+    'delete the folder ~/Old Projects recursively': "rm -r ~/'Old Projects'",
+    'copy ~/My Notes to /tmp/backup': "cp -ri ~/'My Notes' /tmp/backup",
+  };
+  for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(whole)) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.equal(r.command, cmd, q);
+    assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], q);
+  }
+});
+
+test('final3-claude major: a path whose end is unclear is a placeholder with a warning', () => {
+  for (const [q, cmd, k] of [
+    ['delete file /tmp/a.txt b.txt', 'rm <FILE>', 'file'],
+    ['delete file /tmp/my notes.txt', 'rm <FILE>', 'file'],
+    ['copy /tmp/my notes /tmp/b', 'cp -ri <SRC> /tmp/b', 'src'],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.equal(r.command, cmd, q);
+    assert.ok(r.missing.includes(k), q);
+    assert.ok(r.warnings.some((w) => /unclear where the unquoted name ends/.test(w)), `${q}: ${r.warnings.join('; ')}`);
+  }
+  // ends in sentence punctuation: the existing placeholder (the name may include the `.`)
+  const p = run('delete the folder ~/Old Projects.');
+  assert.equal(p.command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+});
+
+test('paths: words of the request after a path are not part of its name', () => {
+  for (const [q, cmd] of [
+    ['make script.sh executable', 'chmod +x script.sh'],
+    ['delete file /tmp/notes.txt now', 'rm /tmp/notes.txt'],
+    ['delete file /tmp/notes.txt permanently', 'rm /tmp/notes.txt'],
+    ['copy /tmp/a /tmp/b', 'cp -ri /tmp/a /tmp/b'],
+    ['copy /tmp/a.txt /tmp/b', 'cp -ri /tmp/a.txt /tmp/b'],
+    ['list files in ~/Old Projects', "ls -lah ~/'Old Projects'"],
+    ['which directory inside node_modules is the largest? show 15', 'du -h -d 1 node_modules 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -n 15'],
+    ['ile jest plików w /etc razem z podkatalogami', 'find /etc -type f | wc -l'],
+    ['utwórz archiwum tar.gz z /etc o nazwie etc.tgz', 'tar -czvf etc.tgz /etc'],
+  ]) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+  // a withheld path keeps its placeholder in an optional part of the template (never `git restore` of everything)
+  assert.equal(pathTail('rm /tmp/a.txt b.txt', '/tmp/a.txt', [], { used: ['b.txt'] }), null);
+  assert.deepEqual(pathTail('rm /tmp/a.txt b.txt', '/tmp/a.txt', []), { ambiguous: true, words: ['b.txt'] });
+});
+
+test('paths: the composer takes the whole name too, never its first word', () => {
+  const r = run('recursively chmod 777 /srv/my app');
+  assert.ok(r.command.endsWith("'/srv/my app'"), r.command);
+  assert.ok(!/(?:^|\s)\/srv\/my(?:\s|$)/.test(r.command), r.command);
+  // a read-only composed command is not blocked by words of the request after its path
+  assert.equal(run('find files in /tmp owned by user bob').command, 'find /tmp -type f -user bob');
+});
+
+test('paths: the one-argument and the several-argument forms agree', () => {
+  // `tellsh delete the folder "~/Old Projects"` is quoted again by joinArgs
+  assert.equal(run('delete the folder ~/Old Projects').command, run("delete the folder '~/Old Projects'").command);
+});
+
+// ---------- (2) prompt ----------
+test('final3-claude major: a medium-risk command never runs on a plain Enter', () => {
+  const med = confirmRule('medium');
+  for (const a of ['', ' ', 'n', 'no', 'x']) assert.equal(med.accepts(a), false, JSON.stringify(a));
+  for (const a of ['y', 'Y', 'yes', 't', 'tak']) assert.equal(med.accepts(a), true, a);
+  assert.match(med.prompt, /Type y to run/);
+  const high = confirmRule('high');
+  for (const a of ['', 'y', 't']) assert.equal(high.accepts(a), false, JSON.stringify(a));
+  for (const a of ['yes', 'YES', 'tak']) assert.equal(high.accepts(a), true, a);
+  // composed (experimental) is like high; an unknown rating too
+  assert.equal(confirmRule('medium', { composed: true }).accepts('y'), false);
+  assert.equal(confirmRule(undefined).accepts(''), false);
+  // safe: Enter runs
+  for (const a of ['', 'y', 'yes']) assert.equal(confirmRule('safe').accepts(a), true, JSON.stringify(a));
+  // incomplete: never runs as is
+  for (const r of ['safe', 'medium', 'high']) assert.equal(confirmRule(r, { incomplete: true }).accepts('yes'), false, r);
+  // the reviewed medium rows need "y"
+  for (const q of ['chmod 777 /srv/my app', 'move /tmp/old notes to /tmp/archive']) assert.equal(run(q).risk, 'medium', q);
+});
+
+// ---------- (3) project code ----------
+test('final3-codex major: tools that run project code are at least medium, also for --help', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    const r = run('show the help for pytest', env);
+    assert.equal(r.risk, 'medium', `${env.shell}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.ok(r.warnings.some((w) => /runs code from the project/.test(w)), env.shell);
+  }
+  for (const c of ['pytest --help', 'pytest --version', 'py.test --help', 'make --help', 'make', 'cargo --version', 'cargo test',
+    'go test ./...', 'go run .', 'go generate', 'python3 script.py', 'python -m mypkg', 'node app.js', 'node server.js --help',
+    'npx eslint --help', 'npm run build', 'npm run --help', 'npm test', 'yarn dev', 'yarn --version', 'pnpm run build',
+    'wrangler --version', 'wrangler dev', 'npx wrangler deploy', 'bun run dev', 'tox --help', 'poetry run pytest', 'uv run x.py', 'bundle exec rake']) {
+    assert.notEqual(assessCommand(c).risk, 'safe', c);
+    assert.notEqual(checkDanger(c, 'safe', { rendered: true }).risk, 'safe', c);
+  }
+  // the tool's own --help / --version, without project code: unchanged
+  for (const c of ['node --version', 'python3 --version', 'npm --version', 'npm --help', 'pnpm --help', 'go version', 'go help', 'git --help']) {
+    assert.equal(checkDanger(c, 'safe', { rendered: true }).risk, 'safe', c);
+  }
+  for (const q of ['pokaz wersje cargo', 'help for make']) assert.equal(run(q).risk, 'medium', q);
+  // a medium intent gets no extra warning (it is medium already)
+  assert.ok(!run('run npm deploy').warnings.some((w) => /runs code from the project/.test(w)));
+});
+
+// ---------- (4) scope options ----------
+test('final3-codex major: an npm workspace is kept, never dropped', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) {
+    const r = run('run npm deploy --workspace staging', env);
+    assert.match(r.command, /^npm run '?deploy'? --workspace staging$/, `${env.shell}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  for (const [q, cmd] of [
+    ['run npm deploy -w staging', 'npm run deploy --workspace staging'],
+    ['run npm deploy --workspace=staging', 'npm run deploy --workspace staging'],
+    ['run the build script in workspace api', 'npm run build --workspace api'],
+    ['install express in workspace api', 'npm install express --workspace api'],
+  ]) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+  // two workspaces: neither is guessed
+  const two = run('run npm deploy --workspace a --workspace b');
+  assert.equal(two.command, 'npm run deploy --workspace <WORKSPACE>');
+  assert.ok(two.missing.includes('workspace'));
+  // a workspace that is not a readable name
+  assert.ok(run('run npm deploy --workspace ../x').missing.includes('workspace'));
+});
+
+test('final3-codex major: a scope npm cannot express is a placeholder, never dropped', () => {
+  for (const [q, cmd] of [
+    ['run npm deploy --env prod', 'npm run deploy <SCOPE>'],
+    ['run npm test in project api', 'npm run test <SCOPE>'],
+    ['run tests with npm --prefix api', 'npm run test <SCOPE>'],
+    ['run npm build --config x.json', 'npm run build <SCOPE>'],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.equal(r.command, cmd, q);
+    assert.ok(r.missing.includes('scope'), q);
+  }
+});
+
+test('final3-codex major: an explicit pull request does not hide an unresolved repository', () => {
+  for (const env of SHELLS) assert.equal(run('merge pr 42 in project acme/backend', env).command, 'gh pr merge 42 --repo acme/backend', env.shell);
+  for (const [q, cmd] of [
+    ['merge pr 42 in project backend', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo <REPO>'],
+    ['view pr 42 in project acme/backend', 'gh pr view 42 --repo acme/backend'],
+    ['list prs in project acme/backend', 'gh pr list --repo acme/backend'],
+    ['merge pr 42 in acme/backend', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo acme/backend'],
+    ['merge pr 42 --repo acme/backend', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo acme/backend'],
+    // gh has no environment: placeholder
+    ['merge pr 42 --env prod', 'gh pr merge 42 <SCOPE>'],
+  ]) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
+  // a wrangler config file is not dropped either
+  assert.ok(run('deploy worker --config other.toml').missing.length > 0);
+});
+
+test('scope mentions: short options belong to one tool', () => {
+  assert.deepEqual(scopeMentions('npm_run_script', 'run build -w api').map((s) => s.kind), ['workspace']);
+  assert.deepEqual(scopeMentions('gh_pr_merge', 'merge pr -w api'), []);
+  assert.deepEqual(scopeMentions('gh_pr_merge', 'merge pr 4 -R a/b').map((s) => [s.kind, s.value]), [['repo', 'a/b']]);
+  // "in this project" is the working directory's
+  assert.deepEqual(scopeMentions('npm_run_script', 'run build in this project'), []);
+});
+
+test('a contested npm script is a placeholder, never the literal marker', () => {
+  const r = run('run npm build or test');
+  assert.equal(r.command, 'npm run <SCRIPT>');
+  assert.ok(!/'\?'/.test(r.command));
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions3-history.test.js b/test/regressions3-history.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..7efde54
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions3-history.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+// Regression tests for the round-3 review findings on history references (src/history.js):
+// search roots as destructive targets, compound-line recency, request verbs as target hints,
+// unused history notes, and multi-argument `ls`.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { buildContext, ctxFeatures } from '../src/history.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, history });
+
+test('history: "delete them" after a search never targets the search root', () => {
+  for (const [q, h, root] of [
+    ['delete them', ['find /var/log -name "*.gz"'], '/var/log'],
+    ['delete them', ['grep -rl TODO src'], 'src'],
+    ['delete them', ['find . -name node_modules -type d'], '.'],
+    ['delete it', ['find /var/log -name "*.gz"'], '/var/log'],
+    ['remove those', ['grep -r TODO /srv/app'], '/srv/app'],
+    ['wipe them', ['find /var/log -name "*.gz"'], '/var/log'], // no history verb: the classifier picks the intent
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q, h);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.ok(!r.command?.includes(` ${root}`) || /<PATH>/.test(r.command), `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.notEqual(r.slotSources?.path, 'history');
+  }
+  // still refused, as before
+  assert.equal(run('delete those files', ['find ~ -size +1G']).context.rule, 'refused');
+  // non-destructive reuse of the search root is fine
+  assert.equal(run('list it', ['find /var/log -name "*.gz"']).command, 'ls -lah /var/log');
+  assert.equal(run('how big is it', ['grep -rl TODO src']).command, 'du -sh src');
+  // the same directory used by a newer non-listing command is an ordinary target again; a newer listing
+  // of it is not (round 4b: "it" after `ls src` may be src or one of its entries)
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['grep -rl TODO src', 'du -sh src']).command, 'rm -r src');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['grep -rl TODO src', 'ls src']).context.rule, 'refused');
+  const ctx = buildContext(['find /var/log -name "*.gz"']);
+  assert.ok(ctx.searchRoots.has('/var/log'));
+});
+
+test('history: the later segment of a compound line wins across entity types', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat old.txt; mkdir newdir']).command, 'rm -r newdir');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat old.txt && du -sh newdir']).command, 'rm -r newdir');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['mkdir olddir; cat new.txt']).command, 'rm new.txt');
+  // a listing: neither the listed directory nor the older file (round 4b)
+  for (const h of ['cat old.txt; ls newdir', 'cat old.txt && ls newdir', 'ls olddir; cat new.txt']) {
+    if (h.startsWith('ls')) assert.equal(run('delete it', [h]).command, 'rm new.txt');
+    else assert.match(run('delete it', [h]).command, /<PATH>/, h);
+  }
+  // the newest target is ambiguous: refuse instead of falling back to old.txt
+  const amb = run('delete it', ['cat old.txt; ls $D']);
+  assert.equal(amb.context.rule, 'refused');
+  assert.ok(!/old\.txt/.test(amb.command), amb.command);
+  // the model features (ctx_last=...) are unchanged: they still rank types by line only
+  const ctx = buildContext(['cat old.txt; ls newdir']);
+  assert.deepEqual(ctx.refOrder, ['dir', 'file']);
+  assert.deepEqual(ctx.entOrder, ['file', 'dir']);
+  assert.deepEqual(ctxFeatures(ctx), ['ctx_last=file', 'ctx_has=file', 'ctx_has=dir']);
+});
+
+test('history: request verbs are not target hints (newest target wins)', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('remove it', ['mkdir /srv/remove-backups', 'mkdir /srv/current']).command, 'rm -r /srv/current');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['mkdir /srv/delete-me', 'mkdir /srv/current']).command, 'rm -r /srv/current');
+  assert.equal(run('kill it', ['pgrep kill-worker', 'pgrep current-worker']).command, 'pkill -f current-worker');
+  assert.equal(run('stop that process', ['pgrep stop-worker', 'pgrep current-worker']).command, 'pkill -f current-worker');
+  assert.equal(run('usuń to', ['mkdir /srv/usun-stare', 'mkdir /srv/current']).command, 'rm -r /srv/current');
+  // only the previous command is a reference target: a target word never selects an older line, and a changing
+  // command whose words do not match the previous value is refused
+  assert.ok(!/remove-backups/.test(run('show that backups folder', ['ls /srv/remove-backups', 'ls /srv/current']).command ?? ''));
+  const old = run('delete that backups folder', ['mkdir /srv/remove-backups', 'mkdir /srv/current']);
+  assert.equal(old.context.rule, 'refused');
+  assert.equal(old.command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+});
+
+test('history: a note never claims a history value the command does not use', () => {
+  const r = run('what about this', ['rm -r foo']);
+  assert.ok(!/foo/.test(r.command ?? ''), r.command);
+  assert.ok(!/foo/.test(r.context.note ?? ''), r.context.note);
+  assert.notEqual(r.context.rule, 'pronoun');
+  assert.ok(!Object.values(r.slotSources ?? {}).includes('history'));
+});
+
+test('history: `ls /a /b` + "it": several operands, none of them is "it" (round 8: no longer the last one)', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['du -sh /a /b']).command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['ls /a /b']).command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+  assert.match(run('show it', ['ls /a /b']).command, /<PATH>/);
+  assert.match(run('how big is it', ['du -sh /a /b']).command, /<PATH>/);
+  assert.equal(run('how big is it', ['du -sh /b']).command, 'du -sh /b');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions3-render.test.js b/test/regressions3-render.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a98b090
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions3-render.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,151 @@
+// Regression tests for the round-3 review findings on rendering, the danger checker and the composer:
+// PowerShell < 7.3 native-argument guard on every slot, danger checker gaps (wrappers, path
+// normalisation, system directories, mv, docker -v=), composer quoting/--author/substitution, and
+// cmd.exe handling of values containing `/`.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+// the parser on its own (it only raises risk); the trust rule (a non-catalog command is high) is in regressions27.test.js
+import { assessCommand as checkDanger, normTarget } from '../src/danger.js';
+import { buildCommand } from '../src/fill.js';
+import { cmdQuote, pwshNativeSlots } from '../src/render.js';
+import { compose, validateComposed } from '../src/compose.js';
+import { extractSlots } from '../src/slots.js';
+// v0.3: commands outside the catalog are high by the allowlist; these cases check the deny rules alone
+const denyOnly = (c, base = 'safe') => checkDanger(c, base, { allowlist: { off: true } });
+
+const PS_WIN = { shell: 'powershell', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const CMD = { shell: 'cmd', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// 1. PowerShell < 7.3: every slot of a native command is checked, not only the first one
+
+test('pwshNativeSlots finds every slot of a native command', () => {
+  assert.deepEqual([...pwshNativeSlots('tar -czvf {archive} {path}')].sort(), ['archive', 'path']);
+  assert.deepEqual([...pwshNativeSlots('tar -xzvf {file}«-C {dest}»')].sort(), ['dest', 'file']);
+  assert.deepEqual([...pwshNativeSlots('scp {target}:{dst}')].sort(), ['dst', 'target']);
+  assert.deepEqual([...pwshNativeSlots('docker logs --tail {count!raw} -f {container}')], ['container']);
+  // cmdlets / expressions are still not native
+  assert.deepEqual([...pwshNativeSlots('if (Test-Path -LiteralPath {file}) { (Get-Item -LiteralPath {file}).LastWriteTime = Get-Date } else { New-Item -ItemType File -Path {file} }')], []);
+  assert.deepEqual([...pwshNativeSlots('Compress-Archive -LiteralPath {path} -DestinationPath {archive}')], []);
+});
+
+test('PowerShell: a later native slot with " is refused (tar -C, tar path)', () => {
+  const x = buildCommand('extract_targz', '', { env: PS_WIN, resolved: { file: 'x.tar.gz', dest: 'out" --to-command="calc' } });
+  assert.equal(x.command, null);
+  assert.match(x.gap, /native program/);
+  const c = buildCommand('compress_targz', '', { env: PS_WIN, resolved: { archive: 'b.tar.gz', path: 'a" --use-compress-program=evil "b' } });
+  assert.equal(c.command, null);
+  assert.match(c.gap, /native program/);
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('compress_targz', '', { env: PS_WIN, resolved: { archive: 'b.tar.gz', path: 'src' } }).command, "tar -czvf 'b.tar.gz' 'src'");
+  const r = suggest(`extract x.tar.gz to 'out" --to-command="calc'`, { env: PS_WIN });
+  assert.equal(r.command, null);
+});
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// 2. danger checker
+
+test('wrapper commands are looked through (timeout, chroot, stdbuf, env, nice, xargs, ...)', () => {
+  for (const c of ['timeout 5 rm -rf /', 'timeout -s KILL 5 rm -rf /', 'chroot / rm -rf /', 'chroot --userspec=a:b /mnt rm -rf /',
+    'stdbuf -oL rm -rf /', 'stdbuf -o L rm -rf /', 'env -u X A=1 rm -rf /', 'nice -n 5 rm -rf /', 'ionice -c 3 rm -rf /',
+    'sudo -u root rm -rf /', 'doas rm -rf /', 'nohup rm -rf ~', 'time -p rm -rf ~', 'exec rm -rf /boot', 'command rm -rf $HOME', 'setsid rm -rf /']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.critical, true, c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', c);
+  }
+});
+
+test('paths like /. // /./ /etc/.. are normalised to /', () => {
+  assert.equal(normTarget('/.'), '/');
+  assert.equal(normTarget('//'), '/');
+  assert.equal(normTarget('/./'), '/');
+  assert.equal(normTarget('/etc/..'), '/');
+  assert.equal(normTarget('/usr//lib/'), '/usr/lib');
+  assert.equal(normTarget('~/./.ssh/'), '~/.ssh');
+  for (const c of ['rm -rf /.', 'rm -rf /./', 'rm -rf //', 'rm -r /etc/../', 'find -L / -delete', 'find -P -O3 /. -delete']) assert.equal(checkDanger(c).critical, true, c);
+});
+
+test('recursive delete of system directories and key home directories is consistently critical', () => {
+  for (const t of ['/etc', '/usr', '/usr/lib', '/usr/local/bin', '/var', '/var/lib', '/boot', '/bin', '/sbin', '/lib64', '/home/me', '~', '$HOME', '~/.ssh', '$HOME/.ssh', '~/.gnupg']) {
+    assert.equal(checkDanger(`rm -r ${t}`).critical, true, t);
+  }
+  for (const t of ['/tmp/x', '/home/me/photos', '~/Downloads/old', 'build']) assert.equal(checkDanger(`rm -r ${t}`).critical, false, t);
+});
+
+test('mv of a system or home directory is critical; ordinary moves stay safe', () => {
+  for (const c of ['mv /etc /tmp/x', 'mv ~ /tmp/x', 'mv /usr/lib /tmp', 'sudo mv /boot /old']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', c);
+    assert.equal(d.critical, true, c);
+  }
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('mv /tmp/a /tmp/b').risk, 'safe');
+});
+
+test('docker -v=/:/h and --mount=…source=/ mount the host root', () => {
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('docker run -v=/:/h alpine').critical, true);
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('docker run -v=//:/h alpine').critical, true);
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('docker run --mount=type=bind,source=/,target=/h alpine').critical, true);
+  const ro = checkDanger('docker run -v=/:/h:ro alpine');
+  assert.equal(ro.risk, 'high');
+  assert.equal(ro.critical, false);
+  assert.equal(denyOnly('docker run -v=/srv/data:/data alpine').risk, 'safe');
+});
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// 3. composer
+
+const grepTools = [{ tool: 'grep', p: 1 }];
+const composeGrep = (q, pattern, paths) => compose(q, grepTools, { ...extractSlots(q), paths }, { patternOf: () => pattern, nameOf: () => null });
+
+test('composer: grep patterns are quoted literally and never reused as a search path', () => {
+  const a = composeGrep('search for ~/foo recursively ignoring case in src', 'recursively', ['~/foo', 'src']);
+  assert.equal(a.command, "grep -i -r -- '~/foo' src");
+  const b = composeGrep('search for "~" recursively ignoring case in /tmp', '~', ['~', '/tmp']);
+  assert.equal(b.command, "grep -i -r -- '~' /tmp");
+  // a real search path keeps tilde expansion
+  const c = composeGrep('search for TODO recursively ignoring case in ~/src', 'TODO', ['~/src']);
+  assert.equal(c.command, 'grep -i -r -- TODO ~/src');
+  // end to end through the pipeline
+  assert.equal(suggest('search for ~/foo recursively ignoring case in src', { env: BASH }).command, "grep -i -r -- '~/foo' src");
+  assert.equal(suggest('search for "~" recursively ignoring case in /tmp', { env: BASH }).command, "grep -i -r -- '~' /tmp");
+});
+
+test('composer: git log --author always gets a value (or is not emitted)', () => {
+  const gitTools = [{ tool: 'git', p: 1 }];
+  const run = (q) => compose(q, gitTools, extractSlots(q), { patternOf: () => null, nameOf: () => null });
+  assert.match(run('git log commits by alice').command, /--author=alice\b/);
+  assert.match(run('git log by author bob').command, /--author=bob\b/);
+  const none = run('git log by author');
+  assert.ok(!none || !/--author(?!=\w)/.test(none.command), none?.command);
+});
+
+test('composer validation rejects command substitution and expansions', () => {
+  for (const c of ['grep -- "$(id)" .', 'grep -- $(id) .', 'grep -- `id` .', 'grep -- "${x}" .', 'grep -- x <(id)']) {
+    const v = validateComposed(c, 'grep');
+    assert.equal(v.ok, false, c);
+  }
+  assert.equal(validateComposed("grep -- '$(id)' .", 'grep').ok, true);
+  assert.equal(validateComposed("grep -- '`id`' .", 'grep').ok, true);
+});
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// 4. cmd.exe: values with /
+
+test('cmd: a value starting with / is fine when glued to a switch (findstr /c:), refused standalone', () => {
+  const r = buildCommand('grep_text', '', { env: CMD, resolved: { pattern: '/api', path: 'src' } });
+  assert.equal(r.command, 'pushd src && (findstr /s /n /c:"/api" * & popd)');
+  const s = buildCommand('grep_text', '', { env: CMD, resolved: { pattern: 'x', path: '/api' } });
+  assert.equal(s.command, null);
+  assert.match(s.gap, /switch/);
+  assert.equal(suggest('delete directory /q', { env: CMD }).command, null);
+  assert.throws(() => cmdQuote('/q'), /switch/);
+});
+
+test('cmd: an embedded / is never left unquoted (foo/q is not read as foo /q)', () => {
+  assert.equal(cmdQuote('foo/q'), 'foo\\q'); // path: Windows separator
+  assert.equal(cmdQuote('a/q', { tilde: false }), '"a/q"'); // other values: quoted
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('delete_dir', '', { env: CMD, resolved: { path: 'foo/q' } }).command, 'rmdir /s foo\\q');
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('find_process', '', { env: CMD, resolved: { name: 'a/q' } }).command, 'tasklist | findstr /i "a/q"');
+  assert.equal(buildCommand('delete_dir', '', { env: BASH, resolved: { path: 'foo/q' } }).command, 'rm -r foo/q');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions3.test.js b/test/regressions3.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e6b19f8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions3.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+// Regression tests for the round-2 review findings (review/r2-claude.md, review/r2-codex.md) on slot
+// extraction: whole-disk phrases and trailing punctuation on paths of changing commands.
+// History, rendering, danger and composer findings are in regressions3-history / regressions3-render.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q) => suggest(q, { env: BASH });
+
+// r2-claude major 1: "on the disk" replaced the folder the user named with /
+test('whole-disk phrases never become the target of a changing command', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('usuń folder cache na dysku').command, 'rm -r cache');
+  for (const q of ['delete the cache folder on the disk', 'delete old logs on my drive', 'usuń plik notatki na dysku']) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.doesNotMatch(r.command, /^rm( -r)? \/$/, q);
+    assert.equal(r.critical, false, q);
+    assert.equal(r.missing.length, 1, q);
+  }
+  // a named folder also wins for read-only intents
+  assert.equal(run('ile miejsca zajmuje folder cache na dysku').command, 'du -sh cache');
+  // still a search scope where that is what the phrase means
+  assert.match(run('find big files on the disk').command, /^find \/ /);
+  assert.match(run('znajdź pliki .log na dysku').command, /^find \/ /);
+  const del = run('usuń pliki tmp na całym dysku');
+  assert.match(del.command, /^find \/ .*-delete$/);
+  assert.equal(del.critical, true);
+  // a literal / is still the root
+  assert.equal(run('delete folder /').command, 'rm -r /');
+});
+
+// r2-codex major 1: trailing punctuation was removed from deletion targets
+test('a path with trailing punctuation is a placeholder for changing commands', () => {
+  for (const [q, slot] of [['delete folder /tmp/data!', 'path'], ['delete folder /tmp/a.txt.', 'path'], ['delete file /tmp/x?', 'file'],
+    ['remove the file notes.txt.', 'file']]) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.ok(r.missing.includes(slot), `${q} -> ${r.command}`);
+    assert.doesNotMatch(r.command, /\/tmp\/|notes/, q);
+    assert.ok(r.warnings.some((w) => /trailing punctuation/.test(w)), q);
+  }
+  // quoted: exact
+  assert.equal(run("delete folder '/tmp/data!'").command, "rm -r '/tmp/data!'");
+  // kept characters are not ambiguous; read-only commands still trim sentence punctuation
+  assert.equal(run('delete file /tmp/data.').command, 'rm /tmp/data.');
+  assert.equal(run('show file /tmp/a.txt.').command, 'cat /tmp/a.txt');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions4.test.js b/test/regressions4.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..dc4679f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions4.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,204 @@
+// Regression tests for the round-3 review findings (review/r3-claude.md, review/r3-codex.md):
+// refused/ambiguous slots never fall back to catalog defaults, punctuation guard on "same for" and the
+// composer, "same for" never replays an older changing command, typed references by recency, literal
+// tildes from history, filtered listings / plural pronouns, danger wrappers, composer pattern slots,
+// ambiguous quoted text, teacher call accounting and order-insensitive held-out matching.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+// the parser on its own (it only raises risk); the trust rule (a non-catalog command is high) is in regressions27.test.js
+import { assessCommand as checkDanger } from '../src/danger.js';
+import { splitCommand } from '../src/shellwords.js';
+import { sameCmd } from '../scripts/lib/cmdnorm.js';
+import { nearKey, heldOutIndex } from '../scripts/lib/heldout.js';
+// v0.3: commands outside the catalog are high by the allowlist; these cases check the deny rules alone
+const denyOnly = (c, base = 'safe') => checkDanger(c, base, { allowlist: { off: true } });
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PWSH = { shell: 'powershell', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+
+test('blocker: a withheld path is a placeholder, never the catalog default `.`', () => {
+  const a = run('delete all log files in /tmp/data!');
+  assert.match(a.command, /^find <PATH> /);
+  assert.ok(!/find \. /.test(a.command), a.command);
+  assert.ok(a.missing.includes('path'));
+  assert.ok(a.warnings.some((w) => /placeholder/.test(w)));
+  // refused history reference (the dir is a search root, the request names "files")
+  const b = run('delete all those log files', ['find /var/log -type f -iname "*.log"']);
+  assert.equal(b.context.rule, 'refused');
+  assert.match(b.command, /^find <PATH> /);
+  assert.ok(b.missing.includes('path'));
+  // an ordinary request still uses the default
+  assert.equal(run('delete all log files').command.startsWith('find . '), true);
+});
+
+test('punctuation guard covers "same for" and the composer', () => {
+  const a = run('same for /tmp/data!', ['rm -r old']);
+  assert.equal(a.command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+  assert.ok(a.missing.includes('path'));
+  assert.ok(a.warnings.some((w) => /placeholder/.test(w)));
+  assert.equal(run('same for /tmp/data', ['rm -r old']).command, 'rm -r /tmp/data');
+  const c = run('change permissions recursively to 777 on /tmp/data!');
+  assert.ok(!/\/tmp\/data/.test(c.command || ''), c.command);
+  assert.notEqual(c.method, 'composed');
+  // a sentence comma after a path does not stop a read-only composition
+  const f = run("find directories named node_modules under ~/code, don't go deeper than 3 levels");
+  assert.equal(f.method, 'composed');
+  assert.equal(f.command, 'find ~/code -maxdepth 3 -type d -name node_modules');
+  assert.equal(run('szukaj słowa password w katalogu /etc, rekurencyjnie, tylko nazwy plików, bez wielkości liter').command, 'grep -i -r -l -- password /etc');
+});
+
+test('"same for" never replays an older changing command past a newer one', () => {
+  const r = run('same for /srv/current', ['rm -r old', 'ls newdir']);
+  assert.equal(r.understood, false);
+  assert.equal(r.command, null);
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused');
+  // the previous command itself, or a safe one, is still repeated
+  assert.equal(run('same for /srv/current', ['rm -r old']).command, 'rm -r /srv/current');
+  // only the previous command is repeated: a safe one too (round 7, one line of history)
+  assert.equal(run('same for /srv/x', ['du -sh old', 'ls newdir']).command, null);
+  assert.equal(run('same for /srv/x', ['ls newdir', 'du -sh old']).command, 'du -sh /srv/x');
+  // any newer line, even one that names nothing, is the previous command (round 4)
+  assert.equal(run('same for /srv/x', ['rm -r old', 'clear']).command, null);
+  // "what about this": no new target at all
+  const w = run('what about this', ['rm -r foo']);
+  assert.equal(w.understood, false);
+  assert.equal(w.command, null);
+});
+
+test('typed process references follow recency', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('kill that process', ['kill 1111', 'pgrep current-worker']).command, 'pkill -f current-worker');
+  assert.equal(run('kill that process', ['pgrep current-worker', 'kill 1111']).command, 'kill 1111');
+  const amb = run('kill that process', ['kill 1111', 'pgrep "$PROC"']);
+  assert.equal(amb.context.rule, 'refused');
+  assert.ok(!/1111/.test(amb.command), amb.command);
+  // pgrep printed newer PIDs: "that pid" may be one of them (round 4b)
+  assert.equal(run('kill that pid', ['kill 1111', 'pgrep current-worker']).command, 'kill <PID>');
+  assert.equal(run('kill that pid', ['pgrep current-worker', 'kill 1111']).command, 'kill 1111');
+});
+
+test('a quoted or escaped ~ from history stays a literal directory named ~', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ["cat '~/notes.txt'"]).command, "rm './~/notes.txt'");
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat \\~/notes.txt']).command, "rm './~/notes.txt'");
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat "~"/notes.txt']).command, "rm './~/notes.txt'");
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat ~/notes.txt']).command, 'rm ~/notes.txt');
+  // ~user expands to a directory we cannot know
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat ~bob/notes.txt']).context.rule, 'refused');
+  assert.equal(sameCmd("cat '~/notes.txt'", 'cat ~/notes.txt'), false);
+  assert.equal(sameCmd("cat '~/notes.txt'", 'cat \\~/notes.txt'), true);
+  assert.deepEqual(splitCommand('cd ~ && ls ~/x').segments.map((s) => s.words), [['cd', '~'], ['ls', '~/x']]);
+  // PowerShell resolves ~ in quoted paths too: unchanged
+  assert.deepEqual(splitCommand("Get-Content '~/x'", 'pwsh').segments[0].words, ['Get-Content', '~/x']);
+});
+
+test('"delete them/it" after a filtered listing never targets the listed directory', () => {
+  for (const [q, h, env] of [
+    ['delete them', ['Get-ChildItem C:\\Users\\me\\Downloads -Recurse -Include *.tmp'], PWSH],
+    ['delete it', ['Get-ChildItem C:\\Users\\me\\Downloads -Recurse -Include *.tmp'], PWSH],
+    ['delete them', ['Get-ChildItem $HOME\\Downloads -Filter *.pdf'], PWSH],
+    ['delete them', ['gci C:\\logs *.log'], PWSH],
+    ['delete them', ['ls -la ~/Downloads | grep pdf'], BASH],
+    ['delete it', ['ls -la ~/Downloads | grep pdf'], BASH],
+    ['usuń je', ['ls ~/Pobrane | grep pdf'], BASH],
+    ['delete them', ['egrep -rl TODO src'], BASH],
+    ['delete them', ['git grep -l TODO src'], BASH],
+    ['delete them', ['ack -l TODO src'], BASH],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q, h, env);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.match(r.command, /<PATH>/, `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.ok(r.missing.includes('path'));
+  }
+  // a pipe into ps/grep still reads a process, not a directory
+  assert.notEqual(run('delete it', ['ps aux | grep node']).context.rule, 'refused');
+});
+
+test('plural pronouns after a plain listing refer to the entries, not the directory', () => {
+  for (const [q, h, env] of [
+    ['delete them', ['ls /tmp/build'], BASH],
+    ['remove those', ['ls /tmp/build'], BASH],
+    ['delete them', ['grep -rl TODO src', 'ls src'], BASH],
+    ['usuń je', ['ls /tmp/build'], BASH],
+    ['delete them', ['Get-ChildItem C:\\tmp\\old'], PWSH],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q, h, env);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.match(r.command, /<PATH>/);
+  }
+  // singular "it" is refused too (round 4b: the directory or one of its entries); non-destructive plural reuse is fine
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['ls /tmp/build']).command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['grep -rl TODO src', 'ls src']).command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+  assert.equal(run('list them', ['ls /tmp/build']).command, 'ls -lah /tmp/build');
+});
+
+test('danger: more command wrappers, whole-disk shred', () => {
+  for (const c of ['unshare rm -rf /', 'unshare -m rm -rf /', 'watch rm -rf /', 'watch -n 1 rm -rf /', "watch 'rm -rf /'",
+    'nsenter -t 1 -m rm -rf /', 'flock /tmp/l rm -rf /', 'taskset -c 0 rm -rf /', 'strace -f rm -rf /', 'systemd-run rm -rf /',
+    'shred -u /dev/sda', 'shred /dev/nvme0n1', 'blkdiscard /dev/sdb', 'wipe /dev/mmcblk0']) {
+    assert.equal(checkDanger(c).critical, true, c);
+  }
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('shred -u notes.txt').critical, false);
+  assert.equal(denyOnly('watch ls').risk, 'safe');
+  assert.equal(denyOnly('taskset 1 ls').risk, 'safe');
+  // a script of the project: medium (v0.3 close4)
+  assert.equal(denyOnly('taskset 1 node bench.js').risk, 'medium');
+});
+
+test('grep pattern slot: option words are not the pattern, a path-like pattern keeps the search dir', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('grep for ~/foo recursively in src').command, "grep -rn -- '~/foo' src");
+  assert.equal(run('grep for ~/foo in src').command, "grep -rn -- '~/foo' src");
+  assert.equal(run('grep for TODO recursively in src').command, 'grep -rn -- TODO src');
+  assert.equal(run('grep TODO in ~/proj').command, 'grep -rn -- TODO ~/proj');
+});
+
+test('quoted text that may end at an escaped quote is a placeholder in every shell', () => {
+  const q = 'search for "a\\" -e evil" in src';
+  for (const env of [BASH, PWSH]) {
+    const r = run(q, null, env);
+    if (!r.understood) continue; // rejecting the request is fine too (v0.4 model); never a cut-off pattern
+    assert.match(r.command, /<PATTERN>/, r.command);
+    assert.ok(!/'a\\'/.test(r.command), r.command);
+    assert.ok(r.missing.includes('pattern'));
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('search for "a\\" in src').command, "grep -rn -- 'a\\' src"); // nothing after it: unambiguous
+});
+
+test('teacher accounting: every request sent is a network call', async () => {
+  const saved = { fetch: globalThis.fetch, key: process.env.TYPESAFE_API_KEY };
+  process.env.TYPESAFE_API_KEY = 'test-placeholder';
+  let requests = 0;
+  globalThis.fetch = async () => { requests++; return { ok: false, status: 503, json: async () => null, headers: { get: () => null } }; };
+  try {
+    const { ask, stats } = await import('../scripts/lib/jev.js');
+    const before = stats.calls;
+    await assert.rejects(ask(`regression-test-${Date.now()}`, {}, { retries: 1 }));
+    assert.equal(requests, 2);
+    assert.equal(stats.calls - before, 2);
+  } finally {
+    globalThis.fetch = saved.fetch;
+    if (saved.key == null) delete process.env.TYPESAFE_API_KEY; else process.env.TYPESAFE_API_KEY = saved.key;
+  }
+});
+
+test('held-out matching ignores word order', () => {
+  assert.equal(nearKey('last 30 kernel messages'), nearKey('kernel messages last 30'));
+  assert.equal(nearKey('pokaż dyski i partycje'), nearKey('pokaż partycje i dyski'));
+  const idx = heldOutIndex(['show all disks and partitions']);
+  assert.ok(idx.has('partitions and disks show'));
+  assert.ok(!idx.has('show disks'));
+});
+
+test('CLI: an unresolvable history reference says so (exit 3, no command)', async () => {
+  const { spawnSync } = await import('node:child_process');
+  const { mkdtempSync, writeFileSync } = await import('node:fs');
+  const { tmpdir } = await import('node:os');
+  const { join } = await import('node:path');
+  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'tellsh-r4-'));
+  const hist = join(dir, 'bash_history');
+  writeFileSync(hist, 'rm -r old\nls newdir\n');
+  const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['bin/tellsh.js', '--dry-run', `--history=${hist}`, 'same', 'for', '/srv/current'], { encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, NO_COLOR: '1' } });
+  assert.equal(r.status, 3);
+  assert.match(r.stdout, /Cannot resolve "same for \/srv\/current" from history/);
+  assert.doesNotMatch(r.stdout, /rm -r/);
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions5.test.js b/test/regressions5.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..773c9b3
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions5.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,148 @@
+// Regression tests for the round-4 review findings (review/r4-claude.md, review/r4-codex.md):
+// "same but" keeps ambiguous slots as placeholders, stale commands are never replayed or modified,
+// listing provenance through `cd`, pipelines and `tellsh` lines, source/destination of refused
+// references, stop words used as names, `-c` command strings and more wrappers in the danger checker,
+// and one held-out index for gen_data.js and teacher.js.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+// the parser on its own (it only raises risk); the trust rule (a non-catalog command is high) is in regressions27.test.js
+import { assessCommand as checkDanger } from '../src/danger.js';
+import { buildContext } from '../src/history.js';
+import { heldOutTexts, heldOutIndex } from '../scripts/lib/heldout.js';
+import { SLOT_CASES } from './slot-cases.js';
+// v0.3: commands outside the catalog are high by the allowlist; these cases check the deny rules alone
+const denyOnly = (c, base = 'safe') => checkDanger(c, base, { allowlist: { off: true } });
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PWSH = { shell: 'powershell', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const refusedPath = (r, slot = 'path') => {
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', JSON.stringify(r.context));
+  assert.ok(r.missing.includes(slot), r.command);
+};
+
+test('blocker: "same but" never replaces an ambiguous previous path with `.`', () => {
+  const r = run('same but delete txt files', ['find "$DIR" -type f -iname "*.log" -delete']);
+  assert.equal(r.command, "find <PATH> -type f -iname '*.txt' -delete");
+  refusedPath(r);
+  // a readable previous path is still reused
+  assert.equal(run('same but delete txt files', ['find /tmp/x -type f -iname "*.log" -delete']).command, "find /tmp/x -type f -iname '*.txt' -delete");
+});
+
+test('stale commands are not replayed by "same for" or modified by "same but"', () => {
+  for (const newer of ['ls', 'echo done', 'sleep 5', 'clear', 'git status', 'ls newdir']) {
+    const r = run('same for /srv/current', ['rm -r old', newer]);
+    assert.equal(r.command, null, newer);
+    assert.equal(r.understood, false);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused');
+  }
+  const sb = run('same but force', ['rm -r old', 'ls newdir']);
+  assert.equal(sb.command, null);
+  assert.equal(sb.context.rule, 'refused');
+  // a later segment of the same line
+  const k = run('same for 2222', ['kill 1111; ls newdir']);
+  assert.equal(k.command, null);
+  assert.equal(buildContext(['kill 1111; ls newdir']).last.skipped, true);
+  assert.equal(buildContext(['kill 1111']).last.skipped, false);
+  // the previous command itself still works
+  assert.equal(run('same for /srv/current', ['rm -r old']).command, 'rm -r /srv/current');
+  assert.equal(run('same for 2222', ['kill 1111']).command, 'kill 2222');
+  assert.equal(run('same for /srv/x', ['du -sh old', 'ls newdir']).command, null);
+  assert.equal(run('same for /srv/x', ['ls newdir', 'du -sh old']).command, 'du -sh /srv/x');
+});
+
+test('a listing after `cd` is a listing of the cd directory', () => {
+  for (const [q, h, env] of [
+    ['delete them', ['cd ~/Downloads && ls | grep pdf']],
+    ['delete it', ['cd ~/Downloads; ls | grep pdf']],
+    ['delete them', ['cd /tmp/build; ls']],
+    ['usuń je', ['cd /tmp/build; ls']],
+    ['delete it', ['cd /tmp/build; ls *.pdf']],
+    ['delete them', ['cd /tmp/build && ls']],
+    ['delete it', ['cd /tmp/build && ls | grep pdf']],
+    ['delete them', ['cd /tmp/build; Get-ChildItem'], PWSH],
+    ['delete it', ['Set-Location C:\\x; Get-ChildItem -Filter *.tmp'], PWSH],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q, h, env);
+    refusedPath(r);
+    assert.ok(!/Downloads|build|C:\\x/.test(r.command), `${JSON.stringify(h)} ${q} -> ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  // singular "it" after a listing is refused too (round 4b); the newest cd with nothing after it is a target
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cd /tmp/build; ls']).command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+  assert.equal(run('delete them', ['cd /tmp/a; cd /tmp/b']).command, 'rm -r /tmp/b');
+  // only the previous line is read: a listing in its own line names nothing, so the cd of an older line is not used
+  for (const h of [['cd ~/Downloads', 'ls | grep pdf'], ['cd /tmp/build', 'ls'], ['cd /tmp/a', 'cd /tmp/b', 'ls']]) {
+    const r = run('delete them', h);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', JSON.stringify(h));
+    assert.ok(!/Downloads|build|\/tmp\/[ab]/.test(r.command), `${JSON.stringify(h)} -> ${r.command}`);
+  }
+});
+
+test('a listing piped into any later stage is a selection of its entries', () => {
+  for (const [h, env] of [
+    [['ls ~/Downloads | sort | grep pdf']], [['ls ~/Downloads | head -50 | grep pdf']], [['ls ~/Downloads | sort | rg pdf']],
+    [['ls -S ~/Downloads | head -1']], [['du -sh ~/Downloads | sort | grep x']],
+    [['Get-ChildItem C:\\x | Sort-Object Length | Select-Object -First 1'], PWSH],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run('delete it', h, env);
+    refusedPath(r);
+    assert.ok(!/Downloads|C:\\x/.test(r.command), `${h} -> ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  // an unpiped listing followed by another command on the same line is a listing too (round 4b)
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['ls /tmp/build; echo done']).command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+});
+
+test('a `tellsh` listing line is a listing too', () => {
+  refusedPath(run('delete them', ['tellsh list directory /tmp/build']));
+  assert.ok(buildContext(['tellsh list directory /tmp/build'], {
+    classify: () => ({ intent: 'list_files', slots: { path: '/tmp/build' } }),
+  }).listedDirs.has('/tmp/build'));
+});
+
+test('a refused or pronoun source keeps the request path as the destination', () => {
+  const a = run('move them to /tmp/old', ['ls /tmp/build | grep pdf']);
+  assert.equal(a.command, 'mv -i <SRC> /tmp/old');
+  refusedPath(a, 'src');
+  const b = run('copy it to /backup', ['cat $F']);
+  assert.equal(b.command, 'cp -ri <SRC> /backup');
+  refusedPath(b, 'src');
+  assert.equal(run('copy it to /backup', ['cat a.txt']).command, 'cp -ri a.txt /backup');
+  assert.equal(run('move it to /tmp/old', ['mkdir /tmp/build']).command, 'mv -i /tmp/build /tmp/old');
+  assert.equal(run('move it to /tmp/old', ['ls /tmp/build']).command, 'mv -i <SRC> /tmp/old'); // listed (round 4b)
+});
+
+test('a stop word right after "folder"/"file" is a name, not a reason to use `.`', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('delete the folder out').command, 'rm -r out');
+  assert.equal(run('delete folder up').command, 'rm -r up');
+  assert.equal(run('delete the file w').command, 'rm w');
+  assert.equal(run('show disk usage of folder out sorted by size').command, 'du -sh out');
+  // still a preposition when a location follows
+  assert.equal(run('delete the cache folder on the disk').command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+});
+
+test('danger: -c command strings and more wrappers are unwrapped', () => {
+  for (const c of ['flock -c "rm -rf /" /tmp/l', 'flock /tmp/l -c "rm -rf /"', 'su -c "rm -rf /"', 'su - root -c "rm -rf /"', 'su -lc "rm -rf /" root',
+    'su --command="rm -rf /"', 'runuser root -c "rm -rf /"', 'runuser -u root -- rm -rf /', 'pkexec rm -rf /', 'pkexec --user root rm -rf /',
+    'chrt 10 rm -rf /', 'chrt -f 10 rm -rf /', 'cgexec -g cpu:x rm -rf /', 'eatmydata rm -rf /', 'torsocks rm -rf /', 'torsocks -P 9050 rm -rf /', 'catchsegv rm -rf /']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c, 'safe');
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', c);
+    assert.equal(d.critical, true, c);
+  }
+  for (const c of ['flock /tmp/l echo hi', 'cgexec -g cpu:x ls', 'chrt -p 1234']) assert.equal(denyOnly(c, 'safe').risk, 'safe', c);
+  // switching user is a privilege change, like sudo (round 4b)
+  assert.equal(denyOnly('su - bob', 'safe').risk, 'medium');
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('su - bob', 'safe').risk, 'high'); // v0.3: su is a wrapper
+});
+
+test('teacher.js and gen_data.js exclude the same held-out texts, including the slot cases', () => {
+  const root = new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname;
+  const idx = heldOutIndex(heldOutTexts(root));
+  for (const [, q] of SLOT_CASES) assert.ok(idx.has(q), q);
+  assert.ok(idx.has('chmod 755 deploy.sh') || !SLOT_CASES.some((c) => c[1] === 'chmod 755 deploy.sh'));
+  for (const f of ['scripts/teacher.js', 'scripts/gen_data.js']) {
+    const src = readFileSync(new URL(`../${f}`, import.meta.url), 'utf8');
+    assert.match(src, /exclusionIndex\(ROOT\)/, f); // one index for both (round 4b: also the eval-only values)
+  }
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions6.test.js b/test/regressions6.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..96aaa9c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions6.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,174 @@
+// Regression tests for the round-4b fixes (review/r4-claude.md, review/r4-codex.md, stricter rules):
+// a history value is the target of a changing command only when it is unambiguous and comes from the most
+// recent history segment that produced its type (never the parent directory of a listing or search, never an
+// older value, never a value a newer listing may have replaced); stale commands are never replayed; the danger
+// checker unwraps -c/--command payloads and scans the trailing command of every wrapper (unsure -> high);
